name: Barbell bench press
musclesText: Primary: pectoralis major (sternal and clavicular heads). Secondary: anterior deltoid, triceps brachii, serratus anterior.

steps.start: Lie on your back on a flat bench with your eyes directly under the racked bar and your shoulders, upper back and glutes in contact with the pad.
steps.setup: Set the J-hooks so you can unrack with arms almost straight, only a few centimetres of elbow bend. Set the safety arms just below the height of your chest at the bottom of the rep, so they catch the bar if you fail but do not touch it on a good rep.
steps.feet: Plant your feet flat on the floor slightly wider than hip-width, roughly under or slightly behind your knees, so you can push your heels into the floor.
steps.grip: Take a medium grip, typically with the index or middle fingers on or just outside the ring marks, so your forearms are vertical at the bottom. Wrap your thumbs around the bar and stack it over the heel of the palm rather than the fingers.
steps.posture: Squeeze your shoulder blades back and down and keep them pinned to the bench. A modest natural arch in the upper back is fine; keep your head and glutes on the bench throughout.
steps.brace: Take a large breath into your belly before each rep, brace your trunk as if about to be prodded, and drive lightly through your feet to keep the body tight.
steps.initiate: Unrack by pressing the bar up and moving it over your shoulders, then pause with arms locked before starting the first descent.
steps.concentric: Press the bar up and slightly back towards your shoulders, driving yourself into the bench and keeping your wrists stacked over your elbows.
steps.breathing: Inhale and brace at the top, hold the breath on the way down and through the hardest part of the press, then exhale near lockout.
steps.eccentric: Lower the bar under control to touch your lower chest around the nipple line or just below, with elbows tucked about 45-70 degrees from your torso rather than flared at 90 degrees.
steps.rom: Touch the chest lightly without bouncing and press to full elbow extension. If a shoulder issue limits depth, a board or slightly shorter range can be used temporarily.
steps.tempo: 2-1-1-0: two seconds down, a brief touch on the chest, one second up, no rest at the top.
steps.finish: Finish each rep with elbows straight, the bar stacked over your shoulders and your shoulder blades still pinned back.
steps.exit: After the last rep, lock out, move the bar back until it touches the uprights, then lower it into the hooks. Use a spotter for heavy sets and never train to failure alone without safeties set.

cues: Push yourself away from the bar

mistakes.m: Bouncing the bar off the chest
mistakes.fix: Slow the descent and touch lightly; reduce the load if you cannot control it.

mistakes.m: Flaring the elbows to 90 degrees
mistakes.fix: Tuck the elbows to about 45-70 degrees and aim the bar at the lower chest.

mistakes.m: Hips lifting off the bench
mistakes.fix: Keep the glutes down; drive the feet back rather than up and reduce the arch if needed.

mistakes.m: Shoulder blades drifting apart as you press
mistakes.fix: Reset the retraction before every set and keep your upper back squeezed into the bench.

safety: Always set safety arms or use a competent spotter for working sets.
Do not use a thumbless grip; the bar can roll out of your hands.
Stop the set if you feel a sharp or pinching pain in the front of the shoulder or any tingling down the arm.
checks: J-hooks and safeties are at the correct heights and both sides match.
Plates are evenly loaded and collars fitted.
The bench is centred and stable under the bar.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if the bar stalls before the halfway point on early reps, your hips lift, the bar path wanders towards your face, or you cannot touch the chest without bouncing.
progressions: Bench press with bands or chains

programming.rehab: Light, pain-free sets with a shortened range (for example a board press) can help reintroduce pressing after a shoulder or pec injury, ideally guided by a physiotherapist.
programming.frequency: 1-3 times per week, with 48-72 h between hard sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Start with the empty 20 kg bar for two warm-up sets, then add load in small jumps until you reach a weight you can lift for the target reps with about 3 reps in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: The last rep should slow down but keep the same bar path and touch point; stop when you estimate 1-3 reps left or if form changes.
programming.progression: Double progression: work within the rep range, and once all sets hit the top of the range add 2.5 kg.
programming.increase: Increase by 2.5 kg once you complete every set at the top of the rep range with good form and at least 1 rep in reserve.
programming.maintain: Keep the load the same if any set falls short of the range; reduce by 5-10 percent if performance drops two sessions in a row or recovery is poor.

name: Incline barbell bench press
musclesText: Primary: pectoralis major (clavicular head), anterior deltoid. Secondary: triceps brachii, serratus anterior, pectoralis major (sternal head).

steps.start: Sit back on an incline bench set at 30-45 degrees under a racked bar, then lie back so your eyes are roughly under the bar.
steps.setup: Use a dedicated incline bench station or an adjustable bench in a rack. Set the hooks so the bar is reachable with nearly straight arms and set safeties just above your chest at the bottom position.
steps.feet: Feet flat on the floor, about hip-width or slightly wider, with knees bent around 90 degrees so you can drive back into the seat without sliding.
steps.grip: Use a medium grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width, so your forearms are close to vertical when the bar touches your upper chest. Full thumb wrap, bar in the heel of the palm.
steps.posture: Pull your shoulder blades back and down into the bench and keep your head, upper back and glutes in contact with the pad.
steps.brace: Breathe into your belly, brace the trunk and keep your ribcage from flaring up as you press.
steps.initiate: Unrack, bring the bar over your shoulders, and settle for a second before lowering.
steps.concentric: Press the bar up and slightly back so it finishes above your shoulders, keeping wrists stacked over elbows.
steps.breathing: Inhale at the top, hold it on the way down and up through the sticking point, then exhale near lockout.
steps.eccentric: Lower the bar under control to your upper chest, just below the collarbones, with elbows slightly in front of the bar and not flared out to the sides.
steps.rom: Touch the upper chest lightly and press to full lockout. Use a shorter range only if shoulder comfort demands it.
steps.tempo: 2-1-1-0: two seconds down, a brief touch, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish with the bar over your shoulders, arms straight and shoulder blades still set.
steps.exit: Lock out, guide the bar back into the hooks until it touches the uprights, then lower it. Sit up only once the bar is secure.

cues: Bar to the top of the chest

mistakes.m: Setting the bench too steep, so it turns into a shoulder press
mistakes.fix: Keep the incline at 30-45 degrees; many people do best around 30.

mistakes.m: Lowering the bar to the mid-chest or belly
mistakes.fix: Aim the bar at the upper chest just under the collarbones.

mistakes.m: Sliding down the bench during the set
mistakes.fix: Set your feet firmly and adjust the seat so your hips stay put.

mistakes.m: Excessive arching that flattens the incline
mistakes.fix: Keep a modest upper-back arch and your glutes on the seat.

safety: Set safeties or use a spotter: a failed incline press comes down near the throat.
Stop if you feel pinching at the front of the shoulder; lowering the incline or narrowing the grip slightly often helps.
checks: Bench angle is locked at 30-45 degrees.
Hooks and safety arms are set evenly.
Collars are on and plates are matched.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if the bar drifts toward your face or neck, your hips lift off the seat, or reps slow dramatically well before your target.

programming.rehab: Light, pain-free incline pressing can be used in later stages of shoulder rehabilitation, with a physiotherapist's guidance.
programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week, 48-72 h between hard chest sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Start around 70-80 percent of your flat bench working weight and adjust until the target reps leave about 2-3 reps in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: Bar speed should stay consistent until the last one or two reps, and the bar should land in the same place each time.
programming.progression: Double progression within the rep range, adding 2.5 kg once all sets reach the top.
programming.increase: Add 2.5 kg when every set reaches the top of the range with clean form.
programming.maintain: Hold the load if reps fall short; drop 5-10 percent if the shoulders feel irritated or performance declines over two sessions.

name: Decline bench press
musclesText: Primary: pectoralis major (sternal and abdominal heads). Secondary: triceps brachii, anterior deltoid.

steps.start: Hook your legs under the leg pads of a decline bench and lie back so your head is lower than your hips and your eyes are under the racked bar.
steps.setup: Use a decline bench of about 15-30 degrees with secure leg hooks. Set the bar where you can unrack it with nearly straight arms; if the station has safety catches, set them just above chest height at the bottom.
steps.feet: Your feet and ankles are locked under the rollers, which anchors you in place of floor drive.
steps.grip: Take a medium grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width, so forearms are vertical at the bottom. Full thumb wrap.
steps.posture: Retract and depress your shoulder blades and keep your head on the bench. The decline already shortens the range, so only a small arch is needed.
steps.brace: Breathe in, brace the trunk and press your shins up into the rollers to stay locked in.
steps.initiate: Unrack with straight arms, ideally with a spotter handing it off, and bring the bar over your lower chest.
steps.concentric: Press the bar straight up over the lower chest to lockout, keeping the wrists over the elbows.
steps.breathing: Breathe in at the top, hold through the descent and the press, and exhale at lockout. Avoid long breath holds across a set, because the head-down position already raises pressure in the head.
steps.eccentric: Lower the bar under control to your lower chest, just below the nipple line, with elbows tucked about 45-60 degrees.
steps.rom: Touch the lower chest lightly and press to lockout; the range is naturally shorter than a flat press.
steps.tempo: 2-1-1-0: two seconds down, light touch, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish with arms straight and the bar stacked over your lower chest and shoulders.
steps.exit: Return the bar to the hooks, rest a moment, then unhook your legs and sit up slowly to avoid dizziness.

mistakes.m: Lowering the bar towards the neck
mistakes.fix: Aim for the lower chest and keep the elbows tucked.

mistakes.m: Bouncing off the chest
mistakes.fix: Control the descent and touch lightly.

mistakes.m: Training heavy without a spotter
mistakes.fix: The bar is hard to escape from a decline; use a spotter or safety catches.

safety: Use a spotter for heavy sets; failing in a decline position is awkward to escape.
Avoid this lift if you have uncontrolled high blood pressure, glaucoma or are prone to dizziness in head-down positions, unless cleared by a doctor.
Sit up slowly after each set.
checks: Leg hooks are secure and adjusted to your leg length.
The bench is locked at the chosen decline.
Collars are fitted and the bar is centred.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if the bar drifts towards your face, you feel light-headed, or you need to bounce the bar to complete reps.

programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week, 48-72 h between hard chest sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Start around your flat bench working weight or slightly less, and pick a load that gives your target reps with 2-3 in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: Reps should stay smooth and the bar should land on the lower chest every time; stop with 1-3 reps in reserve.
programming.progression: Double progression, adding 2.5 kg after all sets reach the top of the range.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets reach the top of the rep range with a controlled touch.
programming.maintain: Keep the load if you feel any dizziness or form slips; reduce if shoulders or elbows are irritated.

name: Dumbbell bench press
musclesText: Primary: pectoralis major (sternal and clavicular heads). Secondary: anterior deltoid, triceps brachii, serratus anterior.

steps.start: Sit on the end of a flat bench with a dumbbell standing on each thigh, then lie back while bringing the dumbbells to your chest, kicking each knee up to help them into position.
steps.setup: Use a flat bench with clear space on both sides. Check the dumbbells are a matching pair and, for adjustable ones, that the collars are tight.
steps.feet: Plant your feet flat on the floor, slightly wider than hip-width, and drive them lightly into the ground.
steps.grip: Hold each dumbbell firmly with a full grip, the handle across the heel of your palm. Start with palms facing your feet or angled slightly in, with the dumbbells just outside your chest.
steps.posture: Retract and depress your shoulder blades and keep your head, upper back and glutes on the bench.
steps.brace: Breathe into your belly and brace before pressing; the dumbbells move independently, so a tight trunk keeps you stable.
steps.initiate: From the chest, start pressing both dumbbells together, pushing your upper back into the bench.
steps.concentric: Press the dumbbells up and slightly in so they finish above your shoulders, without clanging them together. Keep forearms vertical.
steps.breathing: Inhale at the top, hold the breath on the way down and through the press, and exhale as you approach the top.
steps.eccentric: Lower the dumbbells in a slight arc to the sides of your chest, elbows about 45-70 degrees from the torso, feeling a stretch across the chest.
steps.rom: Lower until the dumbbells are about level with your chest or until you feel a comfortable stretch without the shoulders rolling forward; press to full lockout.
steps.tempo: 3-0-1-0: three seconds down, no pause, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish with arms straight and dumbbells stacked over your shoulders, close but not touching.
steps.exit: Lower the dumbbells to your chest, bring your knees up and roll up to sitting with the dumbbells on your thighs. Do not drop them out to the sides from arm's length.

cues: Shoulder blades tucked into the bench
Lower with control into a stretch

mistakes.m: Dropping the dumbbells too deep so the shoulders roll forward
mistakes.fix: Stop at a comfortable stretch with shoulder blades still pinned.

mistakes.m: Pressing with the elbows flared at 90 degrees
mistakes.fix: Tuck the elbows to roughly 45-70 degrees.

mistakes.m: Dropping the dumbbells to the floor from arm's length at the end of a set
mistakes.fix: Bring them to the chest and roll up, or lower them carefully to the floor beside the bench.

safety: Learn the kick-up and roll-up technique before using heavy dumbbells.
Stop if you feel sharp pain at the front of the shoulder or elbow.
checks: The dumbbells match and any collars are tight.
The bench is stable and there is clear space on both sides.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if you cannot get the dumbbells into position safely, one side lags noticeably, or the dumbbells drift apart and wobble at the bottom.

programming.rehab: Light dumbbells through a pain-free range can rebuild pressing strength after shoulder issues; follow a physiotherapist's guidance.
programming.frequency: 1-3 times per week, 48-72 h between hard sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Pick a pair you can press for about 12 reps with 3 in reserve; many beginners start at 6-12 kg per hand.
programming.judgeLoad: The last rep should slow but stay balanced between sides; stop at 1-3 reps in reserve.
programming.progression: Double progression: once all sets reach the top of the range, move up to the next pair, usually 2 kg per hand.
programming.increase: Increase when every set hits the top of the rep range with controlled lowering.
programming.maintain: Stay at the same weight if the jump to the next pair costs more than 3-4 reps; reduce if form breaks or a shoulder is irritated.

name: Incline dumbbell press
musclesText: Primary: pectoralis major (clavicular head), anterior deltoid. Secondary: triceps brachii, serratus anterior.

steps.start: Sit on an incline bench with a dumbbell on each thigh, then lie back while kicking the dumbbells up to your shoulders one knee at a time.
steps.setup: Set an adjustable bench at 30-45 degrees and set the seat, if there is one, so your hips do not slide. Check the bench is locked.
steps.feet: Feet flat on the floor, slightly wider than hip-width, knees bent.
steps.grip: Full grip on each handle, palms facing forward or slightly in, dumbbells just outside your upper chest.
steps.posture: Shoulder blades back and down against the pad, head supported, glutes on the seat.
steps.brace: Breathe in and brace the trunk so your ribcage stays down rather than flaring as you press.
steps.initiate: Press both dumbbells together from the upper chest, driving your upper back into the bench.
steps.concentric: Press up and slightly in so the dumbbells finish over your shoulders and upper chest, forearms vertical throughout.
steps.breathing: Inhale at the top, hold through the descent and early press, exhale near lockout.
steps.eccentric: Lower the dumbbells under control to the sides of your upper chest, elbows slightly in front of the torso, until you feel a stretch across the upper chest.
steps.rom: Lower to about upper-chest level or a comfortable stretch, then press to full lockout.
steps.tempo: 3-0-1-0: three seconds down, no pause, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish with the dumbbells stacked over the shoulders and shoulder blades still set.
steps.exit: Bring the dumbbells to your chest, sit up using the knees for help, and rest them on your thighs before lowering them to the floor.

cues: Upper chest up to the dumbbells

mistakes.m: Bench too steep, turning it into a shoulder press
mistakes.fix: Use 30-45 degrees; lower it if you feel mostly front delts.

mistakes.m: Arching the lower back to flatten the angle
mistakes.fix: Keep the glutes on the seat and the ribcage down.

mistakes.m: Lowering too fast and losing control at the bottom
mistakes.fix: Take three seconds down and stop at a comfortable stretch.

safety: Learn the kick-up technique with light dumbbells first.
Stop if you feel pinching at the front of the shoulder; reduce the incline or range.
checks: Bench and seat are locked at the chosen angle.
Dumbbells are a matching pair and collars are tight.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if you cannot get into position safely, the dumbbells wobble or drift apart, or your lower back arches to complete reps.

programming.rehab: Light, pain-free incline pressing can help restore upper-body pressing after shoulder problems; get a physiotherapist's input.
programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week, 48-72 h between hard chest sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Start with about 80 percent of your flat dumbbell press weight and adjust to leave 2-3 reps in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: Both sides should move evenly and the last rep should slow but not break form.
programming.progression: Double progression, moving up one dumbbell increment (usually 2 kg per hand) after all sets reach the top of the range.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets are at the top of the range with good control.
programming.maintain: Keep the weight if the jump is too large; reduce if the shoulders feel irritated.

name: Dumbbell fly
musclesText: Primary: pectoralis major (sternal and clavicular heads). Secondary: anterior deltoid, biceps brachii (short head, as an elbow stabiliser).

steps.start: Lie on a flat bench holding two dumbbells pressed above your chest, palms facing each other and arms nearly straight.
steps.setup: Use a flat bench with room on both sides. Choose light dumbbells; the fly loads the shoulder at long lever lengths and needs far less weight than a press.
steps.feet: Feet flat on the floor, slightly wider than hip-width.
steps.grip: Neutral grip with palms facing each other. Keep a soft, fixed bend in the elbows of about 15-30 degrees for the whole set.
steps.posture: Shoulder blades gently pulled back and down into the bench, chest up, head and glutes on the pad.
steps.brace: Brace the trunk lightly and keep your lower back in a natural position rather than arching hard.
steps.initiate: Start the descent by opening your arms out to the sides as if hugging a large barrel in reverse, keeping the elbow angle fixed.
steps.concentric: Bring the dumbbells back up along the same wide arc by squeezing your upper arms towards each other, as if hugging a tree. The motion comes from the shoulder, not the elbow.
steps.breathing: Inhale as you lower into the stretch and exhale as you bring the dumbbells together.
steps.eccentric: Lower the dumbbells slowly in a wide arc until your upper arms are about level with the bench and you feel a strong but comfortable stretch across the chest.
steps.rom: Stop the descent when the elbows reach roughly bench height or a comfortable stretch; finish the top just before the dumbbells touch, where tension starts to drop.
steps.tempo: 3-1-1-0: three seconds down, a one-second pause in the stretch, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish with the dumbbells above your chest, a few centimetres apart, elbows still softly bent.
steps.exit: Bend your elbows to bring the dumbbells onto your chest, then roll up to sitting with them on your thighs.

mistakes.m: Bending and straightening the elbows so it becomes a press
mistakes.fix: Lock in a slight bend and keep it constant throughout.

mistakes.m: Going too heavy and dropping too deep
mistakes.fix: Use light dumbbells and stop at upper arms level with the bench.

mistakes.m: Arms fully straight, stressing the elbow
mistakes.fix: Keep a soft 15-30 degree bend.

safety: The bottom position places high stress on the front of the shoulder; never bounce out of the stretch.
Stop if you feel sharp pain in the shoulder or biceps tendon area at the front of the shoulder.
checks: Dumbbells are light enough to control at full stretch.
The bench is stable with space on both sides.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if your elbows bend more as you fatigue, you cannot pause in the stretch, or you feel the strain in the shoulder joint rather than the chest.

programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week, after your main pressing.
programming.initialLoad: Start with about a third to a half of what you use per hand on the dumbbell bench press, aiming for 12-15 reps with 2-3 in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: You should be able to pause briefly in the stretch on every rep and keep the elbow angle constant.
programming.progression: Double progression in the 10-15 rep range, then move up one dumbbell increment.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets hit 15 controlled reps with a pause at the bottom.
programming.maintain: Stay at the same load if the elbow angle changes or the stretch pause disappears; reduce if the front of the shoulder is irritated.

name: Cable fly
musclesText: Primary: pectoralis major (sternal head). Secondary: anterior deltoid, serratus anterior.

steps.start: Stand in the middle of a dual cable station holding a D-handle in each hand, take a step forward so there is tension on both cables, and let your arms open wide to the sides.
steps.setup: Set both pulleys to about shoulder height and attach single D-handles. Select the same weight on both stacks.
steps.feet: Use a staggered stance with one foot forward, knees soft, so you are stable without the cables pulling you backward.
steps.grip: Hold the handles with palms facing forward or slightly in, elbows softly bent at about 15-30 degrees and fixed.
steps.posture: Lean very slightly forward from the hips with a neutral spine, chest up and shoulder blades gently back.
steps.brace: Brace your trunk so your body stays still and only your arms move.
steps.initiate: Start by drawing your upper arms towards each other in a horizontal arc in front of your body.
steps.concentric: Sweep your hands together until they meet in front of your chest, squeezing the chest. Keep the elbow angle fixed so the movement comes from the shoulder.
steps.breathing: Exhale as your hands come together and inhale as they open back out.
steps.eccentric: Let your arms open slowly back along the same arc until your hands are roughly in line with your torso and you feel a stretch across the chest.
steps.rom: Open until your elbows are about level with or slightly behind your torso without your shoulders rolling forward; close until your hands meet in front of your chest.
steps.tempo: 2-1-2-0: two seconds in, one-second squeeze, two seconds back.
steps.finish: Finish each rep with the hands touching or nearly touching at chest height, a brief squeeze, then open.
steps.exit: Let the arms come back under control, step back towards the stack to remove tension, and return each handle to its pulley one at a time.

mistakes.m: Turning it into a press by bending the elbows
mistakes.fix: Fix the elbow angle and move only at the shoulder.

mistakes.m: Leaning far forward and using bodyweight
mistakes.fix: Stay almost upright and lighten the load.

mistakes.m: Letting the cables yank the arms back too far
mistakes.fix: Control the return and stop at a comfortable stretch.

safety: Do not let the arms be pulled behind the body under load; that stresses the front of the shoulder.
Step in and out of position carefully so a handle does not snap back.
checks: Both pulleys are at the same height, about shoulder level.
Pins are fully inserted and the same weight is selected on both sides.
Handles are clipped securely.
reduceLoad: Reduce the weight if your stance shifts each rep, your elbows bend to finish, or you cannot control the return to the stretch.

programming.rehab: Very light cable flies within a pain-free range can be part of later-stage shoulder or pec rehabilitation, guided by a physiotherapist.
programming.frequency: 1-3 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Start with a light stack setting you can move for 15 controlled reps with a full squeeze and 2-3 reps in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: You should hold the squeeze for a second and control the return on every rep.
programming.progression: Double progression within 10-15 reps, then increase by the smallest stack increment.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets reach 15 reps with a held squeeze.
programming.maintain: Keep the load if the stance or elbow angle changes; reduce if the shoulder feels pinched.

name: Low-to-high cable fly
musclesText: Primary: pectoralis major (clavicular head). Secondary: anterior deltoid, serratus anterior.

steps.start: Stand between two cable columns with a D-handle in each hand, arms low and slightly out to the sides, palms facing forward.
steps.setup: Set both pulleys to the lowest setting and attach single D-handles. Select the same light weight on each stack.
steps.feet: Take a small step forward into a staggered or split stance so there is tension on the cables at the bottom.
steps.grip: Hold the handles with palms facing forward and slightly up, elbows softly bent and fixed.
steps.posture: Stand tall with chest up and a neutral spine; keep the shoulder blades gently back and down rather than shrugging.
steps.brace: Brace the trunk and keep the ribs down so you do not lean back as the hands rise.
steps.initiate: Start by sweeping both arms forward and upward in an arc from beside your hips.
steps.concentric: Bring the hands up and together until they meet at about upper-chest height, just below the chin. Think of scooping the arms upward.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you sweep up and squeeze; inhale as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower the hands slowly back along the same arc to just beside or slightly behind your hips.
steps.rom: Move from beside the hips to upper-chest height. Avoid raising the hands above the face, which shifts work to the front delts.
steps.tempo: 2-1-2-0: two seconds up, one-second squeeze, two seconds down.
steps.finish: Finish with the hands meeting at upper-chest height and a brief squeeze.
steps.exit: Lower the handles under control, step back to slacken the cables and return the handles to the low pulleys.

mistakes.m: Shrugging the shoulders as the hands rise
mistakes.fix: Keep shoulders down and stop at upper-chest height.

mistakes.m: Leaning back to swing the weight up
mistakes.fix: Lighten the load and keep the ribs down.

mistakes.m: Turning it into a front raise by lifting too high
mistakes.fix: Finish at the upper chest, not overhead.

safety: Keep the load light; long lever arms load the shoulder heavily.
Stop if you feel pinching at the front of the shoulder.
checks: Both pulleys are at the bottom setting.
Same weight selected on both stacks with pins fully in.
Handles are clipped securely.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if you lean back, shrug, or bend the elbows to get the hands up.

programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week, usually after an upper-chest press.
programming.initialLoad: Start very light, around half of your mid-height cable fly load, and aim for 15 controlled reps with 2-3 in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: Each rep should finish at the same height with a held squeeze and no torso movement.
programming.progression: Double progression within 12-15 reps, then add the smallest stack increment.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets reach 15 reps with no lean or shrug.
programming.maintain: Keep the weight if technique slips; reduce if the shoulders feel irritated.

name: High-to-low cable fly
musclesText: Primary: pectoralis major (sternal and abdominal fibres). Secondary: anterior deltoid, pectoralis minor, serratus anterior.

steps.start: Stand in the middle of a dual cable station holding a D-handle in each hand, arms out wide and above shoulder height.
steps.setup: Set both pulleys to a high position, above head height, and attach single D-handles. Select the same weight on both stacks.
steps.feet: Step forward into a staggered stance so the cables are under tension with your arms wide and slightly behind your torso.
steps.grip: Hold the handles with palms facing down and slightly forward, elbows softly bent and fixed.
steps.posture: Hinge very slightly forward from the hips with a neutral spine and chest up.
steps.brace: Brace your trunk so your torso does not rock forward to help pull the handles down.
steps.initiate: Begin by pulling your upper arms down and in, as if hugging something in front of your waist.
steps.concentric: Sweep the hands down and together in an arc until they meet in front of your lower abdomen, around belly-button height.
steps.breathing: Exhale as the hands come down and together; inhale as they return.
steps.eccentric: Let the hands rise slowly back along the same arc to about shoulder height or just above, feeling the chest stretch.
steps.rom: Move from about shoulder height with arms wide down to the hands meeting at lower-abdomen height. Do not let the arms drift far behind you at the top.
steps.tempo: 2-1-2-0: two seconds down, one-second squeeze, two seconds back up.
steps.finish: Finish with the hands together in front of the lower abdomen and a brief squeeze.
steps.exit: Return the handles under control to shoulder height, step back towards the stack and hand each handle back to its pulley.

cues: Hands sweep down to the belly button

mistakes.m: Bending the elbows so it becomes a pushdown
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbow angle fixed and move from the shoulder.

mistakes.m: Rocking the torso forward to finish the rep
mistakes.fix: Brace and use a lighter weight.

mistakes.m: Letting the arms be pulled back too far at the top
mistakes.fix: Stop the return at shoulder height with a comfortable stretch.

safety: Avoid letting the cables drag the shoulders into an extreme stretch.
Keep the load moderate so the handles cannot pull you off balance.
checks: Both pulleys are set to the same high position.
Pins are fully inserted with equal weight on each side.
Handles are securely clipped.
reduceLoad: Reduce the weight if your torso bobs, your elbows bend to finish, or the handles snap back at the top.

programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Start light enough for 15 controlled reps with a held squeeze and 2-3 reps in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: The squeeze at the bottom should be held for a second without the torso moving.
programming.progression: Double progression within 10-15 reps, then add the smallest stack increment.
programming.increase: Increase when every set reaches 15 reps with a clean squeeze.
programming.maintain: Keep the load if torso movement creeps in; reduce if the shoulders are uncomfortable.

name: Pec deck
musclesText: Primary: pectoralis major (sternal and clavicular heads). Secondary: anterior deltoid, serratus anterior.

steps.start: Sit on the pec-deck machine with your back against the pad and grip a handle in each hand, arms out wide to your sides.
steps.setup: Adjust the seat so the handles are at about mid-chest height and your upper arms are roughly parallel with the floor. Set the arm start position so your hands are just in line with or slightly in front of your torso, not behind it.
steps.feet: Feet flat on the floor or footrest, knees about hip-width apart.
steps.grip: Grip the vertical handles with a neutral grip and a slight, fixed bend in the elbows; on pad versions, place the forearms against the pads.
steps.posture: Sit tall with your head, upper back and hips against the pad and shoulder blades gently pulled back.
steps.brace: Brace lightly so your back stays on the pad throughout.
steps.initiate: Begin by squeezing your arms towards each other in front of your chest.
steps.concentric: Bring the handles together in a smooth arc until they nearly touch in front of your chest, squeezing your chest hard.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you bring the handles together; inhale as they open.
steps.eccentric: Let the handles open slowly under control until your hands are roughly in line with your chest and you feel a stretch, keeping the weight stack from touching down.
steps.rom: Open to a comfortable stretch with hands roughly in line with your torso; close until the handles are nearly touching.
steps.tempo: 2-1-2-0: two seconds in, one-second squeeze, two seconds back.
steps.finish: Finish with the handles together in front of your chest and a held squeeze.
steps.exit: After the last rep, let the handles return slowly to the start position until the stack rests, then release the handles.

cues: Do not let the stack crash

mistakes.m: Seat too low or high so the shoulders take over
mistakes.fix: Adjust so the handles are at mid-chest height.

mistakes.m: Start position set too far back, overstretching the shoulder
mistakes.fix: Set the arm range so the hands start roughly in line with the torso.

mistakes.m: Rounding the shoulders forward at the finish
mistakes.fix: Keep the upper back on the pad and the chest up.

safety: Overstretching at the start position is the main risk; set the range limiter conservatively.
Stop if you feel pain at the front of the shoulder.
checks: Seat height puts the handles at mid-chest level.
Start-range setting is not too far back.
Pin is fully inserted in the stack.
reduceLoad: Reduce the weight if your back leaves the pad, your shoulders roll forward, or the stack slams between reps.
regressions: Lighter pec deck with a shortened range

programming.rehab: Light pec-deck work through a short, pain-free range is a gentle way to load the chest in rehabilitation, ideally under a physiotherapist's guidance.
programming.frequency: 1-3 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Choose a stack weight you can squeeze for 15 reps with 2-3 in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: Every rep should have a held squeeze and a slow return; if the stack drops, it is too heavy.
programming.progression: Double progression within 10-15 reps, then increase by one plate.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets reach 15 reps with a full squeeze.
programming.maintain: Keep the weight if your back leaves the pad; reduce if the shoulder feels strained.

name: Machine chest press
musclesText: Primary: pectoralis major (sternal head). Secondary: anterior deltoid, triceps brachii.

steps.start: Sit upright in the chest press machine with your back against the pad and the handles beside your chest.
steps.setup: Adjust the seat so the handles line up with your mid-chest. On a plate-loaded machine, load plates evenly on both sides; on a selectorised machine, set the pin. If there is a foot lever to bring the handles forward, locate it before you start.
steps.feet: Feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart, and drive lightly through your heels to stay planted.
steps.grip: Grip the horizontal or neutral handles with a full grip; your wrists should be straight and in line with your forearms.
steps.posture: Sit tall with your head and upper back on the pad and shoulder blades pulled back and down.
steps.brace: Breathe in and brace the trunk so your back stays on the pad as you press.
steps.initiate: Start the press by driving the handles forward from the chest without letting the shoulders roll forward off the pad.
steps.concentric: Press the handles forward until your arms are nearly straight, keeping your elbows about 45-70 degrees from your torso.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you press out; inhale as you return.
steps.eccentric: Return the handles under control until your hands are level with your chest and you feel a stretch, without letting the weight touch down.
steps.rom: Use the range from a chest stretch to just short of a hard lockout; keep tension on the stack between reps.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-0: two seconds back, no pause, one second press.
steps.finish: Finish with arms extended and shoulder blades still on the pad.
steps.exit: Return the handles slowly to the start until the weight rests, or use the foot lever to lower them if fitted. Unload plate-loaded machines evenly.

mistakes.m: Seat height wrong so the handles are at the neck or belly
mistakes.fix: Adjust so the handles line up with the mid-chest.

mistakes.m: Shoulders rolling forward off the pad at the end
mistakes.fix: Stop just short of lockout and keep the upper back on the pad.

mistakes.m: Letting the stack crash between reps
mistakes.fix: Control the return and keep the weight just off the stack.

safety: Set the starting range so your shoulders are not pulled behind your torso.
Stop if you feel sharp pain in the shoulder or elbow.
checks: Seat height puts the handles at mid-chest.
Pin fully inserted or plates loaded evenly and secured.
Back pad and range settings are locked.
reduceLoad: Reduce the weight if your back leaves the pad, one arm leads the other on a converging machine, or the stack drops between reps.

programming.rehab: The fixed path makes it suited to gentle, pain-free pressing during rehabilitation; start very light and follow a physiotherapist's advice.
programming.frequency: 1-3 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Start light, about 10-12 reps with 3 reps in reserve, then adjust over the next sets.
programming.judgeLoad: Both arms should press evenly and the last rep should slow without your back leaving the pad.
programming.progression: Double progression within the rep range, then add one stack plate or 2.5-5 kg on a plate-loaded machine.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets reach the top of the range.
programming.maintain: Keep the weight if reps fall short; reduce if the shoulders or elbows are irritated.

name: Incline machine chest press
musclesText: Primary: pectoralis major (clavicular head), anterior deltoid. Secondary: triceps brachii, serratus anterior.

steps.start: Sit in the incline press machine with your back against the reclined pad and the handles beside your upper chest.
steps.setup: Adjust the seat so the handles line up with your upper chest, around the level of your armpits or slightly higher. Set the pin or load plates evenly.
steps.feet: Feet flat on the floor or footrest, hip-width apart.
steps.grip: Grip the handles with a full grip, wrists straight; use the neutral or pronated handles depending on shoulder comfort.
steps.posture: Head and upper back on the pad, shoulder blades back and down, chest up.
steps.brace: Breathe in and brace so your lower back does not arch off the pad as you press.
steps.initiate: Drive the handles up and forward from the upper chest.
steps.concentric: Press along the machine's path until your arms are almost straight, keeping your elbows slightly below your hands.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you press; inhale as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower the handles under control to upper-chest level until you feel a stretch, without letting the stack rest.
steps.rom: From a comfortable stretch at the upper chest to just short of lockout.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-0: two seconds down, no pause, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish with arms extended and shoulder blades still pinned to the pad.
steps.exit: Lower the handles slowly until the weight rests, then release and stand up.

mistakes.m: Seat too low so the press feels like a shoulder press
mistakes.fix: Raise the seat so the handles start at upper-chest height.

mistakes.m: Arching the lower back to press
mistakes.fix: Brace and keep the lower back on the pad.

mistakes.m: Bouncing out of the bottom
mistakes.fix: Control the lowering and keep tension.

safety: Avoid an excessive starting stretch that pulls the shoulders behind the body.
Stop if you feel pinching at the front of the shoulder.
checks: Seat height puts the handles at upper-chest level.
Pin fully inserted or plates loaded evenly.
Back pad angle and handles are locked.
reduceLoad: Reduce the weight if your back arches off the pad, you shrug, or reps slow sharply early in the set.

programming.rehab: A light, fixed-path incline press can help reintroduce upper-chest pressing during later rehabilitation; check with a physiotherapist.
programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Start with a weight you could press for about 12 reps with 3 in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: Smooth reps with the back on the pad; stop with 0-2 reps in reserve.
programming.progression: Double progression, adding one plate when all sets reach the top of the range.
programming.increase: Increase when every set reaches the top of the range.
programming.maintain: Keep the weight if technique slips; reduce if the shoulders feel irritated.

name: Smith machine bench press
musclesText: Primary: pectoralis major (sternal and clavicular heads). Secondary: anterior deltoid, triceps brachii.

steps.start: Lie on a flat bench under the Smith machine so the bar lines up with your lower chest when lowered.
steps.setup: Position the bench so the bar's fixed path touches your lower chest at the bottom. Set the safety stops just above your chest height at the bottom of the rep. Learn the rotate-to-unhook mechanism before loading.
steps.feet: Feet flat on the floor, slightly wider than hip-width.
steps.grip: Medium grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width, so forearms are vertical at the bottom. Full thumb wrap.
steps.posture: Shoulder blades back and down, head and glutes on the bench, slight upper-back arch.
steps.brace: Breathe in, brace the trunk and drive lightly through your feet.
steps.initiate: Rotate your wrists to unhook the bar from the safety hooks, then lower it.
steps.concentric: Press the bar straight up along the guide rails to lockout, keeping wrists over elbows.
steps.breathing: Inhale at the top, hold through the descent and press, exhale near lockout.
steps.eccentric: Lower the bar under control to your lower chest with elbows tucked about 45-70 degrees.
steps.rom: Touch the lower chest lightly or stop just above it, then press to lockout.
steps.tempo: 2-1-1-0: two seconds down, light touch, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish with arms straight and the bar over your lower chest.
steps.exit: At lockout, rotate the bar to engage the nearest hook and confirm it is locked before letting go.

cues: Bar path fixed: set the bench right
Hook it before you let go

mistakes.m: Bench positioned so the bar lands on the neck or belly
mistakes.fix: Do a dry rep with the empty bar to check where it touches.

mistakes.m: Not setting the safety stops
mistakes.fix: Set them just above chest height at the bottom of the rep.

mistakes.m: Flaring the elbows wide
mistakes.fix: Tuck to about 45-70 degrees.

safety: Always set the safety stops; they are your spotter.
Make sure the bar is hooked before releasing your grip.
Many Smith machines have a counterbalanced bar; know its starting weight.
checks: Bench position puts the touch point at the lower chest.
Safety stops are set and locked on both sides.
Plates are loaded evenly with collars on.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if the bar touches somewhere other than your lower chest, your hips lift, or you need to bounce reps.

programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Start with the empty bar and build up to a load you can press for the target reps with 2-3 in reserve. Smith loads are not directly comparable to barbell loads.
programming.judgeLoad: Bar speed should stay smooth; stop with 1-2 reps in reserve.
programming.progression: Double progression, adding 2.5 kg after all sets reach the top.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets reach the top of the range.
programming.maintain: Keep the load if the touch point drifts; reduce if shoulders feel irritated.

name: Push-up
musclesText: Primary: pectoralis major. Secondary: anterior deltoid, triceps brachii, serratus anterior, rectus abdominis and deep trunk muscles.

steps.start: Start in a high plank on the floor with your hands under or slightly wider than your shoulders and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
steps.setup: No equipment needed; use a non-slip floor or mat. Clear the area around you.
steps.feet: Feet together or up to hip-width apart, balanced on the balls of the feet.
steps.grip: Hands flat, slightly wider than shoulder-width, fingers spread and pointing forward or slightly out.
steps.posture: Body straight from head to heels, neck neutral with eyes on the floor slightly ahead of your hands. Squeeze your glutes to keep the hips level.
steps.brace: Brace your abs as if holding a plank and keep the ribs down so the lower back does not sag.
steps.initiate: Begin by bending your elbows and lowering your whole body as one unit.
steps.concentric: Push the floor away, driving your body back up in one piece until your arms are straight, spreading the shoulder blades slightly at the top.
steps.breathing: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you push up.
steps.eccentric: Lower until your chest is a fist's width or less from the floor, elbows angled about 45 degrees from your sides.
steps.rom: Chest close to the floor at the bottom, arms straight at the top. If you cannot reach full depth with good form, use the incline push-up.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-0: two seconds down, no pause, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish with arms straight and the body in a rigid straight line.
steps.exit: After the last rep, lower your knees to the floor and sit back.

mistakes.m: Hips sagging towards the floor
mistakes.fix: Brace the abs and squeeze the glutes; regress to an incline if needed.

mistakes.m: Elbows flaring straight out
mistakes.fix: Keep elbows about 45 degrees from your sides.

mistakes.m: Partial reps, only bending the elbows a little
mistakes.fix: Lower until the chest is near the floor; use an incline to build up.

mistakes.m: Head dropping forward
mistakes.fix: Keep the neck in line with your spine.

safety: Stop if you feel wrist pain; try push-up handles or fists to keep the wrists straight.
Stop if you feel sharp shoulder pain or tingling down the arm.
checks: Floor is dry and non-slip.
There is enough space for your full body length.
reduceLoad: Switch to an incline push-up if your hips sag, you cannot reach full depth, or form breaks before 5 reps.

programming.rehab: Push-ups against a wall or bench can rebuild pressing tolerance after shoulder or wrist issues; progress gradually with a physiotherapist's guidance.
programming.frequency: 2-4 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Test how many full reps you can do with good form; if fewer than 5, start with the incline push-up.
programming.judgeLoad: Stop the set when the hips start to sag or depth decreases, usually 1-3 reps before failure.
programming.progression: Add reps each session; once you can do 3 sets of 20, progress to deficit or weighted push-ups.
programming.increase: Progress when you can complete all sets at the top of your rep target with full depth.
programming.maintain: Hold the rep count if form breaks; reduce the incline difficulty if you cannot reach 5 good reps.

name: Weighted push-up
musclesText: Primary: pectoralis major. Secondary: anterior deltoid, triceps brachii, serratus anterior, rectus abdominis.

steps.start: Get into a high plank position with a weight plate resting flat on your upper back between your shoulder blades, or while wearing a weight vest.
steps.setup: For a plate, have a partner place it on your upper back once you are in position, or kneel and slide it on carefully. Make sure it sits over the shoulder blades, not the lower back. A vest should be snug and not slide.
steps.feet: Feet hip-width apart for extra stability, on the balls of the feet.
steps.grip: Hands flat, slightly wider than shoulder-width, fingers spread.
steps.posture: Body in a straight line from head to heels, neck neutral and glutes squeezed, with the upper back level so the plate stays flat.
steps.brace: Brace hard: the extra load makes the hips more likely to sag.
steps.initiate: Begin by bending the elbows and lowering the body as one unit, keeping the plate balanced.
steps.concentric: Push the floor away and press back up to straight arms, keeping your back flat so the plate does not slide.
steps.breathing: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you push up.
steps.eccentric: Lower under control until your chest is close to the floor, elbows about 45 degrees from your sides.
steps.rom: Chest close to the floor at the bottom, arms straight at the top.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-0: two seconds down, no pause, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish with straight arms and a level back.
steps.exit: Lower your knees to the floor and have your partner lift the plate off, or let it slide off carefully to the side away from your head; remove a vest once seated.

mistakes.m: Placing the plate on the lower back
mistakes.fix: Position it high on the upper back, between the shoulder blades.

mistakes.m: Hips sagging under the load
mistakes.fix: Brace harder or reduce the load.

mistakes.m: Shortening the range as fatigue sets in
mistakes.fix: End the set once depth decreases.

safety: Have a partner place and remove plates to avoid them falling on your head or hands.
Master 3 sets of 20 bodyweight push-ups before adding load.
Stop if you feel wrist or shoulder pain.
checks: The plate has no sharp edges and sits flat, or the vest is fitted snugly.
Floor is non-slip and clear.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if the plate slides, your hips sag, or you cannot reach full depth.

programming.frequency: 1-3 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Start with 5-10 kg once you can do 20 strict bodyweight push-ups, and aim for 10-12 reps.
programming.judgeLoad: Each rep should reach full depth with a flat back; stop with 1-3 reps in reserve.
programming.progression: Double progression, then add 2.5-5 kg.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets reach the top of the range with full depth.
programming.maintain: Keep the load if the back starts to sag; reduce if the wrists or shoulders are uncomfortable.

name: Deficit push-up
musclesText: Primary: pectoralis major (emphasis on the stretched position). Secondary: anterior deltoid, triceps brachii, serratus anterior, rectus abdominis.

steps.start: Set up in a high plank with each hand on a raised push-up handle, a stable plate or a block, so your chest can travel below hand level.
steps.setup: Use two stable push-up handles, parallettes or flat plates of equal height, usually 5-10 cm. Place them slightly wider than shoulder-width so your chest can drop between them.
steps.feet: Feet together or hip-width apart on the balls of the feet.
steps.grip: Grip the handles with a neutral grip, or place your palms flat in the middle of the plates. Keep the wrists straight.
steps.posture: Body straight from head to heels, neck neutral, glutes squeezed.
steps.brace: Brace the abs firmly to stop the hips sagging at the deeper bottom position.
steps.initiate: Begin by bending the elbows and lowering your body as one unit between your hands.
steps.concentric: Push hard through the handles to drive your body back up to straight arms.
steps.breathing: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you push up.
steps.eccentric: Lower slowly until your chest passes below the level of your hands and you feel a strong stretch across the chest, elbows about 45 degrees from your sides.
steps.rom: Go only as deep as your shoulders comfortably allow, typically chest a few centimetres below hand level; press to full lockout.
steps.tempo: 3-1-1-0: three seconds down, one-second pause in the stretch, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish with arms straight and body rigid.
steps.exit: Lower your knees to the floor between the handles and step out of position.

mistakes.m: Going too deep and letting the shoulders roll forward
mistakes.fix: Stop at a comfortable stretch with shoulders still set.

mistakes.m: Using unstable or uneven supports
mistakes.fix: Use matched push-up handles or flat plates that do not rock.

mistakes.m: Hips sagging at the bottom
mistakes.fix: Brace harder and shorten the range if needed.

safety: The extra depth loads the front of the shoulder; build up the deficit gradually.
Stop if you feel sharp shoulder pain or tingling down the arms.
checks: Handles or plates are stable, equal in height and on a non-slip surface.
There is enough clearance for your chest between the supports.
reduceLoad: Reduce the deficit height or switch to a standard push-up if you cannot pause at the bottom or your hips sag.

programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Start with a small deficit of about 5 cm once you can do 15-20 standard push-ups.
programming.judgeLoad: You should be able to pause at the bottom on every rep without losing your plank.
programming.progression: Add reps first, then increase the deficit slightly, then add a weight vest.
programming.increase: Progress when all sets reach the top of the rep range with a full pause.
programming.maintain: Keep the deficit if any reps lose depth; reduce it if the shoulders feel irritated.

name: Incline push-up
musclesText: Primary: pectoralis major. Secondary: anterior deltoid, triceps brachii, serratus anterior, trunk muscles.

steps.start: Place your hands on the edge of a stable bench or box and walk your feet back until your body forms a straight line, angled upwards towards your hands.
steps.setup: Use a stable flat bench, plyo box or a racked barbell at a fixed height. The higher the surface, the easier the exercise; start at a height that lets you do 10-15 good reps.
steps.feet: Feet together or hip-width apart, on the balls of the feet.
steps.grip: Hands on the edge of the bench slightly wider than shoulder-width, fingers forward and wrists stacked under the shoulders.
steps.posture: Body straight from head to heels, neck neutral, glutes squeezed.
steps.brace: Brace your abs as for a plank so the hips do not sag or pike.
steps.initiate: Begin by bending the elbows and lowering your chest towards the edge of the bench.
steps.concentric: Push the bench away and return to straight arms, moving your body as one unit.
steps.breathing: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you push up.
steps.eccentric: Lower under control until your chest lightly touches or nearly touches the edge, elbows about 45 degrees from your sides.
steps.rom: Chest to the edge of the support at the bottom, arms straight at the top.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-0: two seconds down, no pause, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish with straight arms and the body still in one line.
steps.exit: Walk your feet forward towards the bench and stand up.

mistakes.m: Using an unstable surface that can slide
mistakes.fix: Use a fixed bench, a stable box against a wall or a racked bar.

mistakes.m: Hips piking up or sagging
mistakes.fix: Brace and squeeze the glutes; move your feet closer if needed.

mistakes.m: Only lowering partway
mistakes.fix: Touch the chest to the edge each rep; raise the surface if needed.

safety: Check the bench or box cannot tip or slide.
Stop if you feel wrist or shoulder pain.
checks: Support is stable and at the chosen height.
Floor is non-slip for your feet.
reduceLoad: Raise the surface height if you cannot complete 8 good reps or your hips sag.

programming.rehab: Incline push-ups at a high, comfortable angle are a gentle way to rebuild pressing after shoulder or wrist problems; progress gradually and follow a physiotherapist's advice.
programming.frequency: 2-4 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Choose a surface height that allows 10-15 reps with good form and 2-3 in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: Stop the set when depth or body alignment slips.
programming.progression: Add reps, then lower the surface step by step towards the floor push-up.
programming.increase: Lower the surface when you can do 3 sets of 15-20 with good form.
programming.maintain: Keep the same height if form breaks; raise it if you cannot reach 8 reps.

name: Chest dip
musclesText: Primary: pectoralis major (sternal and lower fibres), triceps brachii. Secondary: anterior deltoid, pectoralis minor.

steps.start: Grip the parallel bars and jump or step up to support yourself on straight arms, with your shoulders above your hands.
steps.setup: Use parallel dip bars about shoulder-width apart or slightly wider. Use a step to get into position if the bars are high.
steps.feet: Cross or bend your legs behind you, or keep them slightly forward; bent knees help you lean the torso forward.
steps.grip: Neutral grip on the bars, hands about shoulder-width or slightly wider, wrists stacked over the forearms.
steps.posture: Lean your torso forward about 20-40 degrees, chest up and shoulders down away from the ears.
steps.brace: Brace the trunk so you do not swing.
steps.initiate: Begin by bending the elbows and lowering your body while keeping the forward lean.
steps.concentric: Push down through the bars to straighten your arms, keeping the forward lean, until you are back at the top.
steps.breathing: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you press up.
steps.eccentric: Lower slowly, letting the elbows flare slightly, until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor and you feel a stretch across the chest.
steps.rom: Lower until the upper arms are around parallel with the floor; go no deeper than your shoulders tolerate comfortably.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-0: two seconds down, no pause, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish with arms straight, shoulders depressed and torso still leaning forward.
steps.exit: Step down onto the platform or lower yourself slowly to the floor; do not drop from the bars.

mistakes.m: Staying upright, which shifts work to the triceps
mistakes.fix: Lean the torso forward 20-40 degrees.

mistakes.m: Dropping too deep so the shoulders roll forward
mistakes.fix: Stop at about parallel.

mistakes.m: Shrugging the shoulders up to the ears
mistakes.fix: Keep the shoulders pressed down throughout.

safety: Dips place high stress on the front of the shoulder; avoid them or reduce the depth if you have a shoulder problem.
Stop immediately if you feel sharp pain in the shoulder or sternum.
checks: The dip bars are secure and the right width.
There is a step to mount and dismount safely.
reduceLoad: Switch to an assisted dip if you cannot reach parallel with control or you swing to complete reps.

programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Start with bodyweight; if you cannot do 5 controlled reps, use an assisted machine or band.
programming.judgeLoad: Stop when depth decreases or you begin swinging.
programming.progression: Add reps up to 12-15, then add load with a dip belt.
programming.increase: Add load when you can do 3 sets of 12 with control.
programming.maintain: Keep the load if depth decreases; reduce if the shoulders are irritated.

name: Close-grip bench press
musclesText: Primary: triceps brachii, pectoralis major (sternal head). Secondary: anterior deltoid.

steps.start: Lie on a flat bench with your eyes under the racked bar.
steps.setup: Set the J-hooks so you can unrack with arms nearly straight and set the safety arms just below chest height at the bottom.
steps.feet: Feet flat on the floor, slightly wider than hip-width.
steps.grip: Grip the bar with hands about shoulder-width apart, no narrower; a grip that is too close strains the wrists. Full thumb wrap.
steps.posture: Shoulder blades pulled back and down, slight upper-back arch, head and glutes on the bench.
steps.brace: Breathe in, brace the trunk and drive lightly through the feet.
steps.initiate: Unrack, bring the bar over your shoulders and pause.
steps.concentric: Press the bar up and slightly back to lockout, driving with the triceps and keeping the elbows close.
steps.breathing: Inhale at the top, hold through the descent and press, exhale near lockout.
steps.eccentric: Lower the bar under control to your lower chest with the elbows tucked close to your sides, about 30-45 degrees.
steps.rom: Touch the lower chest and press to full lockout.
steps.tempo: 2-1-1-0: two seconds down, brief touch, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish with arms locked and the bar over your shoulders.
steps.exit: Lock out, guide the bar back to the uprights and lower it into the hooks.

cues: Lock out hard with the triceps

mistakes.m: Grip too narrow, with hands touching
mistakes.fix: Place hands about shoulder-width apart.

mistakes.m: Elbows flaring out
mistakes.fix: Keep them tucked close to your sides.

mistakes.m: Bar touching too high on the chest
mistakes.fix: Aim for the lower chest.

safety: Set safeties or use a spotter.
Stop if you feel wrist or elbow pain; widen the grip slightly.
checks: Safeties and hooks are set evenly.
Collars are on and plates matched.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if your elbows flare, the bar drifts, or you cannot lock out cleanly.

programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Start at about 70-80 percent of your bench press working weight.
programming.judgeLoad: The bar should move smoothly to lockout with tucked elbows; stop with 1-3 reps in reserve.
programming.progression: Double progression, adding 2.5 kg when all sets reach the top.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets reach the top of the range.
programming.maintain: Keep the load if lockout slows; reduce if the elbows or wrists ache.

name: Dumbbell pullover
musclesText: Primary: pectoralis major (sternal head), latissimus dorsi. Secondary: long head of triceps brachii, teres major, serratus anterior, rectus abdominis.

steps.start: Lie on your back along a flat bench, or across it with only your upper back supported, holding one dumbbell above your chest with both hands.
steps.setup: Use a flat bench. Start with a light to moderate dumbbell; this movement takes the shoulder through a large range.
steps.feet: Feet flat on the floor. If lying across the bench, keep your hips level with or slightly below the bench.
steps.grip: Hold one end of the dumbbell with both hands, palms against the inner plate and thumbs wrapped around the handle, forming a diamond shape.
steps.posture: Keep a natural spine, ribs down, and maintain a slight fixed bend in the elbows.
steps.brace: Brace the abs to stop your ribcage flaring as the arms go overhead.
steps.initiate: Begin by lowering the dumbbell in an arc back over your head, keeping the elbows slightly bent.
steps.concentric: Pull the dumbbell back over your chest in the same arc, squeezing the chest and lats.
steps.breathing: Inhale as you lower behind your head and exhale as you pull back.
steps.eccentric: Lower slowly until your upper arms are roughly in line with your torso or a comfortable stretch through the chest and lats.
steps.rom: From above your chest to a comfortable overhead stretch, usually arms in line with the torso. Avoid going deeper than your shoulders allow.
steps.tempo: 3-1-1-0: three seconds down, one-second pause in the stretch, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish with the dumbbell above your chest, arms nearly straight.
steps.exit: Bring the dumbbell to your chest and sit up, or carefully pass it down to the floor.

mistakes.m: Bending the elbows so it becomes a triceps extension
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbow angle fixed.

mistakes.m: Flaring the ribs and arching the lower back
mistakes.fix: Brace the abs and limit the range.

mistakes.m: Going too heavy and overstretching the shoulder
mistakes.fix: Use a moderate weight and stop at a comfortable stretch.

safety: Check your grip on the dumbbell; it passes over your face.
Avoid going too deep if you have shoulder impingement or instability.
Stop if you feel sharp pain in the shoulder.
checks: The dumbbell is secure with no loose plates or collars.
The bench is stable and there is space behind your head.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if your elbows bend, your back arches, or you cannot pause in the stretch.

programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Start with a light dumbbell that lets you complete 12-15 reps with a pause.
programming.judgeLoad: Your ribs should stay down and your elbows fixed; stop with 1-3 reps in reserve.
programming.progression: Double progression, then increase by 2 kg.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets reach 15 reps with control.
programming.maintain: Keep the load if your form changes; reduce if the shoulders are uncomfortable.

name: Pull-up
musclesText: Primary: latissimus dorsi, lower and middle trapezius, rhomboids. Secondary: biceps brachii, brachialis, posterior deltoid, forearm flexors, rectus abdominis.

steps.start: Hang from a fixed bar with an overhand grip, arms fully straight and feet clear of the floor.
steps.setup: Use a solid fixed pull-up bar high enough that your feet do not touch the floor when you hang; use a box or step to reach it if needed.
steps.feet: Keep your legs together and straight or cross your ankles with knees slightly bent; avoid swinging them.
steps.grip: Take an overhand (pronated) grip slightly wider than shoulder width, thumbs wrapped around the bar.
steps.posture: Hang with ribs down and a slight hollow body position, head neutral, looking forwards rather than up at the bar.
steps.brace: Squeeze your glutes and brace your abdominals as if about to be prodded, so your pelvis and legs stay still under you.
steps.initiate: Start by drawing your shoulder blades down and slightly back, so you move from a dead hang into an active hang before your elbows bend.
steps.concentric: Drive your elbows down towards your back pockets and pull until your chin clears the bar, keeping your chest heading towards it.
steps.breathing: Take a breath and brace at the bottom, hold it through the pull, and exhale as you pass the top or on the way down.
steps.eccentric: Lower under control until your elbows are fully straight and your shoulders have returned to an active hang.
steps.rom: Full range: from straight arms at the bottom to chin over the bar at the top, without craning your neck to reach.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-0: two seconds down, no pause at the bottom, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish each rep with chin over the bar and shoulder blades pulled down, then lower without dropping.
steps.exit: After the last rep, lower to straight arms, then step down onto the box or drop lightly with soft knees.

mistakes.m: Kipping or swinging the legs to get up
mistakes.fix: Brace your trunk, squeeze your glutes and slow the rep down; use assistance if you cannot pull strictly.

mistakes.m: Half reps that stop short of straight arms
mistakes.fix: Lower all the way to an active hang each rep and count only full reps.

mistakes.m: Reaching the chin up by craning the neck
mistakes.fix: Keep the head neutral and pull the chest towards the bar instead.

mistakes.m: Shrugging the shoulders up to the ears
mistakes.fix: Set your shoulder blades down first and keep them there as you pull.

safety: Avoid dropping into a passive, jolted dead hang at the bottom, which loads the shoulder joint and elbow abruptly.
Build volume gradually if you are new to pulling, as the elbow flexor tendons adapt more slowly than muscle.
Stop if you feel sharp shoulder or elbow pain, or tingling into the hand.
checks: Check the bar is fixed securely and will take your full bodyweight plus any swing.
Make sure there is clear space around and below you and a stable box to reach the bar.
Chalk or dry your hands if grip is slipping.
reduceLoad: Use an easier option if you cannot complete at least three strict full-range reps, if your legs start swinging, or if your chin no longer clears the bar.

programming.rehab: Not a typical rehab exercise; after a shoulder or elbow injury rebuild with lat pulldowns or assisted pull-ups and seek physiotherapist guidance before returning to full bodyweight.
programming.frequency: 1-3 times per week, with at least 48 h between hard pulling sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Start with bodyweight; if you can do fewer than five strict reps, use sets of two to three reps across several sets or switch to an assisted version.
programming.judgeLoad: Aim to finish each set with one to three clean reps left; stop the set when your chin no longer clears the bar or you start to swing.
programming.progression: Rep progression: add a rep per set each week until you reach the top of the range, then add a small belt load (1.25-2.5 kg).
programming.increase: Increase difficulty when you can do all sets at the top of your rep range with strict form.
programming.maintain: Keep the same difficulty while reps are still climbing; reduce volume if elbow or shoulder discomfort persists after sessions.

name: Assisted pull-up
musclesText: Primary: latissimus dorsi, lower and middle trapezius, rhomboids. Secondary: biceps brachii, brachialis, posterior deltoid, forearm flexors.

steps.start: Kneel on the machine's counterweight pad (or stand in a looped band) and hang from the overhand handles with straight arms.
steps.setup: Select the assistance weight on the stack: more weight means more help. With a band, loop it over the bar and choose a thicker band for more help.
steps.feet: On the machine, place both knees on the centre of the pad, hip-width apart; with a band, put one foot or both knees in the loop.
steps.grip: Hold the overhand handles slightly wider than shoulder width with thumbs wrapped.
steps.posture: Keep your torso tall with a slight lean back, ribs down and head neutral.
steps.brace: Brace your abdominals and keep your hips under you so the pad or band does not swing forward.
steps.initiate: Draw your shoulder blades down before bending the elbows.
steps.concentric: Pull your elbows down and in towards your sides until your chin clears the handles.
steps.breathing: Breathe in at the bottom, hold your brace through the pull, and breathe out as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower slowly until your arms are straight; the assistance can make the descent feel too easy, so control it deliberately.
steps.rom: Full range from straight arms to chin above the handles.
steps.tempo: 3-0-1-0: three seconds down, no pause, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish with chin over the handles and shoulders down, away from the ears.
steps.exit: Lower to straight arms, step carefully off the pad one foot at a time onto the steps (or slide out of the band) before letting go.

mistakes.m: Too much assistance, so the set is not challenging
mistakes.fix: Reduce the counterweight until the last reps are hard but clean.

mistakes.m: Pushing off the pad with the legs
mistakes.fix: Keep the knees resting; let the counterweight, not your legs, provide the help.

mistakes.m: Letting the pad shoot you up at the bottom
mistakes.fix: Control the lowering and keep tension at the bottom.

mistakes.m: Stepping off the pad with weight still pushing up
mistakes.fix: Finish at the bottom with straight arms and step off carefully.

safety: Getting on and off the machine is where most slips happen; hold the handles and step deliberately.
With a band, make sure it cannot slip off your foot and snap upwards.
Stop if you feel sharp shoulder or elbow pain or tingling into the hand.
checks: Confirm the selector pin is fully inserted in the stack.
Check the band for nicks or tears and that it is looped securely around the bar.
Make sure the steps and pad are dry and stable.
reduceLoad: Add assistance (reduce load lifted) if your chin stops clearing the handles, you start pushing with your legs, or you cannot control the lowering.

programming.rehab: Useful for gradual return to vertical pulling with high assistance and slow reps; follow your physiotherapist's guidance after shoulder injury.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week, 48 h between hard sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Choose an assistance level that allows about 10 clean reps with two or three left in reserve; a common start is around half your bodyweight.
programming.judgeLoad: The last two reps should slow but stay full range; if your chin no longer clears or your legs push, add assistance.
programming.progression: Double progression on assistance: build to the top of the rep range, then reduce the counterweight by one plate (or use a thinner band).
programming.increase: Reduce assistance when all sets hit the top of the rep range with full range and control.
programming.maintain: Keep the same assistance while reps are still improving; increase assistance if form breaks down.

name: Chin-up
musclesText: Primary: latissimus dorsi, biceps brachii. Secondary: brachialis, brachioradialis, lower trapezius, rhomboids, rectus abdominis.

steps.start: Hang from a fixed bar with palms facing you, arms straight and feet off the floor.
steps.setup: Use a sturdy fixed bar high enough for a full hang; use a box to reach it.
steps.feet: Keep your legs together, straight or with ankles crossed, and still.
steps.grip: Take an underhand (supinated) grip about shoulder-width apart, thumbs wrapped round the bar, wrists straight.
steps.posture: Hold a slight hollow position with ribs down and head neutral.
steps.brace: Brace your abdominals and squeeze your glutes to stop your legs drifting forward.
steps.initiate: Pull your shoulder blades down to move into an active hang, then start bending your elbows.
steps.concentric: Pull your elbows down close to your sides and in front of your torso until your chin clears the bar and your upper chest approaches it.
steps.breathing: Breathe in and brace at the bottom, then exhale near the top or on the way down.
steps.eccentric: Lower steadily to straight elbows without letting your shoulders shrug up passively.
steps.rom: Straight arms at the bottom to chin above the bar at the top.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: two seconds down, no pause at the bottom, one second up, one-second squeeze at the top.
steps.finish: Finish with your chin over the bar and elbows tucked to your ribs.
steps.exit: Lower to straight arms and step down onto the box or drop lightly with bent knees.

mistakes.m: Grip so narrow the wrists bend and elbows hurt
mistakes.fix: Keep hands about shoulder width with wrists straight in line with the forearm.

mistakes.m: Stopping well short of straight arms
mistakes.fix: Lower fully to an active hang on every rep.

mistakes.m: Kicking the legs to finish reps
mistakes.fix: Brace and stop the set when strict reps run out.

mistakes.m: Leaning far back so it turns into a row
mistakes.fix: Keep a slight hollow and pull vertically.

safety: The supinated grip loads the biceps tendon and inner elbow more; build volume gradually and stop if you feel sharp pain at the elbow.
Avoid dropping into a jolting dead hang between reps.
Stop if you notice tingling into the fingers.
checks: Check the bar is secure and the knurling or grip surface is not slippery.
Use a stable box to mount the bar and clear the floor beneath you.
reduceLoad: Switch to an assisted version or reduce added weight if you cannot reach chin over the bar, your elbows ache during the set, or your legs begin to swing.

programming.frequency: 1-3 times per week, 48 h between hard pulling sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Use bodyweight; if you manage fewer than five reps, do several sets of two or three, or use assistance.
programming.judgeLoad: Finish sets with one to three strict reps left; the chin should still clear the bar on every rep.
programming.progression: Add reps each week; once all sets hit the top of the range, add 1.25-2.5 kg with a belt or dumbbell between the feet.
programming.increase: Add load when every set reaches the top of the rep range with full range and no swing.
programming.maintain: Hold the same load while reps are still climbing, and reduce volume if elbow tenderness lingers.

name: Neutral-grip pull-up
musclesText: Primary: latissimus dorsi, teres major, lower trapezius, rhomboids. Secondary: brachialis, brachioradialis, biceps brachii, posterior deltoid, rectus abdominis.

steps.start: Hang from the parallel handles with palms facing each other, arms straight and feet clear of the floor.
steps.setup: Use the parallel handles of a pull-up station or a multi-grip bar; mount from a box or step.
steps.feet: Keep your legs together and still, straight or with knees slightly bent and ankles crossed.
steps.grip: Grip the parallel handles with palms facing each other, thumbs wrapped; most stations place them a little narrower than shoulder width.
steps.posture: Hang tall with ribs down, a slight hollow and head neutral.
steps.brace: Brace your abdominals and squeeze your glutes to keep the body from swinging between the handles.
steps.initiate: Depress your shoulder blades into an active hang before you bend your elbows.
steps.concentric: Drive your elbows down by your sides until your chin clears the handles and your chest rises towards them.
steps.breathing: Breathe in and brace at the bottom, exhale over the top or as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower under control until the elbows are straight and the shoulders are still active.
steps.rom: From straight arms to chin above the handles; your head passes to one side of the frame, not into it.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-0: two seconds down, no pause, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish with chin above the handles and shoulders pulled down.
steps.exit: Lower to straight arms, then step down onto the box; do not drop onto the station's frame.

mistakes.m: Swinging forward between the handles
mistakes.fix: Brace, keep legs still and slow the lowering.

mistakes.m: Craning the neck over the handles
mistakes.fix: Keep the head neutral and lift the chest instead.

mistakes.m: Cutting the bottom of the rep short
mistakes.fix: Return to straight elbows every rep.

mistakes.m: Hitting the head on the frame
mistakes.fix: Check clearance and keep your face slightly back from the crossbar.
