safety: The neutral grip is often the most comfortable for the elbows and shoulders, but still stop if you feel sharp joint pain.
Watch your head clearance on stations with a crossbar between the handles.
Avoid ballistic drops into the bottom position.
checks: Check the handles are tight and the station is anchored.
Make sure there is enough head clearance above the handles.
reduceLoad: Use assistance or reduce added load when your chin no longer clears the handles, you begin to swing, or the lowering speeds up uncontrollably.

programming.rehab: A comfortable vertical pull for people returning from elbow or shoulder irritation once a physiotherapist has cleared full-bodyweight pulling; start with assistance.
programming.frequency: 1-3 times per week, 48 h between hard pulling sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Use bodyweight; if under five strict reps, use short sets or assistance.
programming.judgeLoad: End sets with one to three reps in reserve and every rep reaching the handles.
programming.progression: Double progression: add reps until the top of the range, then add 1.25-2.5 kg with a dip belt.
programming.increase: Increase load when all sets hit the top of the range with full, controlled reps.
programming.maintain: Keep load the same while reps climb; lower volume if joints feel irritated the next day.

name: Lat pulldown
musclesText: Primary: latissimus dorsi, teres major, lower and middle trapezius, rhomboids. Secondary: biceps brachii, brachialis, posterior deltoid, forearm flexors.

steps.start: Sit at the pulldown station with thighs locked under the pads and arms extended up to a straight bar.
steps.setup: Attach a long straight bar to the high pulley, set the thigh pad so it presses firmly on your thighs, and choose the weight on the stack.
steps.feet: Place your feet flat on the floor about hip-width apart, knees bent around 90 degrees.
steps.grip: Stand to take an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder width, then sit down with the bar, thumbs wrapped.
steps.posture: Sit tall with your chest up and a small lean back of about 10-20 degrees, keeping the lower back in its natural curve.
steps.brace: Brace your abdominals so your torso angle stays fixed rather than rocking back as you pull.
steps.initiate: Begin by drawing your shoulder blades down, then bend your elbows.
steps.concentric: Pull the bar to your upper chest, just below the collarbones, driving your elbows down and slightly back.
steps.breathing: Breathe in at the top with the arms extended, then exhale as you pull or as you return.
steps.eccentric: Let the bar rise under control until your arms are straight and you feel a stretch through your lats.
steps.rom: From fully extended arms with shoulders slightly elevated, to bar at upper chest.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: two seconds as the bar rises, no pause in the stretch, one second pulling down, one-second squeeze at the chest.
steps.finish: Finish with the bar touching or nearly touching your upper chest and the elbows pointing down.
steps.exit: Return the bar to full arm extension, stand up while holding it, and let the stack lower gently before releasing.

cues: Small lean back, not a swing

mistakes.m: Leaning far back and rowing the bar
mistakes.fix: Keep a small fixed lean and reduce the weight.

mistakes.m: Pulling the bar behind the neck
mistakes.fix: Pull to the front of the upper chest.

mistakes.m: Short reps that never reach the stretch
mistakes.fix: Let the arms straighten fully at the top.

mistakes.m: Yanking with momentum
mistakes.fix: Pause briefly at the top and pull smoothly.

safety: Behind-the-neck pulling stresses the shoulder and neck; keep the bar in front.
Stand up with the bar under control rather than letting the stack slam.
Stop if you get sharp shoulder pain or tingling in the hands.
checks: Set the thigh pad so you cannot lift off the seat.
Check the bar clip on the cable is closed and the cable is not frayed.
Make sure the selector pin is fully in the stack.
reduceLoad: Reduce the weight if you need to lean back more than about 20 degrees, your hips lift off the seat, or the bar stops short of your upper chest.

programming.rehab: Light, controlled pulldowns through a pain-free range are often used when rebuilding pulling after shoulder issues; follow your physiotherapist's guidance.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week, 48 h between hard sessions for the same muscles.
programming.initialLoad: Start with a weight you can pull for 12 clean reps with two or three left in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: The last reps should be slow but reach the chest without extra lean; leaning back or a lifting hip signals too heavy.
programming.progression: Double progression: build to the top of the rep range on all sets, then add one stack plate (2.5-5 kg).
programming.increase: Increase load once all sets reach the top of the range with clean form.
programming.maintain: Keep load the same while reps are still increasing; reduce it if form or range shrinks.

name: Neutral-grip lat pulldown
musclesText: Primary: latissimus dorsi, teres major, lower trapezius, rhomboids. Secondary: brachialis, brachioradialis, biceps brachii, posterior deltoid.

steps.start: Sit at the pulldown station with thighs under the pads, holding a parallel handle overhead with straight arms.
steps.setup: Clip a V-handle or wide neutral (parallel) handle to the high pulley, adjust the thigh pad to press firmly and set the stack weight.
steps.feet: Feet flat, about hip-width apart, knees around 90 degrees.
steps.grip: Hold the handles with palms facing each other, thumbs wrapped; with a V-handle your hands are close, with a wide neutral bar about shoulder width.
steps.posture: Sit tall with chest up and a slight lean back of about 15-30 degrees so the handle can travel to your chest.
steps.brace: Brace your trunk so the lean stays constant through the set.
steps.initiate: Draw your shoulder blades down, then start bending your elbows.
steps.concentric: Pull the handle down to your upper chest or sternum, driving the elbows down close to your sides.
steps.breathing: Breathe in with arms extended, exhale through the pull or on the return.
steps.eccentric: Allow the handle to rise slowly until your elbows are straight and the lats are stretched.
steps.rom: From full arm extension to the handle touching your upper chest.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: two seconds as the handle rises, no pause, one second down, one-second hold at the chest.
steps.finish: Finish with the handle at your chest and elbows tucked by your ribs.
steps.exit: Let the handle rise to full extension, stand while holding it and guide the stack down before letting go.

mistakes.m: Rocking the torso back and forth
mistakes.fix: Fix the lean and reduce the weight.

mistakes.m: Elbows flaring wide
mistakes.fix: Keep elbows close to your sides throughout.

mistakes.m: Wrists curling and biceps taking over
mistakes.fix: Keep wrists straight and think of pulling with the elbows.

mistakes.m: Not reaching full extension
mistakes.fix: Let arms straighten at the top of every rep.

safety: Keep the handle in front of your face as it passes; with a V-handle, keep your head slightly back to avoid hitting your chin.
Stop if you notice sharp shoulder pain or tingling in the hands.
checks: Check the handle is securely clipped and the cable is in good condition.
Set the thigh pad firmly and confirm the selector pin is fully in.
reduceLoad: Lower the weight if your lean increases rep to rep, your hips lift, or the handle stops short of your chest.

programming.rehab: Often well tolerated after elbow or shoulder irritation because of the neutral wrist; keep loads light and pain-free and follow your physiotherapist's guidance.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week, 48 h between hard sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Pick a weight you can pull for about 12 controlled reps with two or three in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: Reps should slow near the end of the set without increased lean or shortened range.
programming.progression: Double progression: reach the top of the range on all sets, then add 2.5-5 kg.
programming.increase: Increase load once every set hits the top of the rep range with full range.
programming.maintain: Keep the load while reps are improving; drop it if the lean or range starts to change.

name: Underhand lat pulldown
musclesText: Primary: latissimus dorsi, biceps brachii. Secondary: brachialis, lower trapezius, rhomboids, forearm flexors.

steps.start: Sit at the pulldown with thighs under the pads, holding a straight bar overhead with palms facing you.
steps.setup: Attach a straight bar to the high pulley, lock the thigh pad down firmly and select the weight.
steps.feet: Feet flat and hip-width apart, knees around 90 degrees.
steps.grip: Take an underhand (supinated) grip about shoulder-width apart, thumbs wrapped, wrists straight.
steps.posture: Sit tall with chest up and a slight lean back of 10-20 degrees.
steps.brace: Brace your abdominals so your torso does not swing back as you pull.
steps.initiate: Set your shoulder blades down, then pull the elbows down and slightly forward of your torso.
steps.concentric: Pull the bar to your upper chest, keeping elbows close to your sides and finishing with them just behind your torso.
steps.breathing: Inhale with the arms extended, exhale as the bar comes down or on the return.
steps.eccentric: Let the bar rise under control until the elbows are straight and you feel a full stretch.
steps.rom: Full arm extension to bar at upper chest.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: two seconds as the bar rises, no pause, one second down, one-second squeeze at the chest.
steps.finish: Finish with the bar at your upper chest, elbows tucked and shoulders down.
steps.exit: Let the bar return to full extension, stand while holding it, and lower the stack gently before releasing.

mistakes.m: Turning it into a biceps curl
mistakes.fix: Pull with the elbows and keep the forearms vertical.

mistakes.m: Grip too narrow, causing wrist or elbow strain
mistakes.fix: Keep hands about shoulder width with wrists straight.

mistakes.m: Excessive lean back
mistakes.fix: Keep the torso angle fixed and lighten the load.

mistakes.m: Half reps at the top
mistakes.fix: Straighten your arms completely each rep.

safety: The supinated grip loads the biceps and inner elbow; build up volume gradually.
Stop if you feel sharp elbow or shoulder pain or tingling in the fingers.
checks: Check the bar clip is closed and the cable is intact.
Set the thigh pad firmly and check the selector pin.
reduceLoad: Reduce weight if you start leaning back heavily, the bar fails to reach your chest, or your elbows ache during the set.

programming.frequency: 1-3 times per week, 48 h between hard pulling sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Choose a weight you can pull for about 12 reps with two or three left in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: The last reps should be slow but full range with a steady torso angle.
programming.progression: Double progression: hit the top of the range on all sets, then add 2.5-5 kg.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets reach the top of the range with clean reps.
programming.maintain: Hold the load while reps are rising; reduce if elbow discomfort appears.

name: Single-arm lat pulldown
musclesText: Primary: latissimus dorsi, teres major. Secondary: lower trapezius, rhomboids, biceps brachii, brachialis, internal and external obliques.

steps.start: Sit or half-kneel facing a high pulley, holding a single D-handle overhead with one arm straight.
steps.setup: Clip a D-handle to the high pulley. If seated, use a pulldown station with the thigh pad set firmly; if half-kneeling, set the pulley at its highest point and kneel about an arm's length away.
steps.feet: Seated: feet flat, hip-width. Half-kneeling: the knee on the working side down on a mat, the other foot forward with knee at 90 degrees.
steps.grip: Hold the D-handle with a neutral or slightly pronated grip, thumb wrapped; the palm turns to face forward or in as you pull.
steps.posture: Sit or kneel tall with ribs down and a small lean towards the working side so the cable lines up with your lat.
steps.brace: Brace your trunk and avoid twisting towards the cable as you pull.
steps.initiate: Let the shoulder rise slightly into the stretch, then draw the shoulder blade down before bending the elbow.
steps.concentric: Pull your elbow down and in towards your hip until your hand reaches about shoulder level beside your chest.
steps.breathing: Breathe in at the top, exhale as you pull down.
steps.eccentric: Return slowly until the arm is straight and you feel a deep lat stretch.
steps.rom: From full overhead reach to elbow at your side and hand by your shoulder.
steps.tempo: 3-0-1-1: three seconds as the handle rises, no pause, one second down, one-second squeeze at the bottom.
steps.finish: Finish with the elbow tucked to your side and the shoulder away from the ear.
steps.exit: Let the handle rise to full extension and guide it back to the stack before standing or switching sides.

cues: Do not twist to the cable

mistakes.m: Rotating the torso to move the weight
mistakes.fix: Brace and keep your chest facing the cable; reduce the weight.

mistakes.m: Curling with the biceps
mistakes.fix: Lead with the elbow and keep the forearm in line with the cable.

mistakes.m: Shrugging at the bottom
mistakes.fix: Pull the shoulder down away from the ear before and during the pull.

mistakes.m: Stopping short of the stretch
mistakes.fix: Let the arm extend fully overhead on each rep.

safety: Use a mat under the knee when half-kneeling.
Keep the free hand on your thigh or the pad for stability.
Stop if you feel sharp shoulder pain or pins and needles in the hand.
checks: Check the pulley is locked at the top and the D-handle clip is closed.
Make sure you are far enough from the stack that the weight does not touch down at the top of each rep.
reduceLoad: Reduce the weight if you have to twist your torso, the stack bottoms out at the top, or you cannot finish with the elbow by your side.

programming.rehab: Light, slow single-arm pulls let you work each side through a comfortable range; useful in shoulder rehabilitation under a physiotherapist's guidance.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week, 48 h between hard back sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Start with a weight you can pull for 12-15 reps per side with two or three in reserve; begin with your weaker side.
programming.judgeLoad: The final reps should slow without twisting or shortening the range.
programming.progression: Double progression per side: reach the top of the range, then add the smallest plate or pin increment.
programming.increase: Increase when both sides complete all sets at the top of the range.
programming.maintain: Keep the weight while reps are increasing; match the weaker side rather than progressing ahead of it.

name: Barbell bent-over row
musclesText: Primary: latissimus dorsi, middle trapezius, rhomboids. Secondary: posterior deltoid, biceps brachii, brachialis, erector spinae, hamstrings, forearm flexors.

steps.start: Stand holding the barbell at arm's length in front of your thighs, then hinge forward until your torso is about 30-45 degrees from horizontal.
steps.setup: Load the bar with collars on and lift it from the floor with a deadlift, or take it from a rack set at mid-thigh height.
steps.feet: Feet hip-width apart, toes forward or slightly out, knees softly bent.
steps.grip: Overhand grip just outside shoulder width, thumbs wrapped; straps are optional when grip limits the set.
steps.posture: Hinge at the hips with a flat back from pelvis to head, neck neutral, chest proud.
steps.brace: Take a big breath into your belly and brace hard to keep your torso angle and spine still.
steps.initiate: Start by pulling the shoulder blades back slightly, then drive the elbows up and back.
steps.concentric: Row the bar to your lower ribs or upper abdomen, keeping the elbows at roughly 45 degrees from your torso.
steps.breathing: Breathe in and brace before each rep, hold through the pull, and exhale at the top or as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower the bar under control to straight arms, keeping the same torso angle.
steps.rom: From straight arms with shoulder blades slightly spread, to bar touching the lower ribs.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: two seconds down, no pause, one second up, one-second hold at the ribs.
steps.finish: Finish each rep with the bar at your lower ribs and shoulder blades squeezed together.
steps.exit: After the final rep, lower the bar to your thighs, stand up with a neutral spine, then rerack or deadlift it back to the floor.

mistakes.m: Standing up more each rep to use momentum
mistakes.fix: Fix the torso angle and reduce the load.

mistakes.m: Rounding the lower back
mistakes.fix: Brace harder, reduce the load and hinge from the hips.

mistakes.m: Pulling to the chest with flared elbows
mistakes.fix: Pull to the lower ribs with elbows at around 45 degrees.

mistakes.m: Jerking the bar up with the legs
mistakes.fix: Keep knees still and start each rep with the back.

mistakes.m: Neck cranked up to look at the mirror
mistakes.fix: Keep the neck in line with the spine, eyes on the floor ahead.

safety: The bent-over position loads the lower back isometrically; if your back tires and starts to round, end the set.
Avoid this lift on days your lower back is already fatigued from heavy deadlifts or squats.
Stop if you feel sharp back pain or pain or tingling down a leg.
checks: Put collars on both ends of the bar.
Check you have room in front and behind and a clear floor.
If taking the bar from a rack, set the hooks at mid-thigh height.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if your torso rises above about 45 degrees, your lower back rounds, or the bar no longer reaches your ribs.

programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week, at least 48-72 h after heavy hinge work.
programming.initialLoad: Start with a load you can row for 10 clean reps with two or three in reserve, typically well under your deadlift.
programming.judgeLoad: The torso should stay still and the bar touch the ribs on every rep; any rise or loss of contact means too heavy.
programming.progression: Double progression: reach the top of the range on all sets, then add 2.5 kg.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets hit the top of the range with a constant torso angle.
programming.maintain: Keep the load the same while reps are climbing; reduce if your lower back fatigues before your upper back.

name: Pendlay row
musclesText: Primary: middle trapezius, rhomboids, latissimus dorsi. Secondary: posterior deltoid, biceps brachii, brachialis, erector spinae, hamstrings, forearm flexors.

steps.start: Stand over a loaded barbell on the floor and hinge until your torso is roughly parallel to the floor, arms hanging straight to the bar.
steps.setup: Load the bar with standard-diameter (45 cm) plates so it sits at the right height, and fit collars.
steps.feet: Feet hip-width apart with the bar over the middle of your feet, knees bent enough to reach the bar with a flat back.
steps.grip: Overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder width, thumbs wrapped.
steps.posture: Torso parallel or nearly parallel to the floor, flat back, hips around shoulder height or slightly lower, neck neutral.
steps.brace: Breathe in and brace hard before every rep, because each rep starts from a dead stop.
steps.initiate: Pull the slack out of the bar, then explosively drive your elbows up and back without lifting your torso.
steps.concentric: Row the bar quickly to your lower chest or upper abdomen, touching the body.
steps.breathing: Reset your breath and brace on the floor between every rep; exhale after the bar returns.
steps.eccentric: Lower the bar under control back to the floor and let it come to a complete stop.
steps.rom: From the floor (dead stop) to the bar touching your torso.
steps.tempo: X-1-X-0: explosive up, controlled down, one-second dead stop on the floor before the next rep.
steps.finish: Finish each rep with the bar settled on the floor and your back still flat.
steps.exit: After the last rep, leave the bar on the floor, then stand up by pushing through your legs with a neutral spine.

cues: Back flat, parallel to the floor

mistakes.m: Torso lifting up to finish reps
mistakes.fix: Keep your back parallel and lower the weight.

mistakes.m: Bouncing the bar off the floor
mistakes.fix: Let the bar settle completely and reset each rep.

mistakes.m: Rounding the back to reach the bar
mistakes.fix: Bend the knees more and hinge from the hips; use standard-size plates.

mistakes.m: Pulling the bar to the belly button with bent wrists
mistakes.fix: Pull to the lower chest with straight wrists.

safety: The parallel torso position is demanding on the lower back; reduce load or switch to a chest-supported row if you cannot keep it flat.
Do not attempt with an acute back injury.
Stop if you get sharp back pain or pain radiating into a leg.
checks: Use full-size plates or blocks so the bar starts at a reachable height.
Fit collars and check the floor is clear and non-slip.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if your torso rises above parallel, the bar fails to touch your torso, or your lower back starts to round.

programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week, separated from heavy deadlifts by at least 48 h.
programming.initialLoad: Start with a load you could row explosively for about 8 reps with two or three in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: Each rep should be fast and touch your torso; once bar speed drops sharply or the torso lifts, stop the set.
programming.progression: Double progression: work up to the top of the range, then add 2.5 kg.
programming.increase: Increase load when all sets reach the top of the range with fast, clean reps.
programming.maintain: Keep the same load while bar speed or reps are improving; reduce it if the back angle changes.

name: Seated cable row
musclesText: Primary: middle trapezius, rhomboids, latissimus dorsi. Secondary: posterior deltoid, biceps brachii, brachialis, forearm flexors, erector spinae.

steps.start: Sit on the bench of a low cable row station, knees slightly bent, holding a close-grip V-handle with arms extended.
steps.setup: Attach a close-grip V handle to the low pulley and select the weight; sit so you can reach the handle with a straight back.
steps.feet: Place your feet on the foot platform, hip-width apart, knees softly bent and not locked.
steps.grip: Hold the V-handle with palms facing each other, thumbs wrapped, wrists straight.
steps.posture: Sit upright with the torso vertical or leaning back no more than about 10 degrees, chest up, spine neutral.
steps.brace: Brace your abdominals so the torso does not rock forward and back to move the weight.
steps.initiate: Start by letting the shoulder blades slide back, then drive the elbows back.
steps.concentric: Pull the handle to your upper abdomen, keeping elbows close to your sides, until the handle touches or nearly touches your torso.
steps.breathing: Breathe in as you reach forward, exhale as you pull the handle in.
steps.eccentric: Let the arms straighten and the shoulder blades move forward under control, with a slight forward lean from the hips if you like but no rounding of the lower back.
steps.rom: From arms fully extended with shoulder blades protracted, to handle at the upper abdomen with shoulder blades squeezed.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: two seconds out, no pause, one second in, one-second squeeze at the torso.
steps.finish: Finish with the handle at your stomach, chest tall and elbows just behind the torso.
steps.exit: Return the handle slowly to full extension, bend your knees, and lower the weight to the stack before letting go.

mistakes.m: Swinging the torso back to move the weight
mistakes.fix: Fix your torso near vertical and reduce the weight.

mistakes.m: Rounding the lower back on the return
mistakes.fix: Hinge only slightly from the hips and keep the spine neutral.

mistakes.m: Shrugging the shoulders up
mistakes.fix: Keep shoulders down away from the ears as you pull.

mistakes.m: Locking the knees straight
mistakes.fix: Keep a soft bend to protect the knees and lower back.

safety: Do not jerk the weight off the stack from a rounded position at the start of the set.
Stop if you feel sharp lower back pain or tingling in the hands.
checks: Check the V-handle clip is closed and the cable is intact.
Confirm the selector pin is fully inserted and the foot platform is dry.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if you have to lean back beyond about 10 degrees, your lower back rounds when reaching forward, or the handle stops short of your torso.

programming.rehab: Light cable rows through a pain-free range are a common rehab staple for posture and shoulder blade control; follow your physiotherapist's guidance.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week, 48 h between hard back sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Pick a weight you can row for about 12 reps with two or three in reserve while keeping your torso still.
programming.judgeLoad: The final reps should be slow but reach the torso without rocking.
programming.progression: Double progression: hit the top of the rep range on all sets, then add one stack plate (2.5-5 kg).
programming.increase: Increase once all sets reach the top of the range with a stable torso.
programming.maintain: Keep the load the same while reps are improving; reduce if you start rocking.

name: Chest-supported row
musclesText: Primary: middle and lower trapezius, rhomboids, latissimus dorsi. Secondary: posterior deltoid, biceps brachii, brachialis, forearm flexors.

steps.start: Lie face-down on an incline bench with your chest on the pad and a dumbbell in each hand hanging straight below your shoulders.
steps.setup: Set an adjustable bench to about 30-45 degrees and place two dumbbells by the front feet of the bench; a plate-loaded chest-pad row works the same way.
steps.feet: Stand on the balls of your feet or plant them flat behind the bench, legs straight or slightly bent, so your chest stays pressed to the pad.
steps.grip: Hold the dumbbells with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) or overhand grip for more upper-back emphasis, thumbs wrapped.
steps.posture: Keep your chest on the pad, the top of your sternum near the top edge, neck neutral and chin slightly tucked.
steps.brace: Brace lightly and keep your chest in contact with the pad rather than lifting off it.
steps.initiate: Start by drawing your shoulder blades back, then drive your elbows up.
steps.concentric: Row the dumbbells up towards your lower ribs until your elbows are just behind your torso.
steps.breathing: Breathe out as you row and in as you lower; the pad can restrict breathing, so keep breaths steady.
steps.eccentric: Lower the dumbbells under control until your arms are straight and shoulder blades spread.
steps.rom: From arms hanging straight to elbows just behind the torso.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: two seconds down, no pause, one second up, one-second squeeze at the top.
steps.finish: Finish with your shoulder blades squeezed together and chest still on the pad.
steps.exit: Lower the dumbbells to straight arms, set them on the floor beside the bench, then push yourself up off the pad.

mistakes.m: Lifting the chest off the pad to heave the weight
mistakes.fix: Keep the sternum on the pad and use lighter dumbbells.

mistakes.m: Craning the neck up
mistakes.fix: Look down at the floor just ahead of the bench.

mistakes.m: Shrugging the shoulders
mistakes.fix: Keep shoulders down and pull with the elbows.

mistakes.m: Partial reps
mistakes.fix: Let the arms fully straighten each rep.

safety: The pad removes most lower back load, making this a good option when your back is fatigued.
Set the dumbbells down rather than dropping them from height.
Stop if you feel sharp shoulder pain or tingling in the hands.
checks: Check the bench pin is locked at the chosen angle.
Place the dumbbells where you can reach them from the bench without twisting.
reduceLoad: Reduce the weight if your chest leaves the pad, your elbows cannot get beside your torso, or you start shrugging.

programming.rehab: A back-friendly row for people who cannot tolerate bent-over positions; use light loads and slow reps, guided by a physiotherapist after injury.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week, 48 h between hard back sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Start with dumbbells you can row for 12 reps with two or three in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: Reps should slow but stay full range with your chest on the pad.
programming.progression: Double progression: reach the top of the range on all sets, then go up 2 kg per hand.
programming.increase: Increase once all sets hit the top of the range cleanly.
programming.maintain: Hold the load while reps climb; reduce if your chest starts to lift.

name: Dumbbell single-arm row
musclesText: Primary: latissimus dorsi, middle trapezius, rhomboids. Secondary: posterior deltoid, biceps brachii, brachialis, forearm flexors, obliques.

steps.start: Kneel with one knee and the same-side hand on a flat bench, holding a dumbbell in the other hand with the arm hanging straight.
steps.setup: Use a flat bench and place the dumbbell on the floor beside it on your working side.
steps.feet: Put one knee on the bench under your hip and the other foot flat on the floor out to the side, knee slightly bent.
steps.grip: Support hand flat on the bench under your shoulder; hold the dumbbell with a neutral grip, thumb wrapped.
steps.posture: Keep your back flat and roughly parallel to the floor, shoulders level and neck neutral.
steps.brace: Brace your trunk to stop your torso twisting as the dumbbell rises.
steps.initiate: Start by drawing the shoulder blade back, then drive the elbow up and back.
steps.concentric: Row the dumbbell towards your hip, elbow close to your side, until the elbow is just above the torso.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you row, inhale as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower the dumbbell under control until your arm is straight and you feel a stretch in the lat.
steps.rom: From a straight arm with the shoulder blade spread, to elbow just past the torso.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: two seconds down, no pause, one second up, one-second squeeze.
steps.finish: Finish with the dumbbell at your hip and shoulders still level.
steps.exit: Lower the dumbbell to straight arm, set it on the floor, then switch sides or stand up by pushing off the bench.

mistakes.m: Rotating the torso to swing the weight up
mistakes.fix: Brace, keep shoulders level and use a lighter dumbbell.

mistakes.m: Pulling straight up to the chest
mistakes.fix: Pull in an arc towards your hip.

mistakes.m: Rounding the back
mistakes.fix: Keep the support arm straight and back flat.

mistakes.m: Cutting the bottom short
mistakes.fix: Let the arm straighten fully each rep.

safety: The bench support reduces lower back strain; keep the supporting hand directly under the shoulder.
Lift the dumbbell from the floor with a flat back.
Stop if you feel sharp shoulder or back pain or tingling into the hand.
checks: Check the bench is stable and will not tip when you lean on it.
Use a dumbbell with tight, secure heads.
reduceLoad: Reduce the weight if your torso twists, you cannot pause at the top, or the dumbbell no longer reaches your hip.

programming.rehab: Light, supported single-arm rows are useful in shoulder and upper back rehab; keep it pain-free and follow your physiotherapist's guidance.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week, 48 h between hard back sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Choose a dumbbell you can row for 12 reps per side with two or three in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: Reps should slow without twisting the torso or shortening range.
programming.progression: Double progression per side: top of the range on all sets, then add 2 kg.
programming.increase: Increase when both sides complete all sets at the top of the range.
programming.maintain: Keep the load while reps improve; reduce if twisting creeps in.

name: Seal row
musclesText: Primary: middle and lower trapezius, rhomboids, latissimus dorsi. Secondary: posterior deltoid, biceps brachii, brachialis, forearm flexors.

steps.start: Lie face-down on a high flat bench with your chest near the top edge and a barbell (or two dumbbells) hanging below you at arm's length.
steps.setup: Use a dedicated seal row bench or raise a flat bench on boxes or plates so your arms hang straight without the weight touching the floor. Place the loaded barbell underneath.
steps.feet: Lie with your legs straight along the bench and feet resting or hooked on the bench end.
steps.grip: Reach down and take an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder width on the barbell, or a neutral grip on dumbbells.
steps.posture: Chest on the pad, head neutral or slightly over the edge, spine long.
steps.brace: Brace lightly and press your hips into the bench so your body does not lift.
steps.initiate: Start by pulling the shoulder blades together, then drive the elbows up.
steps.concentric: Row the bar until it touches the underside of the bench or your elbows pass the torso.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you row, inhale as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower the weight slowly until your arms are straight and the shoulder blades spread apart.
steps.rom: From straight arms to the bar touching the bench underside.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: two seconds down, no pause, one second up, one-second squeeze.
steps.finish: Finish each rep with the bar at the bench and shoulder blades pinched.
steps.exit: Lower the bar to arm's length, set it onto the floor or blocks, then climb off the bench carefully.

mistakes.m: Lifting the chest or hips off the bench
mistakes.fix: Keep body pressed down and use less weight.

mistakes.m: Bench too low so plates hit the floor
mistakes.fix: Raise the bench so you get a full stretch without touchdown.

mistakes.m: Yanking from the bottom
mistakes.fix: Start with the shoulder blades and pull smoothly.

safety: Make sure the bench is stable on any boxes or plates used to raise it.
Get on and off carefully; have the weight start on the floor or blocks you can reach.
Stop if you feel sharp shoulder pain or numbness in the hands.
checks: Check the raised bench is level and cannot slide.
Fit collars on the barbell and make sure you can reach it from the bench.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if your chest lifts off the pad, the bar no longer reaches the bench, or you lose the pause at the top.

programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week, 48 h between hard back sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Start with a load you can row for 10-12 reps with two or three in reserve; expect it to be lighter than your bent-over row.
programming.judgeLoad: Reps should still reach the bench and pause briefly near the end of the set.
programming.progression: Double progression: top of the range on all sets, then add 2.5 kg.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets reach the top of the rep range with full contact.
programming.maintain: Keep the load while reps are improving; reduce if you lose contact with the bench.

name: T-bar row
musclesText: Primary: latissimus dorsi, middle trapezius, rhomboids. Secondary: posterior deltoid, biceps brachii, brachialis, erector spinae, hamstrings, forearm flexors.

steps.start: Straddle the loaded end of a landmine or T-bar, hinge forward and hold the close neutral handle under the bar with arms straight.
steps.setup: Set one end of a barbell in a landmine or corner, load plates on the free end, fit a collar and hook a close-grip V-handle under the bar just below the plates.
steps.feet: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart either side of the bar, knees bent, bar between your feet.
steps.grip: Hold the V-handle with palms facing each other, thumbs wrapped, wrists straight.
steps.posture: Hinge until your torso is about 30-45 degrees from horizontal, back flat, neck neutral.
steps.brace: Breathe in and brace firmly to hold your torso angle and protect the lower back.
steps.initiate: Start by pulling the shoulder blades back, then drive the elbows up past your sides.
steps.concentric: Row the plates towards your chest until the handle reaches your lower chest or upper abdomen.
steps.breathing: Brace before each rep, exhale near the top or on the way down.
steps.eccentric: Lower the handle slowly to straight arms, keeping the torso still.
steps.rom: From straight arms to handle at the lower chest; use smaller plates if larger ones hit your chest early.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: two seconds down, no pause, one second up, one-second squeeze.
steps.finish: Finish with the elbows behind your torso and shoulder blades squeezed together.
steps.exit: Lower the bar until the plates rest on the floor, release the handle and stand up with a neutral spine.

mistakes.m: Standing up as you row
mistakes.fix: Keep the torso angle fixed and reduce load.

mistakes.m: Using large plates that cut range short
mistakes.fix: Use smaller-diameter plates (e.g. 10-15 kg) to allow full range.

mistakes.m: Rounding the lower back
mistakes.fix: Bend the knees more and brace.

mistakes.m: Hips shooting back and forth
mistakes.fix: Keep the hips still and move only the arms.

safety: This is a bent-over lift; stop when your lower back fatigues before your upper back.
Keep the free end of the barbell secure in the landmine so it cannot slide out.
Stop if you feel sharp back pain or pain spreading into a leg.
checks: Check the landmine sleeve or corner is secure and the bar end will not slip.
Fit a collar on the plates and check the V-handle sits securely under the bar.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if your torso rises, your back rounds, or the handle stops short of your chest.

programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week, 48-72 h after heavy hinge work.
programming.initialLoad: Start with a load you can row for 10 reps with two or three in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: Each rep should reach your chest with a fixed torso; heaving or rising means too heavy.
programming.progression: Double progression: reach the top of the range, then add 2.5 kg.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets hit the top of the range with a steady torso.
programming.maintain: Keep the load while reps are improving; reduce if your lower back fatigues first.

name: Machine row
musclesText: Primary: middle trapezius, rhomboids, latissimus dorsi. Secondary: posterior deltoid, biceps brachii, brachialis, forearm flexors.

steps.start: Sit on the row machine with your chest against the pad and arms reaching forward to the handles.
steps.setup: Adjust the seat so the handles line up with your mid-chest, and set the chest pad so you can just reach the handles with straight arms. Select the weight or load plates evenly.
steps.feet: Feet flat on the floor or the foot rests, about hip-width apart.
steps.grip: Use the neutral handles for a lats-focused pull or the horizontal handles for more upper-back focus, thumbs wrapped.
steps.posture: Sit tall with your chest pressed against the pad, spine neutral and head in line.
steps.brace: Brace lightly and keep your chest in contact with the pad throughout.
steps.initiate: Draw your shoulder blades back first, then drive your elbows back.
steps.concentric: Pull the handles until your elbows are just behind your torso.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you pull, inhale as you return.
steps.eccentric: Return the handles slowly until your arms are straight and the shoulder blades are spread.
steps.rom: From arms straight with a stretch through the upper back to elbows just behind the torso.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: two seconds forward, no pause, one second back, one-second squeeze.
steps.finish: Finish with the shoulder blades squeezed and chest still on the pad.
steps.exit: Return the handles fully so the weight rests on the stack or the stops, then release and stand.

mistakes.m: Leaning back off the pad
mistakes.fix: Keep your chest pressed in and reduce the load.

mistakes.m: Seat too low, pulling to the neck
mistakes.fix: Raise the seat so handles meet mid-chest.

mistakes.m: Shrugging the shoulders
mistakes.fix: Pull with the elbows and keep shoulders down.

mistakes.m: Letting the stack crash between reps
mistakes.fix: Control the return and keep light tension.

safety: Set the start position so the stack does not slam at the stretch.
Stop if you feel sharp shoulder pain or tingling in the hands.
checks: Check the seat and chest pad pins are fully locked.
On plate-loaded machines, load both sides evenly and fit collars where provided.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if your chest leaves the pad, your elbows fail to reach your torso, or you start shrugging.

programming.rehab: Supported machine rows are well suited to rebuilding upper back strength with light, pain-free loads; follow your physiotherapist's guidance after injury.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week, 48 h between hard back sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Choose a weight you can row for 12 reps with two or three in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: Reps should slow towards the end but keep full range and chest contact.
programming.progression: Double progression: hit the top of the range, then add one stack plate or 2.5-5 kg.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets reach the top of the range with clean form.
programming.maintain: Keep the load while reps are improving; reduce if range shortens.

name: Straight-arm pulldown
musclesText: Primary: latissimus dorsi, teres major. Secondary: long head of triceps brachii, posterior deltoid, rectus abdominis.

steps.start: Stand facing a high pulley, hinge slightly forward and hold a straight bar or rope at about eye level with arms nearly straight.
steps.setup: Attach a straight bar or rope to the high pulley and set a light to moderate weight.
steps.feet: Stand a step or two back from the stack with feet hip-width apart, knees softly bent.
steps.grip: Overhand grip on a straight bar about shoulder width, or hold the rope ends with palms facing each other; keep a slight fixed bend in the elbows.
steps.posture: Hinge forward 20-30 degrees at the hips with a neutral back and ribs down.
steps.brace: Brace your abdominals so your torso does not rock as the arms move.
steps.initiate: Start by setting the shoulders down, then sweep the arms down from the shoulder.
steps.concentric: Pull the bar or rope in an arc down towards your thighs, keeping the elbow angle fixed, until your hands reach your upper thighs.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you pull down, inhale as the arms rise.
steps.eccentric: Let the arms rise slowly in the same arc until they are about level with your head and you feel a lat stretch.
steps.rom: From arms roughly overhead or at eye level to hands at the thighs.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: two seconds up, no pause, one second down, one-second squeeze at the thighs.
steps.finish: Finish with the bar or rope at your thighs and lats squeezed.
steps.exit: Let the arms rise to the start, step forward to let the stack settle, then release.

mistakes.m: Bending the elbows into a pushdown
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbow angle fixed and think of pushing with the pinkies.

mistakes.m: Hinging the hips to help the weight down
mistakes.fix: Hold the torso angle and reduce load.

mistakes.m: Shrugging at the top
mistakes.fix: Set shoulders down before each rep.

mistakes.m: Weight too heavy
mistakes.fix: Use a load that lets you feel the lats, usually much lighter than a pulldown.

safety: Keep the elbows softly bent rather than locked to protect them.
Stop if you feel sharp shoulder pain in the overhead position.
checks: Check the attachment is secure and the cable is intact.
Stand far enough back that the stack does not bottom out at the top.
reduceLoad: Reduce the weight if your elbows bend more as you pull, your torso rocks, or you cannot reach your thighs.

programming.rehab: Light, slow reps can help retrain lat activation after shoulder issues once a physiotherapist approves overhead range.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week, often as a warm-up or finisher.
programming.initialLoad: Start light: a weight you can move for 15 controlled reps without the elbows bending.
programming.judgeLoad: You should feel the lats working and keep a fixed elbow angle; triceps or shoulder dominance means too heavy.
programming.progression: Double progression: reach the top of the range, then add the smallest increment.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets reach the top of the range with fixed elbows.
programming.maintain: Keep the load while reps are improving; reduce if technique changes.

name: Face pull
musclesText: Primary: posterior deltoid, middle and lower trapezius, rhomboids. Secondary: infraspinatus, teres minor, upper trapezius.

steps.start: Stand facing a cable stack holding the rope attachment with arms extended in front of you at upper-chest to face height.
steps.setup: Attach a rope to a pulley set at upper-chest to face height and choose a light weight.
steps.feet: Stand one or two steps back with feet hip-width apart, or in a split stance for extra stability, knees soft.
steps.grip: Hold the rope ends with an overhand grip (thumbs towards you) or neutral grip, thumbs wrapped, hands close to the knots.
steps.posture: Stand tall with ribs down and a neutral spine; avoid leaning back.
steps.brace: Brace your abdominals lightly so your torso stays still.
steps.initiate: Start by drawing the shoulder blades back, then pull the rope towards your face, leading with the elbows.
steps.concentric: Pull the rope towards your eyes or forehead, separating the ends as you go, elbows high and wide, until your hands are beside your ears and your knuckles point up and back.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you pull, inhale as you return.
steps.eccentric: Let the rope travel slowly back to straight arms, allowing the shoulder blades to move forward.
steps.rom: From arms straight in front to hands beside the ears with upper arms roughly in line with the shoulders.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: two seconds forward, no pause, one second in, one-second hold at the face.
steps.finish: Finish with the rope split either side of your face, elbows high and shoulder blades squeezed.
steps.exit: Return the rope to straight arms, step forward to let the stack rest, then release.

mistakes.m: Leaning back and using bodyweight
mistakes.fix: Stand tall and lighten the load.

mistakes.m: Elbows dropping into a low row
mistakes.fix: Keep elbows at or just below shoulder height.

mistakes.m: Pulling to the chest or neck
mistakes.fix: Aim for the eyes or forehead.

mistakes.m: Shrugging the shoulders up
mistakes.fix: Keep shoulders down while pulling the shoulder blades back.

safety: Use moderate loads; heavy weight turns this into a row and loses the rear delt and rotator cuff focus.
Stop if you feel a pinching pain at the front or top of the shoulder.
checks: Set the pulley at upper-chest to face height and lock it in place.
Check the rope is securely clipped and its stopper knots are intact.
reduceLoad: Reduce the weight if you lean back, your elbows drop, or you cannot hold the finish position for a second.

programming.rehab: Light face pulls are a common shoulder-health and posture exercise; use a pain-free range and consult a physiotherapist for an existing shoulder injury.
programming.frequency: 2-4 times per week; recovers quickly.
programming.initialLoad: Start with a weight you can pull for 15-20 controlled reps while holding the finish position.
programming.judgeLoad: You should feel the rear shoulders and upper back; leaning or arms-only pulling means too heavy.
programming.progression: Double progression: add reps to the top of the range, then add the smallest weight increment.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets hit the top of the range with a one-second pause.
programming.maintain: Keep the load while reps are improving; reduce if posture slips.

name: Back extension
musclesText: Primary: erector spinae, gluteus maximus. Secondary: hamstrings (biceps femoris, semitendinosus, semimembranosus).

steps.start: Position yourself on a 45-degree hyperextension bench with your thighs on the pad and heels locked under the foot rollers, body in a straight line.
steps.setup: Adjust the hip pad so its top edge sits just below your hip crease, letting you bend freely at the hips.
steps.feet: Feet flat on the platform, heels pressed against the rollers, about hip-width apart.
steps.grip: Cross your arms over your chest, or hold a plate against your chest once bodyweight is easy.
steps.posture: Keep a neutral spine from head to pelvis, chin slightly tucked.
steps.brace: Brace your abdominals and squeeze your glutes to keep the spine neutral.
steps.initiate: Start the descent by hinging at the hips, keeping the back flat.
steps.concentric: Drive your hips into the pad and squeeze your glutes to raise your torso until your body forms a straight line with your legs.
steps.breathing: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you rise.
steps.eccentric: Hinge forward under control until your torso is close to vertical or you feel a strong hamstring stretch without the back rounding.
steps.rom: From the straight-line position down to the deepest point you can reach with a neutral spine; do not arch past straight at the top.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: two seconds down, no pause, one second up, one-second hold at the top.
steps.finish: Finish in a straight line from head to heels with glutes squeezed.
steps.exit: After the last rep, hold the top briefly, then carefully step down off the platform one foot at a time.

mistakes.m: Hyperextending at the top
mistakes.fix: Stop when your body forms a straight line.

mistakes.m: Pad too high, blocking the hinge
mistakes.fix: Set the pad below the hip crease.

mistakes.m: Swinging up with momentum
mistakes.fix: Slow the rep and hold the top for a second.

mistakes.m: Rounding the back at the bottom
mistakes.fix: Limit depth to the point you can stay neutral.

safety: Avoid arching the lower back past neutral at the top.
If you have a current back injury, see a physiotherapist before loading this movement.
Stop if you feel sharp back pain or pain or tingling down a leg.
checks: Set the pad height and check the pin is locked.
Make sure your heels are secure under the rollers before you lean forward.
reduceLoad: Use bodyweight only or reduce the plate if you cannot keep your back flat at the bottom, you start swinging, or you feel strain in the lower back rather than hip and back muscle effort.

programming.rehab: Slow bodyweight back extensions through a comfortable range are often part of back rehabilitation; follow your physiotherapist's guidance.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week, 48 h between sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Start with bodyweight; add a small plate held to the chest only once you can do 15-20 controlled reps.
programming.judgeLoad: Reps should stay smooth with a flat back; any rounding or lurching means too much load.
programming.progression: Rep progression: add reps to 20, then add a 2.5-5 kg plate.
programming.increase: Increase load when all sets reach the top of the range with a one-second pause.
programming.maintain: Keep the load while reps are improving; reduce if your lower back feels sore the next day.

name: Inverted row
musclesText: Primary: middle trapezius, rhomboids, latissimus dorsi. Secondary: posterior deltoid, biceps brachii, brachialis, rectus abdominis, gluteus maximus.

steps.start: Lie under a bar set at about hip height, hanging from it with straight arms and your body in a straight line from heels to head.
steps.setup: Set a barbell in a rack or a Smith machine bar at about hip height; lock the Smith bar or check the barbell sits securely in the hooks.
steps.feet: Heels on the floor, legs straight and together; bend the knees with feet flat to make it easier.
steps.grip: Overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder width, thumbs wrapped.
steps.posture: Keep your body rigid like a plank, from head to heels, neck neutral.
steps.brace: Squeeze your glutes and brace your abdominals so your hips do not sag.
steps.initiate: Start by pulling your shoulder blades back, then bend the elbows.
steps.concentric: Pull your chest up to the bar until it touches or nearly touches, elbows at about 45 degrees from your sides.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower under control until your arms are straight while keeping the body rigid.
steps.rom: From straight arms to chest at the bar.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: two seconds down, no pause, one second up, one-second hold at the bar.
steps.finish: Finish each rep with your chest at the bar and shoulder blades squeezed.
steps.exit: Lower to straight arms, put your bottom on the floor, then let go and stand up.

mistakes.m: Hips sagging
mistakes.fix: Squeeze glutes and brace; bend the knees if needed.

mistakes.m: Pulling the chin rather than the chest
mistakes.fix: Lead with the chest and keep the neck neutral.

mistakes.m: Partial reps
mistakes.fix: Reach straight arms at the bottom and chest at the bar.

mistakes.m: Shrugging up
mistakes.fix: Keep shoulders down away from the ears.

safety: Make sure the bar cannot roll out of the hooks or unlock.
Stop if you feel sharp shoulder or elbow pain.
checks: Check the rack hooks or Smith lock are secure before hanging.
Set the bar at a height where your back stays clear of the floor with straight arms.
reduceLoad: Raise the bar or bend your knees if your hips sag, your chest no longer reaches the bar, or you cannot control the lowering.

programming.rehab: A scalable bodyweight row; a higher bar makes it gentle for rebuilding pulling strength, following your physiotherapist's guidance.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week, 48 h between hard back sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Set the bar height so you can do about 10-12 reps with two or three in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: Reps should still touch the chest and keep the hips up; sagging means it is too hard.
programming.progression: Progress by lowering the bar a notch, straightening the legs, then elevating the feet or adding a weight vest.
programming.increase: Make it harder when all sets reach the top of the range with clean reps.
programming.maintain: Keep the same setting while reps are improving; raise the bar if form breaks.

name: Rack pull
musclesText: Primary: erector spinae, gluteus maximus, upper trapezius. Secondary: hamstrings, rhomboids, latissimus dorsi, forearm flexors.

steps.start: Stand at a barbell resting on safety pins or blocks set around knee height, feet under the bar.
steps.setup: Set the pins or blocks so the bar sits just below or at the knees, load it evenly and fit collars.
steps.feet: Feet hip-width apart, toes slightly out, bar over the middle of your feet and touching or close to your legs.
steps.grip: Double overhand grip just outside the legs; use a mixed grip or straps only when grip limits heavy sets.
steps.posture: Hinge with hips back, shins near vertical, back flat and chest up, shoulders slightly in front of the bar.
steps.brace: Take a big breath into your belly and brace hard before pulling, as for a deadlift.
steps.initiate: Pull the slack out of the bar until you feel tension, then push your feet into the floor and drive your hips forward.
steps.concentric: Stand up by extending hips and knees together, keeping the bar in contact with your thighs, until you are fully upright.
steps.breathing: Breathe and brace at the bottom, hold your breath through the pull, exhale at the top or after setting the bar down.
steps.eccentric: Lower the bar by pushing the hips back first, keeping it close to your thighs, until it rests on the pins or blocks.
steps.rom: From pins at about knee height to full hip lockout; do not lean back past upright.
steps.tempo: 1-1-X-1: one second down, one-second reset on the pins, powerful pull, one-second hold at lockout.
steps.finish: Finish standing tall with glutes squeezed, knees straight and shoulders neutral, not leaned back.
steps.exit: Lower the bar to the pins under control, release your grip and stand up; unload from both sides evenly.

mistakes.m: Leaning back at lockout
mistakes.fix: Stand tall with glutes squeezed and ribs down.

mistakes.m: Rounding the upper or lower back under heavy load
mistakes.fix: Reduce the load and brace before each pull.

mistakes.m: Bar drifting away from the legs
mistakes.fix: Keep the lats tight and drag the bar up the thighs.

mistakes.m: Bouncing off the pins
mistakes.fix: Let the bar settle and reset each rep.

mistakes.m: Pins set so high the lift barely moves
mistakes.fix: Start around knee height for a meaningful range.

safety: The shortened range lets you handle heavy loads; progress gradually as heavy pulls can overload the lower back.
Lowering onto steel pins can damage the bar and be noisy; set down with control or use blocks.
Stop if you feel sharp back pain or pain or tingling down a leg.
checks: Check the safety pins are fully inserted at equal height on both sides.
Fit collars and make sure plates are loaded evenly.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if your back rounds, you cannot lock out without leaning back, or bar speed slows sharply in the first reps.

programming.frequency: 1 time per week, at least 72 h from heavy deadlifts or squats.
programming.initialLoad: Start around your conventional deadlift working weight and build up in sets of 3-5 until the reps slow but stay clean.
programming.judgeLoad: Every rep should lock out without leaning back or rounding; aim to finish with one or two reps in reserve.
programming.progression: Double progression: reach the top of the range on all sets, then add 5 kg.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets hit the top of the range with a flat back and crisp lockout.
programming.maintain: Keep the load while reps improve; reduce if your lower back feels beaten up between sessions.

name: Seated dumbbell shoulder press
musclesText: Primary: anterior deltoid, lateral deltoid. Secondary: triceps brachii, upper and middle trapezius, serratus anterior.

steps.start: Sit tall on the bench with a dumbbell on each thigh, then kick them up one at a time with your knees so they arrive at shoulder height.
steps.setup: Set an adjustable bench to upright or one notch back from vertical (about 75-85 degrees) so your back is fully supported and your head clears the top of the pad.
steps.feet: Plant your feet flat, slightly wider than hip width, with knees bent to about 90 degrees so you feel stable on the seat.
steps.grip: Hold the handles with a full grip, palms facing forward or angled slightly in, with the dumbbells just outside and level with your shoulders and forearms vertical.
steps.posture: Keep your shoulder blades and the back of your head against the pad, ribs down and only the natural small arch in your lower back.
steps.brace: Take a breath into your belly and tighten your trunk as if bracing for a light push, so your ribs do not flare as the weights go up.
steps.initiate: Drive the dumbbells straight up by pushing through the palms, keeping forearms stacked under the handles.
steps.concentric: Press up and slightly inwards until the dumbbells are over your shoulders and almost touching, without letting them clash.
steps.breathing: Inhale and brace at the bottom, exhale steadily through the top half of the press.
steps.eccentric: Lower under control along the same path until the handles are around ear to chin height, elbows slightly in front of your torso.
steps.rom: Work from roughly ear or chin level to just short of locking the elbows; go only as deep as your shoulders allow without pain or the elbows drifting far behind you.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-0: two seconds down, no pause, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish each rep with the dumbbells stacked over the shoulders and the biceps near the ears, then start the next lowering phase.
steps.exit: After the last rep lower the dumbbells to shoulder height, bring them to your thighs, then sit forward and set them on the floor one at a time rather than dropping them out wide.

cues: Back flat on the pad, ribs down
Elbows a little in front of the body
Do not clash the bells at the top

mistakes.m: Arching the lower back off the pad to move more weight.
mistakes.fix: Bring the bench one notch more upright, reduce the load and keep your ribs pulled down.

mistakes.m: Flaring the elbows directly out to the sides behind the body.
mistakes.fix: Angle the elbows about 30 degrees forward so the upper arms sit slightly in front of the torso.

mistakes.m: Cutting the range short at the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Lower until the handles reach around ear level each rep and choose a load you can control there.

mistakes.m: Dropping the dumbbells out to the sides at the end of the set.
mistakes.fix: Bring them back to the thighs under control before putting them down.

safety: Use the knee kick to get heavy dumbbells into position rather than curling them up with your arms.
Stop if you feel a pinching pain at the front or top of the shoulder and reduce the depth or load.
Ask a spotter to guide the elbows when working close to failure.
Keep wrists stacked; bent-back wrists under load can irritate the wrist.
checks: Bench angle pin is fully engaged and the seat is secure.
Dumbbells are matched and collars or heads are tight on adjustable dumbbells.
Clear floor space beside the bench to set the weights down.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if your lower back lifts off the pad, the dumbbells drift unevenly, you cannot reach ear level on the way down or shoulder pain appears.

programming.rehab: Light dumbbells through a pain-free range can help rebuild overhead pressing after shoulder issues, ideally guided by a physiotherapist.
programming.frequency: 1-3 times per week, 48-72 h between hard sessions for the shoulders.
programming.initialLoad: Pick a pair you can press for about 12 clean reps, finishing the set with 2-3 reps in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: The last two reps should slow but keep the same path; if the elbows flare or the back arches, the load is too heavy.
programming.progression: Double progression: work up to the top of the rep range on all sets, then move up to the next dumbbell pair.
programming.increase: Increase when you hit the top of the rep range on every set with good form and at least 1 rep in reserve.
programming.maintain: Keep the load if reps fall within the range; reduce it if form breaks, range shortens or the shoulder aches afterwards.

name: Standing barbell overhead press
musclesText: Primary: anterior deltoid, lateral deltoid, triceps brachii. Secondary: upper trapezius, serratus anterior, rectus abdominis and obliques, gluteus maximus as stabilisers.

steps.start: Stand under the bar in the rack, unrack it onto the front of your shoulders and take two short steps back.
steps.setup: Set the rack hooks at about upper-chest or collarbone height so you can unrack with a slight knee bend, and set safety arms just below shoulder height if available.
steps.feet: Stand with feet about hip to shoulder width apart, weight even across the whole foot, knees straight but not hyperextended.
steps.grip: Hold the bar just outside shoulder width with a full grip, bar low in the palm over the forearm bones, forearms vertical and elbows slightly in front of the bar.
steps.posture: Stand tall with glutes squeezed, ribs down and chin slightly tucked so the bar has a clear path past your face.
steps.brace: Take a big breath into your belly, brace hard and squeeze your glutes and quads so your torso stays rigid; there is no dip or leg drive.
steps.initiate: Press the bar straight up off the shoulders while pulling your head slightly back out of its path.
steps.concentric: Once the bar passes your forehead, move your head forward through the window so the bar finishes over the middle of your foot and the back of your neck, elbows locked.
steps.breathing: Hold the braced breath through the press, exhale at or near lockout, then take a fresh breath at the top or back at the shoulders before the next rep.
steps.eccentric: Lower the bar in a straight line back to the front rack, moving your head back slightly as it passes your face.
steps.rom: Full range from the bar resting on the front of the shoulders to locked elbows overhead with the shoulders shrugged up slightly.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-0: two seconds down, no pause, one controlled but forceful second up.
steps.finish: Finish with the bar over the mid-foot, arms locked, biceps beside the ears and traps lightly shrugged.
steps.exit: Lower the bar to the front rack, walk forward until it touches the uprights and lower it onto the hooks; if you fail, step back and let it down onto the safeties.

mistakes.m: Leaning back excessively and turning it into an incline press.
mistakes.fix: Squeeze glutes harder, keep ribs down and reduce the load until you can stay vertical.

mistakes.m: Pressing the bar forward around the face.
mistakes.fix: Move your head back first and keep the bar path straight, then bring your head through.

mistakes.m: Using a knee dip to start the bar.
mistakes.fix: Lock the knees and treat it as a strict press; use a push press only as a separate exercise.

mistakes.m: Elbows flaring well behind the bar at the start.
mistakes.fix: Set elbows slightly in front of the bar with vertical forearms before every rep.

safety: Keep the lumbar spine neutral; repeated big back arching under load can aggravate the lower back.
Use safety arms or a clear area to bail forward or back.
Stop if you get pinching shoulder pain at the top and check mobility or switch to a landmine or dumbbell press.
Wear flat, stable shoes.
checks: Rack hooks at the correct height and both sides level.
Collars fitted to both sides of the bar.
Safety arms set if your rack has them, and space behind you is clear.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if you need to lean back or bend the knees to finish, the bar drifts forward, bar speed stalls badly on early reps or your lower back aches.
progressions: Behind-the-neck press (advanced, only with good mobility)

programming.frequency: 1-3 times per week, 48-72 h between heavy pressing sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Start with an empty bar and add small jumps until about 8 reps feels like 2-3 left in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: Reps should be steady with no lean-back or knee bend; slowing near lockout is fine, grinding early reps means it is too heavy.
programming.progression: Double progression or small linear jumps; use 1-1.25 kg fractional plates per side when progress slows.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets hit the target reps with strict form and at least 1 rep in reserve.
programming.maintain: Hold the load when reps fall in range; reduce 5-10 percent if you lean back, miss reps or feel lower back or shoulder pain.

name: Seated barbell shoulder press
musclesText: Primary: anterior deltoid, lateral deltoid, triceps brachii. Secondary: upper trapezius, serratus anterior.

steps.start: Sit on the upright bench under the racked bar, back against the pad, and take your grip before unracking.
steps.setup: Use a shoulder-press station or place an upright bench in a squat rack, and set the hooks so the bar is a few centimetres below arm's reach when seated; set safety arms at about chin height when seated.
steps.feet: Feet flat and slightly wider than hips, knees bent, pushing lightly into the floor to stay planted on the seat.
steps.grip: Take a grip just outside shoulder width, bar low in the palms, so your forearms are vertical when the bar is at your upper chest.
steps.posture: Keep your upper back and buttocks on the pad, chest up and ribs down, avoiding a large arch to turn it into an incline press.
steps.brace: Breathe into your belly and brace before unracking, then rebrace before each rep.
steps.initiate: Unrack the bar to locked arms over your head, ideally with a spotter's help, then lower it to the top of your chest to begin.
steps.concentric: Press the bar up from the upper chest, moving the head back slightly, then finish with the bar over the crown of your head and elbows locked.
steps.breathing: Inhale and brace at the top or at the chest, hold through the hardest part of the press and exhale near lockout.
steps.eccentric: Lower the bar under control past your face to touch lightly on the upper chest just below the collarbones.
steps.rom: From the upper chest to locked elbows; shorten slightly if your shoulders will not let the bar reach the chest with forearms vertical and no pain.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-0: two seconds down, light touch on the chest, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish with arms locked, bar balanced over the shoulders and head through.
steps.exit: After the last rep lock out, move the bar back until it contacts the uprights and lower it onto the hooks; never try to rerack from the chest.

cues: Sit tall, glutes on the seat

mistakes.m: Arching hard so the chest rises to meet the bar.
mistakes.fix: Keep the bench fully upright, ribs down and glutes on the seat; lighten the load.

mistakes.m: Bouncing the bar off the chest.
mistakes.fix: Lower slowly and touch lightly before pressing.

mistakes.m: Hooks set too high, forcing a risky unrack.
mistakes.fix: Lower the hooks so you unrack with slightly bent elbows, or use a spotter for the liftoff.

mistakes.m: Bar drifting forward away from the face.
mistakes.fix: Pull the head back and press straight up, keeping the bar close.

safety: Use safety arms or a spotter because you cannot step away from a failed rep when seated.
Keep collars on; a seated position makes sliding plates hard to manage.
Avoid pressing into shoulder pain; reduce depth or switch to dumbbells.
checks: Bench is locked upright and positioned so the bar clears your face.
Hooks and safety arms set at correct heights on both sides.
Collars fitted and plates matched.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if you arch off the pad, need a spotter on early reps, the bar path wanders or shoulder discomfort builds.

programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week, 48-72 h between heavy pressing.
programming.initialLoad: Start with an empty bar, add small jumps and stop at a weight you can press for 8 reps with 2-3 in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: Reps should be smooth with the back on the pad; if you start arching or bouncing, it is too heavy.
programming.progression: Double progression with 2.5 kg total jumps, using fractional plates when needed.
programming.increase: Increase when you complete the top of the rep range on all sets with at least 1 rep in reserve.
programming.maintain: Hold the load while reps are in range; reduce it after a missed rep, poor bar path or shoulder pain.

name: Machine shoulder press
musclesText: Primary: anterior deltoid, lateral deltoid. Secondary: triceps brachii, upper trapezius, serratus anterior.

steps.start: Sit in the machine with your back on the pad and hands on the handles at shoulder height.
steps.setup: Adjust the seat so the handles start level with or slightly above your shoulders; on a selectorised machine set the pin, on a plate-loaded one load both sides evenly.
steps.feet: Place your feet flat on the floor or footrests, about hip width, to keep your hips pressed into the seat.
steps.grip: Grip the handles with a full grip, choosing the neutral or forward-facing handles, with wrists straight over the forearms.
steps.posture: Keep your head, upper back and buttocks against the pads with ribs down.
steps.brace: Brace your trunk lightly so your back does not peel off the pad as you press.
steps.initiate: Push the handles up smoothly without jerking the stack off its rest.
steps.concentric: Press until the elbows are almost straight, keeping the movement even between both arms.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower the handles under control to shoulder height without letting the weight stack touch down.
steps.rom: From about shoulder height to just short of lockout; keep the bottom position pain free.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-0: two seconds down, no pause, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish with arms nearly straight overhead, shoulders down from the ears and back still on the pad.
steps.exit: Lower the handles slowly until the stack rests, then let go; on plate-loaded machines engage any start lever and unload both sides evenly.

cues: Handles at shoulder height to start
Do not let the stack touch between reps

mistakes.m: Seat too low so the start position stretches the shoulder excessively.
mistakes.fix: Raise the seat so the handles begin around shoulder height.

mistakes.m: Banging the weight stack between reps.
mistakes.fix: Stop just before the plates touch and keep tension.

mistakes.m: Arching the back off the pad.
mistakes.fix: Reduce the load and keep the ribs down.

mistakes.m: Pressing with one side dominant.
mistakes.fix: Watch the handles and slow down; use a lighter load if they do not move evenly.

safety: Keep fingers clear of moving parts and the weight stack.
Avoid forcing a deep start position if it pinches the shoulder.
On plate-loaded machines, load and unload evenly so the lever arm does not tip.
checks: Seat height set and the pin fully inserted.
Selector pin fully in the stack.
Back pad and handles secure and undamaged.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if you cannot control the lowering, the back lifts from the pad, the stack crashes or one arm lags.
regressions: Light machine press through partial range

programming.rehab: The fixed path and easy loading make light sets through a comfortable range useful when returning from shoulder pain, ideally guided by a physiotherapist.
programming.frequency: 1-3 times per week, 48-72 h between hard shoulder sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Choose a pin you can press for about 12-15 reps with 2-3 in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: The last reps should slow but stay even, with the back on the pad.
programming.progression: Double progression: reach the top of the rep range on all sets, then move up one plate.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets reach the top of the range with at least 1 rep in reserve.
programming.maintain: Keep the load if you are within the range; reduce if form slips or the shoulder aches afterwards.

name: Arnold press
musclesText: Primary: anterior deltoid, lateral deltoid. Secondary: triceps brachii, upper trapezius, serratus anterior, rotator cuff.

steps.start: Sit on an upright bench and kick the dumbbells up to the front of your shoulders, palms facing you as at the top of a curl.
steps.setup: Set the bench to upright or one notch back from vertical so your back is supported and the dumbbells can pass in front of your face.
steps.feet: Feet flat and a little wider than hips, knees bent around 90 degrees.
steps.grip: Hold the dumbbells with palms facing your body, handles roughly vertical, elbows in front of you and close together at chin to chest height.
steps.posture: Keep your back on the pad, chest up and ribs down throughout the rotation.
steps.brace: Brace your trunk before each rep so the rotation does not pull your back off the bench.
steps.initiate: Begin by moving the elbows out to the sides while you start rotating the palms away from your face.
steps.concentric: Continue rotating and pressing in one smooth motion so the palms face forward by the time the dumbbells pass your head, then press to just short of lockout overhead.
steps.breathing: Inhale at the bottom, exhale as you rotate and press up.
steps.eccentric: Reverse the path: lower and bring the elbows back in front as you rotate the palms back towards your face, finishing in the start position.
steps.rom: From palms-in at chin height in front of the body to arms nearly straight overhead with palms forward; keep the rotation pain free.
steps.tempo: 2-0-2-0: two seconds down with rotation, no pause, two seconds up with rotation.
steps.finish: Finish with the dumbbells over your shoulders, palms forward and biceps near the ears.
steps.exit: Rotate back to the start position, lower the dumbbells to your thighs and set them on the floor one at a time.

mistakes.m: Rotating first and pressing afterwards, making two separate movements.
mistakes.fix: Blend the rotation and press so the palms finish turning as the dumbbells pass the head.

mistakes.m: Using momentum to swing the weights up.
mistakes.fix: Slow the tempo and lighten the dumbbells, as the rotation needs control.

mistakes.m: Leaning back off the pad.
mistakes.fix: Keep the bench upright and ribs down, and reduce the load.

mistakes.m: Starting with the dumbbells too low in front of the stomach.
mistakes.fix: Start at chin height with forearms close to vertical.

safety: Use lighter loads than a standard dumbbell press because the rotation adds strain at the front of the shoulder.
Skip or modify the rotation if it pinches in the front of the shoulder.
Use the knee kick to bring heavy dumbbells into position.
checks: Bench pin secure and angle set.
Dumbbells matched and secure.
Enough room in front of your face for the rotation.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if the rotation becomes jerky, you lean back, the dumbbells drift unevenly or the front of the shoulder aches.

programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week, 48-72 h between hard shoulder sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Start with dumbbells about 15-20 percent lighter than you use for a standard seated dumbbell press.
programming.judgeLoad: The rotation should stay smooth on the final reps; if you start swinging, the load is too heavy.
programming.progression: Double progression: reach the top of the rep range on all sets, then move up one dumbbell increment.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets reach the top of the range with clean rotation and 1-2 reps in reserve.
programming.maintain: Keep the load while reps are in range; reduce if the shoulder aches or the rotation breaks down.

name: Dumbbell lateral raise
musclesText: Primary: lateral deltoid. Secondary: anterior deltoid, upper trapezius, supraspinatus.

steps.start: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides or slightly in front of your thighs.
steps.setup: Choose light dumbbells; this lift uses small loads and stalls with heavy weights.
steps.feet: Stand with feet about hip width apart, knees soft.
steps.grip: Hold the handles with a relaxed grip, palms facing your thighs, elbows slightly bent and fixed.
steps.posture: Stand upright or lean very slightly forward from the hips, chest up, shoulders down away from the ears.
steps.brace: Lightly brace your trunk so you do not rock or lean back to swing the weights.
steps.initiate: Lead with the elbows and move the dumbbells out to the sides, not up towards the ears.
steps.concentric: Raise the arms out and slightly forward until the upper arms are about level with the shoulders, with elbows and hands at roughly the same height.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower slowly along the same arc until the dumbbells are just beside the thighs.
steps.rom: From arms by your sides to about shoulder height; going higher mostly adds trapezius work.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: one second up, one second pause at the top, two seconds down.
steps.finish: Finish with the upper arms at shoulder height, pinkies and thumbs roughly level, before lowering.
steps.exit: Lower the dumbbells to your sides and set them down or rack them by bending at the hips and knees.

mistakes.m: Swinging the body to lift heavier dumbbells.
mistakes.fix: Use a lighter pair and keep your torso still.

mistakes.m: Shrugging the shoulders up as the arms rise.
mistakes.fix: Think long neck and stop at shoulder height.

mistakes.m: Bending and straightening the elbows during the rep.
mistakes.fix: Fix a slight bend in the elbows and keep it constant.

mistakes.m: Hands rising well above the elbows.
mistakes.fix: Keep the hands level with or slightly below the elbows.
