safety: Keep loads light; heavy, swinging reps strain the shoulder and lower back.
Stop if you feel pinching at the top of the shoulder and lower the end point or raise slightly further forward.
Avoid turning the thumbs down (pouring the jug) if it causes discomfort.
checks: Dumbbells matched and in good condition.
Room around you to raise the arms without hitting anyone.
Mirror or clear sight line to check arm height if possible.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if you swing, shrug, bend the elbows to finish or cannot reach shoulder height with control.

programming.rehab: Very light dumbbells through a pain-free partial range can support shoulder rehabilitation under the guidance of a physiotherapist.
programming.frequency: 2-4 times per week; the lateral deltoids recover quickly from light isolation work.
programming.initialLoad: Pick a pair you can raise for 15 strict reps with 2 in reserve; this is often 4-10 kg for most lifters.
programming.judgeLoad: Reps should stay strict to shoulder height; any swinging or shrugging means it is too heavy.
programming.progression: Double progression with small jumps; add reps first because a 2 kg jump is a large relative increase.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets hit the top of the rep range with strict form.
programming.maintain: Keep the load while you are within range; reduce it if form becomes swingy or the shoulder pinches.

name: Cable lateral raise
musclesText: Primary: lateral deltoid. Secondary: anterior deltoid, upper trapezius, supraspinatus.

steps.start: Stand side-on to the cable stack with the pulley on the opposite side of your working arm, holding the handle in front of your hips.
steps.setup: Set the pulley at its lowest position and attach a single D-handle; the cable will run across the front of your body.
steps.feet: Stand about a foot's length away from the stack with feet hip width apart, knees soft.
steps.grip: Hold the handle in the hand farthest from the machine with a light grip, palm facing you, so the cable crosses in front of your thighs; rest the other hand on the machine or your hip.
steps.posture: Stand tall with a slight forward lean from the hips, shoulders down and chest up.
steps.brace: Brace your trunk lightly so the cable does not twist your torso towards the stack.
steps.initiate: Lead with the elbow and sweep the handle out and away from the machine.
steps.concentric: Raise the arm out to the side, slightly in front of the body, until the upper arm reaches about shoulder height, keeping a slight fixed bend in the elbow.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower slowly back across the body until the hand is in front of the opposite hip, keeping tension on the cable.
steps.rom: From the hand in front of the opposite hip to the upper arm at shoulder height; the cable keeps tension right at the bottom.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: one second up, one second hold, two seconds down.
steps.finish: Finish at shoulder height with the elbow and hand roughly level, then lower.
steps.exit: Return the handle slowly to the bottom until the stack rests, then let go; complete the same reps on the other arm.

cues: Do not let the stack touch

mistakes.m: Twisting the torso towards the stack to lift the weight.
mistakes.fix: Hold the machine with the free hand, brace and reduce the load.

mistakes.m: Pulling up with a shrug.
mistakes.fix: Keep the shoulder down and stop at shoulder height.

mistakes.m: Letting the stack crash at the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Lower slowly and keep light tension throughout.

mistakes.m: Standing too far away so the cable pulls you off balance.
mistakes.fix: Stand closer and stay square.

safety: Keep the load light; this is an isolation exercise for small muscles.
Keep the shoulder down and stop if you feel pinching at the top.
Hold the machine for balance with the free hand.
checks: Pulley locked at the lowest position.
Handle and clip secure.
Cable not frayed and pin fully in the stack.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if you twist, shrug, lean away or cannot control the lowering back across the body.

programming.rehab: Light cable work through a pain-free range can support shoulder rehabilitation when guided by a physiotherapist.
programming.frequency: 2-4 times per week, alternating sides within each set block.
programming.initialLoad: Start with the lightest plate or two and pick a load you can raise for 15 strict reps.
programming.judgeLoad: Reps should stay smooth with the torso still; twisting or shrugging means it is too heavy.
programming.progression: Double progression: add reps per arm, then move up one plate.
programming.increase: Increase when you reach the top of the rep range on all sets for both arms.
programming.maintain: Keep the load if reps fall within the range; reduce if the torso twists or shoulder discomfort appears.

name: Leaning cable lateral raise
musclesText: Primary: lateral deltoid. Secondary: anterior deltoid, upper trapezius, supraspinatus, obliques as stabilisers.

steps.start: Stand side-on to the cable column, holding the frame with the near hand and the handle in the far hand in front of your hips, then lean away.
steps.setup: Set the pulley to the lowest position and attach a single D-handle.
steps.feet: Place your feet close together near the base of the column, with the inside foot slightly closer to the post.
steps.grip: Hold the post or column at about chest height with the near hand and the handle in the far hand, palm facing in, cable crossing in front of your body.
steps.posture: Lean your whole body away from the column in a straight line from ankles to head, about 15-30 degrees, with the near arm long and supporting you.
steps.brace: Brace your trunk and squeeze your glutes so your body stays straight and does not bend at the waist.
steps.initiate: Lead with the elbow and sweep the handle out to the side, away from the machine.
steps.concentric: Raise the arm until the upper arm is about level with the shoulder; because you are leaning, this is a longer arc with tension right from the bottom.
steps.breathing: Exhale on the way up, inhale on the way down.
steps.eccentric: Lower under control back across the front of the body until the hand is in front of the hips.
steps.rom: From the hand in front of the hips to the upper arm level with the shoulder; avoid going much above that.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: one second up, one second pause, two seconds down.
steps.finish: Finish with the arm at shoulder height and your body still in a straight lean.
steps.exit: Lower the handle under control, stand up by walking your feet towards the column, then let the stack rest and switch sides.

cues: Shoulder down away from the ear

mistakes.m: Bending at the waist instead of leaning in a straight line.
mistakes.fix: Brace, squeeze the glutes and keep your body straight from ankles to head.

mistakes.m: Using the support arm to pull your body upright on each rep.
mistakes.fix: Keep the support arm long and relaxed and the lean constant.

mistakes.m: Raising the arm well above shoulder height and shrugging.
mistakes.fix: Stop at shoulder level and keep the shoulder down.

mistakes.m: Loading too heavily for the lean position.
mistakes.fix: Use a lighter plate than for the upright cable raise.

safety: Make sure your grip on the post is secure before leaning away.
Keep the lean modest if you have grip or elbow issues on the supporting side.
Stop if the top of the shoulder pinches.
checks: Post or column is solid and suitable to hold.
Pulley at the lowest setting and clip closed.
Floor dry and non-slip under your feet.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if your body angle changes during the set, you shrug, or you cannot lower slowly.
progressions: Leaning cable lateral raise with a pause at the top
Lengthened partial reps after full-range failure

programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Start lighter than your upright cable lateral raise, usually the lightest plate, and aim for 15 strict reps.
programming.judgeLoad: Reps should be controlled without the body lean changing; swinging means it is too heavy.
programming.progression: Double progression per arm, then move up one plate.
programming.increase: Increase when every set reaches the top of the range on both arms.
programming.maintain: Keep the load within range; reduce it if the lean breaks or shoulder pain appears.

name: Machine lateral raise
musclesText: Primary: lateral deltoid. Secondary: anterior deltoid, upper trapezius, supraspinatus.

steps.start: Sit in the machine with your chest against the pad or back upright, upper arms against the arm pads or hands on the handles at your sides.
steps.setup: Adjust the seat height so the machine's pivot points line up with your shoulder joints and set the pin to a light weight.
steps.feet: Place your feet flat on the floor or footrests, hip width.
steps.grip: Rest the outer forearms or elbows against the pads, or grip the handles lightly; the pressure should be through the elbows, not the hands.
steps.posture: Sit tall with chest up, shoulders down and back, and head neutral.
steps.brace: Brace lightly so your torso stays still on the seat.
steps.initiate: Drive the elbows out and up against the pads without shrugging.
steps.concentric: Raise the arms until the upper arms are level with the shoulders.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower slowly until the arms are by your sides, stopping just before the stack touches.
steps.rom: From arms by your sides to upper arms at shoulder height.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: one second up, one second pause, two seconds down.
steps.finish: Finish with the elbows at shoulder height and shoulders still down.
steps.exit: Lower the pads slowly until the stack rests, then release and stand up.

cues: Pivot lines up with the shoulders
Keep the stack off the rest

mistakes.m: Seat too high or low so the arms rub against the pads awkwardly.
mistakes.fix: Adjust the seat until the pivot sits level with your shoulder joint.

mistakes.m: Pulling with the hands and shrugging.
mistakes.fix: Relax the hands and push through the elbows.

mistakes.m: Bouncing the weight at the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Lower slowly and stop before the stack touches.

safety: Keep fingers away from moving parts.
Stop if the top of the shoulder pinches and reduce the range.
Do not force a range beyond what is comfortable.
checks: Seat height pin engaged.
Selector pin fully in.
Pads secure and undamaged.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if you shrug, lean back or cannot pause at the top.
regressions: Machine lateral raise with partial range

programming.rehab: The guided path suits light, pain-free sets during shoulder rehabilitation, ideally with a physiotherapist's guidance.
programming.frequency: 2-4 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Choose a pin you can lift for 15 controlled reps with a one-second pause at the top.
programming.judgeLoad: The final reps should still pause at the top without shrugging.
programming.progression: Double progression: add reps, then move up one plate.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets hit the top of the rep range with a pause.
programming.maintain: Keep the load while within range; reduce if form slips or the shoulder aches.

name: Dumbbell front raise
musclesText: Primary: anterior deltoid. Secondary: lateral deltoid, pectoralis major (clavicular head), upper trapezius, serratus anterior.

steps.start: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand resting in front of your thighs.
steps.setup: Choose light dumbbells; the long lever makes this exercise much harder than the weight suggests.
steps.feet: Stand with feet hip width apart, knees soft, weight even over the feet.
steps.grip: Hold the handles with palms facing your thighs (overhand) or a neutral grip, elbows with a slight fixed bend.
steps.posture: Stand upright with chest up, shoulders down and back, and neck neutral.
steps.brace: Brace your trunk and squeeze the glutes so you do not lean back as the weights rise.
steps.initiate: Lift the dumbbells forward from the shoulders without swinging the hips.
steps.concentric: Raise both arms straight in front of you until the hands reach shoulder height, arms roughly parallel to the floor.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower slowly along the same path back to the front of the thighs.
steps.rom: From in front of the thighs to shoulder height; going higher adds little for the front deltoid and increases trapezius involvement.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: one second up, one second pause at shoulder height, two seconds down.
steps.finish: Finish with the dumbbells at shoulder height in front of you, then lower.
steps.exit: Lower the dumbbells to your thighs and set them down by bending at the hips and knees.

mistakes.m: Leaning back and swinging the dumbbells up.
mistakes.fix: Brace, squeeze the glutes and use a lighter pair.

mistakes.m: Raising well above shoulder height.
mistakes.fix: Stop when the arms are parallel to the floor.

mistakes.m: Shrugging as the arms rise.
mistakes.fix: Keep the shoulders pulled down and think long neck.

mistakes.m: Dropping the weights quickly.
mistakes.fix: Take two seconds to lower each rep.

safety: Keep loads light; the front deltoid already works hard in pressing.
Avoid lumbar extension by keeping the ribs down.
Stop if you feel pain at the front of the shoulder and reduce the range or switch to a neutral grip.
checks: Dumbbells matched and secure.
Clear space in front of you.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if you lean back, swing, shrug or cannot pause at shoulder height.

programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week; often unnecessary if you already do plenty of pressing.
programming.initialLoad: Pick dumbbells you can raise for 12-15 strict reps; usually lighter than for lateral raises.
programming.judgeLoad: The last reps should be slow but still reach shoulder height without leaning back.
programming.progression: Double progression: add reps, then move to the next dumbbell.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets hit the top of the rep range with strict form.
programming.maintain: Keep the load while reps are in range; reduce if you need to swing or the shoulder aches.

name: Reverse dumbbell fly
musclesText: Primary: posterior deltoid. Secondary: rhomboids, middle and lower trapezius, infraspinatus and teres minor.

steps.start: Hinge forward at the hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, with a dumbbell in each hand hanging under your chest; or lie chest-down on an incline bench.
steps.setup: Use light dumbbells; if chest-supported, set a bench to about 30 degrees and lie face down with your chin just over the top.
steps.feet: Standing, feet hip width with knees bent; chest-supported, toes or feet on the floor behind the bench for stability.
steps.grip: Hold the handles with palms facing each other, elbows slightly bent and fixed.
steps.posture: Keep a flat back from hips to head with the neck neutral, eyes on the floor a little ahead.
steps.brace: Brace your trunk to hold the hinge, so your torso does not rise as you lift.
steps.initiate: Move the arms out to the sides by leading with the elbows, without pulling the shoulder blades hard together first.
steps.concentric: Sweep the dumbbells out and up in a wide arc until the upper arms are in line with your torso.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you raise the dumbbells, inhale as you lower them.
steps.eccentric: Lower slowly along the same arc until the dumbbells hang under your shoulders.
steps.rom: From arms hanging down to upper arms level with the torso; going beyond that mostly shifts work to the trapezius.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: one second up, one second pause, two seconds down.
steps.finish: Finish with arms out wide in a T shape, elbows slightly bent, before lowering.
steps.exit: Lower the dumbbells, set them on the floor while still hinged or stand up holding them close to your body, then put them down.

mistakes.m: Standing up during the set so the movement becomes a lateral raise.
mistakes.fix: Hold the hinge or use the chest-supported version.

mistakes.m: Rowing the dumbbells by bending the elbows.
mistakes.fix: Fix the elbow angle and keep the arms wide.

mistakes.m: Using momentum from the torso.
mistakes.fix: Reduce the load and pause at the top.

mistakes.m: Craning the neck up to look in the mirror.
mistakes.fix: Keep the neck in line with the spine.

safety: If your lower back fatigues in the standing hinge, use the chest-supported bench version.
Keep loads light; the rear deltoids are small.
Stop if you feel pinching at the back of the shoulder.
checks: Bench angle secure if chest-supported.
Dumbbells matched and light.
Clear space to the sides for the arms.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if your torso rises, you start rowing, or you cannot reach torso height with a pause.
progressions: Chest-supported reverse fly with a pause

programming.rehab: Light chest-supported sets can help rebuild upper-back and rear-shoulder endurance for posture-related shoulder issues, ideally guided by a physiotherapist.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Start with light dumbbells you can raise for 15 strict reps; this is often 2-6 kg.
programming.judgeLoad: Reps should finish at torso height without the body rising; swinging means it is too heavy.
programming.progression: Double progression: add reps, then move up one dumbbell.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets reach the top of the rep range with a pause at the top.
programming.maintain: Keep the load within range; reduce if form slips or the lower back tires first.

name: Reverse pec deck
musclesText: Primary: posterior deltoid. Secondary: rhomboids, middle trapezius, infraspinatus and teres minor.

steps.start: Sit facing the machine with your chest against the pad, arms reaching forward to the handles.
steps.setup: Adjust the handles to the rear-delt position so they are in front of you, and set the seat so the handles are at shoulder height.
steps.feet: Place your feet flat on the floor or footrests, about hip width.
steps.grip: Hold the handles with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) or overhand grip, elbows slightly bent.
steps.posture: Keep your chest on the pad, shoulders down and neck neutral.
steps.brace: Brace lightly so your chest stays on the pad and you do not lean back.
steps.initiate: Sweep the handles outwards by leading with the elbows.
steps.concentric: Move the arms back until the upper arms are in line with your shoulders and torso.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you open your arms, inhale as you return.
steps.eccentric: Bring the handles back under control until your hands are in front of your shoulders, stopping before the stack touches.
steps.rom: From arms in front of the shoulders to upper arms in line with the torso.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: one second out, one second pause, two seconds back.
steps.finish: Finish with the arms wide and in line with the body, shoulders down.
steps.exit: Return the handles slowly until the stack rests, release and step out.

mistakes.m: Leaning back off the chest pad.
mistakes.fix: Keep the chest pressed on the pad and reduce the load.

mistakes.m: Squeezing the shoulder blades hard together and shrugging.
mistakes.fix: Think of moving the arms wide and keep the shoulders down.

mistakes.m: Seat height wrong so the handles are too high or low.
mistakes.fix: Set the seat so the handles are level with the shoulders.

safety: Keep fingers clear of moving parts.
Check the handles are set for rear delts so they do not swing unexpectedly.
Stop if the back of the shoulder pinches.
checks: Handle position lever locked in the rear-delt setting.
Seat height pin engaged.
Selector pin fully inserted.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if you lean back, shrug or cannot pause at the end range.

programming.rehab: The guided path suits light, pain-free sets for rear-shoulder and upper-back strength in rehabilitation, ideally with a physiotherapist's guidance.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Choose a pin you can move for 15 controlled reps with a one-second pause.
programming.judgeLoad: The final reps should still pause without leaning back.
programming.progression: Double progression: add reps, then move up a plate.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets hit the top of the range.
programming.maintain: Keep the load within range; reduce if you lean back or shrug.

name: Rear-delt cable fly
musclesText: Primary: posterior deltoid. Secondary: rhomboids, middle trapezius, infraspinatus and teres minor.

steps.start: Stand side-on to the cable column, holding the handle or the cable end in the hand farthest from the machine with your arm reaching across your body.
steps.setup: Set the pulley at about shoulder height and use a single D-handle, or hold the cable ball directly.
steps.feet: Stand with feet hip width, slightly staggered, about one step away from the column.
steps.grip: Hold the handle with a neutral or overhand grip, elbow slightly bent and fixed; rest the free hand on your hip or the machine.
steps.posture: Stand tall with chest up, shoulders square to the front and neck neutral.
steps.brace: Brace your trunk so your torso does not rotate as the arm sweeps back.
steps.initiate: Start the sweep by leading with the elbow away from the machine.
steps.concentric: Sweep the arm across and back at shoulder height until the upper arm is in line with your shoulders.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you sweep back, inhale as you return.
steps.eccentric: Return the arm slowly across your body until the hand is in front of the opposite shoulder.
steps.rom: From the hand in front of the opposite shoulder to the arm level with and in line with the shoulders.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: one second out, one second pause, two seconds back.
steps.finish: Finish with the arm out wide at shoulder height, shoulder blade not shrugged.
steps.exit: Return the arm slowly until the stack rests, let go, turn around and repeat on the other side.

mistakes.m: Rotating the torso to move the cable.
mistakes.fix: Brace, keep the hips and chest square and use a lighter load.

mistakes.m: Bending the elbow into a row.
mistakes.fix: Keep the slight elbow bend fixed.

mistakes.m: Taking the arm too far back so the shoulder rolls forward.
mistakes.fix: Stop when the arm is in line with the shoulders.

mistakes.m: Shrugging the shoulder up.
mistakes.fix: Keep the shoulder down and neck long.

safety: Keep the load light enough to control the end range.
Stop if you feel pinching at the back or front of the shoulder.
Ensure the cable path does not cross your face.
checks: Pulley locked at shoulder height.
Clip and handle secure.
Cable in good condition and pin fully inserted.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if you rotate, row, shrug or cannot pause at the end.
progressions: Rear-delt cable fly with a pause

programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Start with the lightest plate and aim for 15 strict reps per arm.
programming.judgeLoad: Reps should be smooth with the torso still.
programming.progression: Double progression per arm, then move up one plate.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets hit the top of the range on both sides.
programming.maintain: Keep the load within range; reduce if form breaks.

name: Dumbbell shrug
musclesText: Primary: upper trapezius. Secondary: levator scapulae, forearm flexors (grip), rhomboids.

steps.start: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand hanging at your sides, palms facing your thighs.
steps.setup: Pick up the dumbbells from the rack or floor with a neutral back, bending at the hips and knees.
steps.feet: Stand with feet hip width apart, knees soft.
steps.grip: Hold the handles in a neutral grip with a firm full grip; use straps if your grip fails before your traps.
steps.posture: Stand upright with chest up, arms straight and neck neutral, chin neither tucked nor jutting.
steps.brace: Brace lightly to keep the torso still.
steps.initiate: Lift the shoulders straight up towards your ears.
steps.concentric: Shrug as high as possible without bending the elbows or rolling the shoulders.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you shrug up, inhale as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower the shoulders slowly to a full stretch with the arms straight.
steps.rom: From a full stretch with shoulders down to shoulders as close to the ears as possible.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: one second up, one second hold at the top, two seconds down.
steps.finish: Finish at the top with a one-second squeeze before lowering.
steps.exit: Lower the dumbbells under control and set them down by bending at the hips and knees.

mistakes.m: Rolling the shoulders in circles.
mistakes.fix: Shrug straight up and down.

mistakes.m: Bending the elbows to help.
mistakes.fix: Keep arms straight and use a lighter load.

mistakes.m: Short, bouncing reps.
mistakes.fix: Pause at the top and lower fully.

mistakes.m: Pushing the head forward.
mistakes.fix: Keep the chin neutral and eyes forward.

safety: Keep the neck neutral to avoid neck strain.
Use a neutral back when picking up and setting down heavy dumbbells.
Stop if you feel tingling or numbness in the arms.
checks: Dumbbells matched and in good condition.
Straps ready if needed.
Clear floor space to set the weights down.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if your range shrinks, you bend the elbows or need to bounce the weight.
regressions: Lighter dumbbell shrug with a pause

programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Choose dumbbells you can shrug for 12-15 reps with a full pause at the top.
programming.judgeLoad: The last reps should still reach full height with a pause.
programming.progression: Double progression: add reps, then move up one dumbbell.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets hit the top of the rep range with a pause.
programming.maintain: Keep the load within range; reduce if the range shortens or neck discomfort appears.

name: Barbell shrug
musclesText: Primary: upper trapezius. Secondary: levator scapulae, forearm flexors (grip), rhomboids.

steps.start: Stand tall holding the barbell in front of your thighs with straight arms.
steps.setup: Set the bar in a rack at mid-thigh height so you can unrack it without deadlifting from the floor.
steps.feet: Stand with feet hip width apart, knees soft.
steps.grip: Use an overhand grip just outside the thighs; use straps if your grip fails first.
steps.posture: Stand upright with chest up, arms straight and neck neutral.
steps.brace: Brace your trunk so the bar does not pull you forward.
steps.initiate: Lift the shoulders straight up towards the ears.
steps.concentric: Shrug as high as possible, keeping the bar close to your thighs and elbows straight.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you shrug, inhale as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower the shoulders slowly to a full stretch.
steps.rom: From a full stretch to shoulders as high as possible.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: one second up, one second hold, two seconds down.
steps.finish: Finish with a pause at the top before lowering.
steps.exit: Walk the bar back into the rack and lower it onto the hooks or safety pins.

mistakes.m: Rolling the shoulders forward or back.
mistakes.fix: Shrug straight up and down.

mistakes.m: Bending the elbows.
mistakes.fix: Keep the arms straight and reduce the load.

mistakes.m: Leaning back to move the bar.
mistakes.fix: Brace and use a lighter weight.

mistakes.m: Pulling the bar from the floor each set.
mistakes.fix: Unrack from a rack set at mid-thigh height.

safety: Unrack from the rack to protect your lower back.
Keep the neck neutral.
Stop if you feel tingling or numbness in the arms.
checks: Rack hooks or pins at mid-thigh height.
Collars fitted.
Straps ready if needed.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if the range shortens, you lean back or bend the elbows.
regressions: Light barbell shrug with a pause

programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Start with a bar you can shrug for 12-15 reps with a full pause.
programming.judgeLoad: The last reps should still reach full height without leaning back.
programming.progression: Double progression: add reps, then add 5 kg.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets hit the top of the range with a pause.
programming.maintain: Keep the load within range; reduce if the range shortens or the lower back aches.

name: Cable external rotation
musclesText: Primary: infraspinatus, teres minor. Secondary: posterior deltoid, supraspinatus, middle trapezius as stabilisers.

steps.start: Stand side-on to the cable column with the working arm farthest from the machine, holding the handle across your stomach.
steps.setup: Set the pulley at elbow height and attach a single D-handle; place a small rolled towel between your elbow and side if you like.
steps.feet: Stand with feet hip width apart, about one step away from the column.
steps.grip: Hold the handle with a light grip, elbow bent to 90 degrees and tucked against your side or the towel.
steps.posture: Stand tall, shoulders square and down, neck neutral.
steps.brace: Brace lightly so your torso does not rotate.
steps.initiate: Rotate the forearm outwards, keeping the elbow pinned to your side.
steps.concentric: Rotate until the forearm points straight forward or slightly beyond, as far as is comfortable without the elbow leaving your side.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you rotate out, inhale as you return.
steps.eccentric: Return slowly until the hand is back across your stomach.
steps.rom: From the hand across the stomach to the forearm pointing forward or slightly out, staying pain free.
steps.tempo: 2-0-2-1: two seconds out, one second pause, two seconds back.
steps.finish: Finish with the forearm rotated out and the elbow still against your side.
steps.exit: Return the handle slowly until the stack rests, then let go and switch sides.

mistakes.m: Letting the elbow drift away from the body.
mistakes.fix: Use a towel roll and keep it squeezed in place.

mistakes.m: Rotating the torso.
mistakes.fix: Keep the hips and chest square and use a lighter load.

mistakes.m: Using too heavy a load.
mistakes.fix: Choose a light weight you can control for 15 or more reps.

safety: Use light loads; the rotator cuff muscles are small.
Never push through sharp pain, and stop if you feel numbness or tingling.
If you are rehabbing an injury, follow a physiotherapist's guidance.
checks: Pulley at elbow height.
Clip and handle secure.
Lightest plate selected to start.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if the elbow drifts, the torso rotates, you shrug or feel pain.
progressions: Cable external rotation at 90 degrees of shoulder abduction

programming.rehab: Very light, slow sets through a pain-free range are a common part of shoulder rehabilitation; follow a physiotherapist's plan if you have an injury.
programming.frequency: 2-4 times per week, often in a warm-up.
programming.initialLoad: Start with the lightest plate; most people need only a few kilograms.
programming.judgeLoad: Reps should be smooth with the elbow pinned and no pain.
programming.progression: Double progression: add reps up to 20, then move up one plate.
programming.increase: Increase when you reach 20 controlled reps on all sets.
programming.maintain: Keep the load within range; reduce if any pain or form loss appears.

name: Standing barbell curl
musclesText: Primary: biceps brachii (long and short heads). Secondary: brachialis, brachioradialis, wrist flexors, anterior deltoid as a stabiliser.

steps.start: Stand tall holding a straight barbell at arm's length against the front of your thighs, palms facing forward.
steps.setup: Load a straight barbell lightly with collars, or pick a fixed-weight straight bar from the rack; set it on a rack at mid-thigh height so you can lift it out without bending far.
steps.feet: Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees soft and weight spread evenly through the whole foot.
steps.grip: Take a shoulder-width underhand (supinated) grip so your forearms run straight down from your elbows; wrap your thumbs around the bar.
steps.posture: Stand upright with ribs stacked over the pelvis, chest up and shoulders drawn slightly back and down; elbows sit just in front of your hips.
steps.brace: Squeeze your glutes and tighten your abdominals as if about to be prodded, so the lower back does not arch as the bar rises.
steps.initiate: Start by bending at the elbows while keeping your upper arms still; do not lean back or swing the hips to get the bar moving.
steps.concentric: Curl the bar in an arc towards your upper chest, letting the elbows drift forward only slightly at the very top, and keep your wrists neutral rather than curled.
steps.breathing: Breathe out as you curl the bar up and breathe in as you lower it.
steps.eccentric: Lower the bar under control until your elbows are fully straight, resisting the weight the whole way rather than letting it drop.
steps.rom: Move from full elbow extension at the bottom to roughly shoulder height at the top, stopping before the forearms are vertical and tension disappears.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: two seconds down, no pause at the bottom, one second up, a brief squeeze at the top.
steps.finish: Finish each rep with arms straight and the bar touching your thighs, body still upright, before starting the next.
steps.exit: After the last rep lower the bar to your thighs, then bend your knees and keep a flat back to return it to the rack or floor.

mistakes.m: Leaning back and swinging the hips to start the rep.
mistakes.fix: Reduce the load until you can curl with your torso still, or stand with your back against a wall to learn the position.

mistakes.m: Elbows travelling far forward so the shoulders take over.
mistakes.fix: Keep your upper arms close to vertical and stop the bar around shoulder height.

mistakes.m: Cutting the bottom short and never straightening the arms.
mistakes.fix: Lower until the elbows are fully extended on every rep, even if that means a lighter bar.

mistakes.m: Wrists curling back or bending into extension under load.
mistakes.fix: Hold the wrists in line with the forearms and grip the bar firmly.

safety: If a straight bar causes wrist or inner elbow discomfort, switch to the EZ-bar curl rather than forcing the position.
Avoid heavy cheat reps that load the lower back; keep the trunk braced throughout.
Stop the set if you feel sharp pain at the front of the elbow or shoulder.
checks: Check that the plates are secured with collars on both sides.
Make sure the bar knurling is clean and your hands are dry, using chalk if needed.
Clear space in front of you so the bar can be set down safely.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if you must lean back to finish reps, if you cannot fully straighten your arms at the bottom, or if your elbows or wrists ache during or after sessions.
progressions: Barbell curl with a slower 4-second lowering

programming.rehab: Can be used with a very light bar and slow tempo late in elbow rehabilitation once cleared by a physiotherapist; otherwise prefer cable or dumbbell options.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week for the biceps, with 48 h between hard sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Start with an empty or light bar and choose a load you can curl 12 times with strict form and two reps in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: The last two reps should slow down but your torso should stay still; if you need to swing, the load is too heavy.
programming.progression: Double progression: work within 8-12 reps, adding reps each session until all sets reach the top of the range.
programming.increase: Increase by 2.5 kg total (1.25 kg per side) once every set reaches 12 strict reps at the target RIR.
programming.maintain: Keep the load the same while you are still adding reps or tidying technique; reduce it after a poor night's sleep or if elbow discomfort appears.

name: EZ-bar curl
musclesText: Primary: biceps brachii (short head emphasis with the narrow grip), brachialis. Secondary: brachioradialis, wrist flexors.

steps.start: Stand upright holding an EZ bar at arm's length against your thighs with your hands on the inner angled grips.
steps.setup: Use a fixed EZ bar or load an Olympic EZ bar with collars; pick it up from a rack or from the floor with a flat back.
steps.feet: Stand with feet about hip-width apart, knees unlocked, weight centred over mid-foot.
steps.grip: Place each hand on the inner bend of the bar so your palms angle slightly inwards in a semi-supinated grip, roughly a little narrower than shoulder width.
steps.posture: Keep your chest lifted, shoulders back and down, and upper arms hanging close to your sides.
steps.brace: Brace your abdominals and squeeze your glutes to stop your hips pushing forward as you curl.
steps.initiate: Begin by flexing at the elbows while the upper arms stay still beside your torso.
steps.concentric: Curl the bar up in an arc to just below your collarbones, keeping the wrists straight on the angled grips and the elbows close together.
steps.breathing: Exhale on the way up, inhale on the way down.
steps.eccentric: Lower the bar slowly along the same arc until your arms are straight and the bar rests lightly against your thighs.
steps.rom: Full elbow extension at the bottom to the point just before your forearms become vertical at the top.
steps.tempo: 3-0-1-0: three seconds down, no pause, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish each rep with arms fully extended and posture unchanged.
steps.exit: After the final rep hold the bar at your thighs, hinge with a flat back and bent knees, and place it on the floor or rack.

mistakes.m: Gripping the outer angles instead of the inner ones.
mistakes.fix: Place your hands on the inner bends to match the narrow-grip version described here.

mistakes.m: Letting the elbows flare out to the sides.
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows tucked and pointing down towards the floor throughout.

mistakes.m: Rocking the torso to start each rep.
mistakes.fix: Lower the load and pause briefly at the bottom of each rep to remove momentum.

mistakes.m: Dropping the bar quickly on the way down.
mistakes.fix: Count three seconds on every lowering phase.

safety: The angled grip is usually kinder to the wrists than a straight bar; still stop if you feel sharp wrist or elbow pain.
Keep your lower back neutral and avoid leaning back to finish reps.
checks: Confirm collars are tight on a loadable EZ bar.
Check that both sides are loaded with matching plates.
Make sure you have room to lower the bar to the floor safely.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if your elbows flare, your torso swings, or you cannot control a three-second lowering on the last reps.

programming.rehab: A light EZ-bar curl with a slow tempo can help rebuild elbow flexor tolerance after injury; follow your physiotherapist's guidance on load.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week, 48 h between hard biceps sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Begin with the empty EZ bar or a light fixed bar that you can curl 12-15 times with two to three reps to spare.
programming.judgeLoad: Aim to finish each set with one to two reps in reserve and no change in posture or elbow position.
programming.progression: Double progression within 8-12 reps; add reps first, then load.
programming.increase: Add 2.5 kg once you complete all sets at 12 reps with good form.
programming.maintain: Hold the weight steady while reps are still climbing; drop 10 per cent if form breaks or the elbows ache.

name: Alternating dumbbell curl
musclesText: Primary: biceps brachii (both heads, with supination emphasis). Secondary: brachialis, brachioradialis, forearm flexors.

steps.start: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with palms facing your thighs.
steps.setup: Choose a matched pair of dumbbells from the rack and step back into clear space.
steps.feet: Feet hip-width apart, knees soft, weight even across both feet.
steps.grip: Hold each dumbbell in the middle of the handle in a neutral grip; you will rotate to a palm-up grip as you curl.
steps.posture: Stand tall with chest up, shoulders level and down, and upper arms hanging vertically at your sides.
steps.brace: Tighten your abdominals lightly so your torso does not twist or sway as one arm works.
steps.initiate: Curl one dumbbell while the other arm stays straight at your side, starting the movement by bending the elbow.
steps.concentric: As the dumbbell rises, turn your palm upwards so it faces your shoulder by mid-range, and keep curling until the forearm is nearly vertical; keep the elbow beside your ribs.
steps.breathing: Breathe out as each dumbbell rises and in as it lowers.
steps.eccentric: Lower the dumbbell under control, rotating back to a neutral grip near the bottom, until your elbow is fully straight; then curl the other arm.
steps.rom: From full elbow extension with a neutral grip to full flexion with the palm turned up; both arms complete the same range.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: two seconds down, one second up, a one-second squeeze at the top.
steps.finish: A rep is complete when both arms have curled once; finish each side with the arm straight before switching.
steps.exit: After the last rep lower both dumbbells to your sides, then bend your knees to return them to the rack.

cues: Turn the palm up as you curl

mistakes.m: Swinging the body or twisting the shoulders to help the dumbbell up.
mistakes.fix: Lower the weight and keep your shoulders square to the front.

mistakes.m: Not supinating, so the movement becomes a hammer curl.
mistakes.fix: Actively rotate your little finger upwards as the dumbbell passes your hip.

mistakes.m: Starting the next arm before the first has fully lowered.
mistakes.fix: Finish each lowering with a straight elbow before the other side begins.

mistakes.m: Elbow drifting forward to lift the weight higher.
mistakes.fix: Stop when the forearm is near vertical and keep the upper arm pinned.

safety: Pick dumbbells you can control on both sides; the weaker arm sets the load.
Avoid twisting the lower back to shift heavy dumbbells.
Stop if supinating causes sharp pain at the elbow or forearm.
checks: Check the dumbbell heads are secure on adjustable or spin-lock dumbbells.
Make sure the floor around you is clear of other weights.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if one side cannot match the other's reps, if your torso twists, or if you stop rotating the palm fully.

programming.rehab: Light dumbbells and slow reps are a common step in returning to loaded elbow flexion after injury; check with a physiotherapist first.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week, 48 h between hard biceps sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Choose dumbbells you can curl 12 times per arm with the palm fully rotated and two reps to spare.
programming.judgeLoad: The last reps on the weaker arm should be slow but strict; any torso twist means the load is too heavy.
programming.progression: Double progression in the 8-12 rep range per arm.
programming.increase: Move up one dumbbell increment (usually 2 kg per hand) when all sets reach 12 reps per arm.
programming.maintain: Stay at the same dumbbells while reps are climbing, and drop a size if the jump causes you to swing.

name: Incline dumbbell curl
musclesText: Primary: biceps brachii (long head emphasised in the lengthened position). Secondary: brachialis, brachioradialis.

steps.start: Sit back on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight down behind your torso, palms facing forward.
steps.setup: Set an adjustable bench to 45-60 degrees; a lower angle increases the stretch on the front of the shoulder, so start nearer 60 if you are new to it.
steps.feet: Place your feet flat on the floor slightly wider than hip-width for stability.
steps.grip: Hold the dumbbells with a supinated, palms-forward grip, thumbs wrapped around the handles.
steps.posture: Keep your head, upper back and hips on the pad with the chest lifted; let the arms hang vertically so the elbows sit slightly behind your body.
steps.brace: Brace lightly through your trunk and keep your shoulders pressed back into the bench so they do not roll forward.
steps.initiate: Begin by bending the elbows without letting the upper arms swing forward.
steps.concentric: Curl both dumbbells up towards your shoulders, keeping the upper arms close to vertical so the biceps do the work from the stretched position.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you curl, inhale as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower slowly until the elbows are fully straight and you feel a stretch in the biceps; do not bounce at the bottom.
steps.rom: Full extension with the arms hanging behind the torso to the point where the forearms are near vertical at the top.
steps.tempo: 3-0-1-0: three seconds down, no pause, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish each rep with the arms hanging straight and your back still against the pad.
steps.exit: After the set, lower the dumbbells to full extension, sit upright carefully and place them on the floor beside the bench before standing.

mistakes.m: Elbows swinging forward to start the curl, turning it into a standard curl.
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows pointing at the floor and use a lighter weight.

mistakes.m: Shoulders rolling forward off the bench.
mistakes.fix: Pull the shoulder blades back and keep them in contact with the pad.

mistakes.m: Setting the bench too low and feeling strain at the front of the shoulder.
mistakes.fix: Raise the bench towards 60 degrees.

mistakes.m: Lifting the head and chest off the pad as reps get hard.
mistakes.fix: End the set when you can no longer keep your back on the bench.

safety: The stretched position loads the long head tendon; use moderate weights and avoid bouncing at the bottom.
Raise the incline or stop if you feel pain at the front of the shoulder.
Get into and out of the bench carefully with the dumbbells close to your body.
checks: Check the bench back and seat pins are fully locked.
Make sure the bench is stable and on flat floor.
Place dumbbells within easy reach before sitting back.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if you cannot reach full extension under control, if the elbows drift forward, or if the front of the shoulder aches.

programming.rehab: Not ideal early in rehabilitation because of the stretched shoulder position; use only with very light weights if a physiotherapist approves.
programming.frequency: 1-3 times per week, 48 h between hard biceps sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Start with dumbbells roughly 60-70 per cent of what you use for a standing curl and aim for 12 controlled reps.
programming.judgeLoad: You should reach full extension on every rep with your shoulders on the pad; the last two reps should be hard but strict.
programming.progression: Double progression from 8 to 12 reps.
programming.increase: Increase by one dumbbell increment (about 2 kg) when every set reaches 12 reps.
programming.maintain: Keep the load the same while reps are building; reduce it if the shoulder position becomes uncomfortable.

name: Hammer curl
musclesText: Primary: brachialis, brachioradialis, biceps brachii. Secondary: wrist flexors and extensors as grip stabilisers.

steps.start: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing your thighs.
steps.setup: Pick a matched pair of dumbbells and step away from the rack into clear space.
steps.feet: Stand with feet hip-width apart and knees slightly bent.
steps.grip: Hold both dumbbells in a neutral grip, thumbs pointing forward, and keep that grip for the whole rep.
steps.posture: Keep your chest up, shoulders down and back, and upper arms vertical by your sides.
steps.brace: Brace your abdominals so your torso does not rock as both dumbbells rise together.
steps.initiate: Start by bending both elbows at the same time while the upper arms stay still.
steps.concentric: Curl both dumbbells up with thumbs leading until the forearms are close to vertical, keeping the wrists straight and the elbows at your sides.
steps.breathing: Breathe out as you curl, breathe in as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower both dumbbells under control until your elbows are fully straight.
steps.rom: Full elbow extension to the point where the dumbbells are near shoulder height, without the elbows moving forward.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: two seconds down, one second up, a brief hold at the top.
steps.finish: Finish with arms straight, dumbbells by your thighs and posture unchanged.
steps.exit: Lower the dumbbells to your sides after the last rep and bend your knees to place them back on the rack.

mistakes.m: Rotating the palms up during the curl.
mistakes.fix: Keep the palms facing each other throughout; think of hammering a nail.

mistakes.m: Using hip drive to lift heavier dumbbells.
mistakes.fix: Lower the load or stand against a wall to keep the torso still.

mistakes.m: Letting the wrists bend under the weight.
mistakes.fix: Grip firmly and keep the knuckles in line with the forearm.

mistakes.m: Shortening the lowering phase.
mistakes.fix: Count two seconds down and fully straighten the elbows.

safety: The neutral grip is often comfortable for sore wrists, but stop if you feel sharp pain on the thumb side of the forearm.
Avoid heavy swinging that loads the lower back.
checks: Check adjustable dumbbell collars are tight.
Make sure there is space either side so the dumbbells do not hit anything.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if you need momentum to finish reps, if wrists bend, or if outer elbow discomfort develops.

programming.rehab: Light neutral-grip curls are often well tolerated during elbow or wrist rehabilitation; follow a physiotherapist's guidance for load and volume.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week, 48 h between hard arm sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Pick dumbbells you can curl together for 12 strict reps with two in reserve; most people handle a little more than on a supinated curl.
programming.judgeLoad: The final reps should slow down but the elbows and torso should not move.
programming.progression: Double progression from 8 to 12 reps.
programming.increase: Increase by 2 kg per hand once all sets reach 12 reps.
programming.maintain: Keep the load steady while reps are still increasing; reduce it if grip or wrist control fades before the elbows.

name: Cross-body hammer curl
musclesText: Primary: brachialis, brachioradialis. Secondary: biceps brachii, wrist stabilisers.

steps.start: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with a neutral grip.
steps.setup: Select a matched pair of dumbbells and stand in clear space with room in front of your chest.
steps.feet: Feet hip-width apart, knees soft, weight evenly spread.
steps.grip: Neutral grip with palms facing your body and thumbs forward; the grip stays neutral as the dumbbell crosses your body.
steps.posture: Stand upright with chest up, shoulders level and the working upper arm close to your side.
steps.brace: Brace your trunk so your shoulders stay square and do not rotate towards the working arm.
steps.initiate: Bend one elbow and start moving the dumbbell diagonally upwards across the front of your torso.
steps.concentric: Curl the dumbbell towards the opposite shoulder, keeping the palm facing your chest, until the forearm is angled across your body near the opposite collarbone; the upper arm stays close to your side.
steps.breathing: Exhale as the dumbbell crosses your body, inhale as it returns.
steps.eccentric: Lower the dumbbell along the same diagonal path back to your side until the elbow is straight, then repeat on the other arm.
steps.rom: From full extension at your side to the dumbbell reaching the opposite chest or shoulder line.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: two seconds down, one second up, short squeeze at the top.
steps.finish: Each rep ends with the arm straight by your side before switching arms.
steps.exit: Finish the set with both dumbbells at your sides, then bend your knees to rack them.

mistakes.m: Turning the torso to swing the dumbbell across.
mistakes.fix: Keep your chest facing forward and reduce the load.

mistakes.m: Letting the upper arm lift away from the body.
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbow close to the ribs and move only at the elbow joint.

mistakes.m: Curling straight up instead of across the body.
mistakes.fix: Aim the end of the dumbbell at the opposite shoulder on every rep.

mistakes.m: Rushing the lowering phase.
mistakes.fix: Take two seconds to return to full extension.

safety: Keep the load moderate; the diagonal path makes heavy weights easy to swing.
Stop if you feel sharp pain at the outer elbow or wrist.
checks: Make sure adjustable dumbbell collars are secure.
Check there is room in front of you so the dumbbell will not hit anything as it crosses.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if your torso rotates, the elbow lifts away from your side, or you cannot reach the opposite shoulder line under control.
progressions: Cross-body hammer curl with a 3-second lowering

programming.rehab: Light cross-body curls can be used in later elbow rehabilitation if pain free; check with a physiotherapist.
programming.frequency: 1-3 times per week, 48 h between hard arm sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Use dumbbells a little lighter than your standard hammer curl and aim for 12 strict reps per arm.
programming.judgeLoad: You should finish each set with one to two reps left and no torso rotation.
programming.progression: Double progression from 10 to 12 reps per arm.
programming.increase: Increase by 2 kg per hand when all sets reach 12 reps per arm.
programming.maintain: Keep the same dumbbells while reps are building; drop a size if the path starts to curve or swing.

name: EZ-bar preacher curl
musclesText: Primary: biceps brachii (short head emphasis), brachialis. Secondary: brachioradialis, wrist flexors.

steps.start: Sit at a preacher bench with the backs of your upper arms flat on the angled pad, holding an EZ bar at chest height.
steps.setup: Adjust the seat so the top of the pad sits in your armpits with your upper arms fully supported; load the EZ bar evenly and rest it on the bench's bar holders.
steps.feet: Place your feet flat on the floor or footrests, hip-width apart, to keep you stable on the seat.
steps.grip: Hold the EZ bar on the angled grips with palms facing up and slightly in, hands roughly shoulder-width apart.
steps.posture: Sit tall with your chest against the top edge of the pad and shoulders down; keep your triceps in contact with the pad throughout.
steps.brace: Lightly brace your trunk and avoid leaning back as the bar rises.
steps.initiate: Begin by curling the bar from the bottom position while keeping your elbows fixed on the pad.
steps.concentric: Curl the bar towards your chin until your forearms are about vertical, keeping your wrists straight on the angled grips.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower the bar slowly until your elbows are almost straight, keeping tension rather than letting the bar drop and hyperextend the elbows.
steps.rom: From just short of full lockout at the bottom to forearms near vertical at the top; going past vertical removes tension.
steps.tempo: 3-0-1-0: three seconds down, no pause, one second up.
steps.finish: Each rep finishes with the arms nearly straight and the triceps still on the pad.
steps.exit: After the last rep curl the bar back up to the holders and set it down, then stand up; never let go of the bar at full extension.

cues: Armpits snug to the top of the pad
Do not drop into the bottom

mistakes.m: Letting the bar drop quickly at the bottom so the elbows snap straight.
mistakes.fix: Slow the last third of the lowering and stop just short of locking out.

mistakes.m: Lifting the elbows off the pad and shrugging to finish reps.
mistakes.fix: Reduce the load and keep the triceps pressed into the pad.

mistakes.m: Seat set too low so the shoulders roll forward.
mistakes.fix: Raise the seat until the pad sits snugly under your armpits.

mistakes.m: Curling past vertical and resting at the top.
mistakes.fix: Stop when your forearms are vertical and start the next lowering.

safety: The bottom of a preacher curl places high stress on the biceps tendon; never bounce or drop into full extension with heavy loads.
Stop immediately if you feel a sudden sharp pain or a pop at the front of the elbow.
Return the bar to the holders rather than dropping it.
checks: Check the seat height is set and the pin is locked.
Confirm collars are tight on the EZ bar.
Make sure the bar holders are positioned so you can reach and return the bar easily.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if you cannot control the bottom third of the rep, if your elbows lift, or if the front of the elbow feels sore after sessions.
progressions: Preacher curl with a pause near the bottom

programming.rehab: Generally better avoided in early biceps tendon rehabilitation because of the loaded stretch; consult a physiotherapist before using it.
programming.frequency: 1-3 times per week, 48 h between hard biceps sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Start with the empty EZ bar or about 70 per cent of your standing EZ curl and aim for 12 controlled reps.
programming.judgeLoad: You should be able to control the bottom of every rep; if the bar speeds up as it lowers, it is too heavy.
programming.progression: Double progression within 8-12 reps.
programming.increase: Add 2.5 kg once every set reaches 12 reps with a controlled three-second lowering.
programming.maintain: Keep the load while reps or tempo control are still improving; reduce it if the elbows feel tender.

name: Single-arm dumbbell preacher curl
musclesText: Primary: biceps brachii, brachialis. Secondary: brachioradialis, wrist flexors.

steps.start: Sit or stand at a preacher bench with one upper arm flat on the pad, holding a dumbbell in that hand with the arm nearly straight.
steps.setup: Set the seat height so the top of the pad sits under your armpit; position yourself slightly to the side so the working arm runs straight down the centre of the pad.
steps.feet: Feet flat and hip-width apart on the floor; if standing, stagger your stance slightly for balance.
steps.grip: Hold the dumbbell in an underhand grip, palm facing up, with your hand centred on the handle; rest your free hand on the top of the pad or your working shoulder.
steps.posture: Keep your chest against the top edge of the pad, shoulder down and back, triceps flat on the pad.
steps.brace: Brace your trunk lightly so you do not lean back or twist as you curl.
steps.initiate: Start the curl by bending the elbow while the back of the upper arm stays on the pad.
steps.concentric: Curl the dumbbell up towards your shoulder until your forearm is about vertical, keeping the wrist straight and the palm facing you.
steps.breathing: Breathe out as you curl, breathe in as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower the dumbbell slowly until your elbow is nearly straight, keeping tension at the bottom.
steps.rom: From just short of full lockout to forearm vertical.
steps.tempo: 3-0-1-1: three seconds down, one second up, one second squeeze at the top.
steps.finish: Finish each rep nearly straight and in control; complete all reps on one arm before switching.
steps.exit: After the last rep curl the dumbbell up, take it with your free hand or set it on the floor carefully, then switch arms.

cues: Palm faces up all the way
Slow and controlled at the bottom

mistakes.m: Letting the dumbbell drop into full extension.
mistakes.fix: Slow down and stop just short of locking the elbow.

mistakes.m: Twisting the torso to help lift.
mistakes.fix: Keep your chest square on the pad and use a lighter dumbbell.

mistakes.m: Wrist curling inwards at the top.
mistakes.fix: Keep the wrist neutral and focus on bending the elbow.

mistakes.m: Placing the arm at an angle across the pad.
mistakes.fix: Line the upper arm up with the slope of the pad.

safety: Control the stretched bottom position to protect the biceps tendon.
Stop if you feel sharp pain at the front of the elbow.
Hand the dumbbell off carefully rather than dropping it.
checks: Check seat height and locking pin.
Make sure the dumbbell is within easy reach and the floor beside the bench is clear.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if the lowering speeds up near the bottom, the upper arm lifts, or one arm cannot match the other's reps.

programming.rehab: With a light dumbbell, a shortened bottom range and slow reps, it can help rebuild one-sided elbow flexor strength; agree the plan with a physiotherapist.
programming.frequency: 1-3 times per week, 48 h between hard biceps sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Start with a dumbbell you can curl 12 times per arm with a controlled three-second lowering.
programming.judgeLoad: The weaker arm should reach 1-2 reps in reserve without any twist or bounce.
programming.progression: Double progression in the 8-12 rep range per arm.
programming.increase: Increase by one dumbbell step (1-2 kg) when both arms complete 12 reps on all sets.
programming.maintain: Keep the load while the weaker arm catches up; reduce it if the bottom range becomes uncontrolled.

name: Machine preacher curl
musclesText: Primary: biceps brachii, brachialis. Secondary: brachioradialis.

steps.start: Sit in the preacher curl machine with your upper arms on the pad and your hands on the handles, arms nearly straight.
steps.setup: Set the seat so the top of the arm pad sits under your armpits and your elbows line up with the machine's pivot point (usually marked); select the weight with the pin.
steps.feet: Place your feet flat on the floor or footplate, hip-width apart.
steps.grip: Grip the handles with palms facing up, or use the angled handles if fitted, with a firm but relaxed grip.
steps.posture: Sit tall with your chest touching the top of the pad and shoulders down; keep your triceps flat on the pad.
steps.brace: Brace lightly and keep your hips on the seat so you do not lean back.
steps.initiate: Begin by bending your elbows, keeping them aligned with the pivot and in contact with the pad.
steps.concentric: Curl the handles up until your forearms are about vertical or the machine reaches its end range, keeping your wrists straight.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you curl, inhale as you return.
steps.eccentric: Lower the handles slowly until your arms are nearly straight, without letting the weight stack touch down between reps.
steps.rom: From nearly full extension to the top of the machine's arc; keep the stack just off resting at the bottom.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: two seconds down, one second up, a short squeeze at the top.
steps.finish: Finish each rep with arms nearly straight and the stack still hovering.
steps.exit: After the last rep lower the handles slowly until the stack rests, release the handles and stand up.

cues: Do not let the stack touch

mistakes.m: Elbows not lined up with the pivot, causing awkward strain.
mistakes.fix: Adjust the seat height until the elbow joint matches the machine's axis.

mistakes.m: Lifting the elbows off the pad to finish reps.
mistakes.fix: Reduce the weight and keep the triceps pressed down.

mistakes.m: Letting the stack crash at the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Lower in two seconds and stop just before the plates touch.

mistakes.m: Leaning back to drag the handles up.
mistakes.fix: Keep your chest on the pad throughout.

safety: Line the joint up with the pivot to keep force on the muscle rather than the elbow joint.
Do not let the arms snap into full extension under load.
checks: Check the selector pin is fully inserted.
Set and lock the seat height before loading.
Confirm the handles and cable or cam move smoothly through range.
reduceLoad: Reduce the weight if the stack slams, elbows leave the pad, or you cannot keep a two-second lowering.
regressions: Machine curl with a light pin setting

programming.rehab: A fixed path and small weight steps make it a useful option during elbow rehabilitation; start light and follow your physiotherapist's guidance.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week, 48 h between hard biceps sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Start a few pins below what feels heavy and choose the weight you can curl 15 times with two reps in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: The last reps should be slow but the elbows should stay on the pad and the stack should not crash.
programming.progression: Double progression from 10 to 15 reps.
programming.increase: Move up one pin (2.5-5 kg) when all sets reach 15 reps.
programming.maintain: Keep the pin the same while reps are rising; go back one pin if your form breaks after an increase.

name: Concentration curl
musclesText: Primary: biceps brachii (peak contraction emphasis), brachialis. Secondary: brachioradialis, wrist flexors.

steps.start: Sit on the end of a flat bench, lean forward and rest the back of your working upper arm against the inside of the same-side thigh, dumbbell hanging at arm's length.
steps.setup: Use a flat bench at a height that lets you sit with thighs roughly parallel to the floor, and have a single dumbbell ready by your foot.
steps.feet: Place your feet wider than shoulder-width, flat on the floor, so the thigh supports the arm.
steps.grip: Hold the dumbbell with an underhand grip, palm facing away from the thigh; place your free hand on the other knee for support.
steps.posture: Lean forward from the hips with a long, neutral spine; the elbow rests just above the inside of the knee on the thigh.
steps.brace: Brace lightly so your torso does not rise or rock as you curl.
steps.initiate: Begin by bending the elbow while the upper arm stays pressed into the thigh.
steps.concentric: Curl the dumbbell up towards the front of the same-side shoulder, keeping the palm up and the wrist straight, and squeeze at the top.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you curl, inhale as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower the dumbbell slowly until the arm is fully straight below you.
steps.rom: Full elbow extension to the point where the dumbbell nears the shoulder.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-2: two seconds down, one second up, two-second squeeze at the top.
steps.finish: Finish each rep with the arm straight and still braced on the thigh; complete one side before switching.
steps.exit: After the set lower the dumbbell to the floor between your feet, sit upright, and switch arms.

cues: Elbow braced on the inner thigh

mistakes.m: Using the thigh to push the arm up.
mistakes.fix: Keep the leg still and let the arm do all the work; lighten the dumbbell.

mistakes.m: Lifting the torso to help the curl.
mistakes.fix: Hold your chest angle and stop the set when it changes.

mistakes.m: Resting the elbow on top of the knee, which lets it slide.
mistakes.fix: Place the upper arm against the inner thigh just above the knee.

mistakes.m: Curling the wrist at the top.
mistakes.fix: Keep the wrist neutral and focus on the elbow bend.

safety: Keep your spine long while leaning forward to avoid rounding the lower back.
Stop if the inner elbow or upper arm develops sharp pain.
checks: Make sure the bench is stable and the right height.
Have the dumbbell on the floor within reach before sitting.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if the leg or torso starts helping, or if you cannot hold a squeeze at the top.
regressions: Light concentration curl with a slower tempo

programming.rehab: With light weights, the supported position makes it a reasonable option during late elbow rehabilitation; follow your physiotherapist's advice.
programming.frequency: 1-3 times per week, 48 h between hard biceps sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Choose a dumbbell you can curl 15 times per arm with a two-second squeeze at the top.
programming.judgeLoad: You should keep the squeeze and full extension on every rep with one to two reps left.
programming.progression: Double progression from 10 to 15 reps per arm.
programming.increase: Increase by one dumbbell step once both arms reach 15 reps on all sets.
programming.maintain: Keep the load the same while the squeeze can still be held; reduce it if the leg starts to assist.

name: Cable curl
musclesText: Primary: biceps brachii, brachialis. Secondary: brachioradialis, wrist flexors.

steps.start: Stand facing a low pulley holding an EZ or straight bar attachment at arm's length in front of your thighs.
steps.setup: Set the pulley to its lowest position and clip on an EZ bar (or straight bar) attachment; select the weight on the stack.
steps.feet: Stand about half a step back from the pulley with feet hip-width apart, knees soft, so the cable runs at a slight angle to your hands.
steps.grip: Hold the bar with palms up, on the angled grips of an EZ attachment or shoulder-width on a straight bar.
steps.posture: Stand upright, chest up, shoulders back and down, with upper arms by your sides.
steps.brace: Brace your abdominals and squeeze your glutes so the cable does not pull you forward.
steps.initiate: Start by bending at the elbows while the upper arms stay beside your torso.
steps.concentric: Curl the bar up towards your upper chest, keeping wrists straight and elbows close to your sides; the cable keeps tension right to the top.
steps.breathing: Exhale on the way up, inhale on the way down.
steps.eccentric: Lower the bar slowly until your arms are straight, keeping the stack from touching down.
steps.rom: From full elbow extension to the bar at upper chest height.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: two seconds down, one second up, short squeeze at the top.
steps.finish: Finish each rep with arms straight and the weight still suspended.
steps.exit: After the last rep let the bar return slowly until the stack rests, then step towards the pulley and let go.

cues: Do not let the stack rest

mistakes.m: Standing too far back so the cable pulls the elbows forward.
mistakes.fix: Stand closer to the pulley so the cable runs nearly vertical.

mistakes.m: Leaning back to finish heavy reps.
mistakes.fix: Reduce the load and keep the ribs down.

mistakes.m: Letting the stack touch between reps.
mistakes.fix: Stop the lowering just before the plates meet.

mistakes.m: Elbows drifting forward at the top.
mistakes.fix: Stop the curl at upper chest height with elbows still at your sides.

safety: Release the bar only after the stack has returned, so it does not snap back.
Avoid jerking the cable from a dead stop, which stresses the elbow.
checks: Check the attachment clip is fully closed on the cable.
Make sure the selector pin is pushed fully in.
Check the cable for fraying before use.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if you lean back, the stack touches between reps, or the elbows drift forward.
regressions: Cable curl with a light stack

programming.rehab: Small stack increments and smooth tension make cable curls a good choice in elbow rehabilitation; start light and follow your physiotherapist's guidance.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week, 48 h between hard biceps sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Choose a stack weight you can curl 15 times with two reps in reserve and no torso movement.
programming.judgeLoad: The last reps should slow down without leaning back or the stack touching.
programming.progression: Double progression from 10 to 15 reps.
programming.increase: Move up one plate on the stack when all sets reach 15 reps.
programming.maintain: Keep the weight the same while reps are still increasing; drop one plate if technique slips.

name: Bayesian cable curl
musclesText: Primary: biceps brachii (long head emphasised with the shoulder extended). Secondary: brachialis, brachioradialis.

steps.start: Stand facing away from a low pulley with one arm extended behind your torso, holding a single handle.
steps.setup: Set the pulley at its lowest position, attach a single D-handle and select a light weight.
steps.feet: Step forward one to two paces from the pulley into a staggered stance, opposite foot forward, so there is tension with your arm behind you.
steps.grip: Hold the handle with your palm facing forward in an underhand grip; the free hand can rest on your hip.
steps.posture: Stand tall with chest up and shoulders back; the working upper arm angles slightly behind the torso.
steps.brace: Brace your trunk so the cable does not pull your shoulder forward or rotate your torso.
steps.initiate: Start by bending the elbow while keeping the upper arm angled back behind your body.
steps.concentric: Curl the handle forward and up towards your shoulder, letting the elbow move forward only slightly at the very end.
steps.breathing: Breathe out as you curl, breathe in as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower the handle slowly until the elbow is straight and the arm is back behind you, feeling a stretch at the front of the upper arm.
steps.rom: From full extension with the arm behind you to the hand near the front of the shoulder.
steps.tempo: 3-0-1-0: three seconds down, no pause, one second up.
steps.finish: Each rep finishes with the arm straight behind you and your posture unchanged; complete all reps on one side before switching.
steps.exit: After the last rep step back towards the pulley to unload the cable, then release the handle.

mistakes.m: Letting the shoulder roll forward with the cable.
mistakes.fix: Keep your chest up and shoulder blade gently back.

mistakes.m: Swinging the elbow forward to start the curl.
mistakes.fix: Keep the upper arm behind the torso and reduce the load.

mistakes.m: Standing too close to the pulley so there is no tension at the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Step further forward until the arm is loaded when straight.

mistakes.m: Twisting the torso towards the working side.
mistakes.fix: Brace and keep the hips square.

safety: The stretched shoulder position can irritate the front of the shoulder; reduce the range or skip the exercise if it hurts.
Use moderate loads and avoid jerking out of the stretched bottom position.
checks: Check the D-handle clip is secure.
Confirm the selector pin is fully inserted and the pulley is at its lowest setting.
Make sure the area in front of you is clear for stepping.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if your shoulder rolls forward, the elbow swings, or you cannot control the stretch at the bottom.
progressions: Bayesian curl with a pause in the stretch

programming.frequency: 1-3 times per week, 48 h between hard biceps sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Start with a light stack weight you can curl 15 times per arm while keeping the arm behind you.
programming.judgeLoad: Aim for one to two reps in reserve with no shoulder rolling or torso twist.
programming.progression: Double progression from 10 to 15 reps per arm.
programming.increase: Increase by one plate when both arms reach 15 reps on all sets.
programming.maintain: Keep the load the same while reps are building; reduce it if the shoulder position feels strained.

name: Dumbbell spider curl
musclesText: Primary: biceps brachii (short head emphasis), brachialis. Secondary: brachioradialis.

steps.start: Lie face down on an incline bench with your chest on the pad and your arms hanging straight down towards the floor, a dumbbell in each hand.
steps.setup: Set an adjustable bench to about 30-45 degrees, high enough that the dumbbells hang without touching the floor.
steps.feet: Place your feet on the floor behind the bench, toes or balls of the feet pressing down for stability; stand on the footplate if one is fitted.
steps.grip: Hold the dumbbells with palms facing forward in an underhand grip.
steps.posture: Keep your chest on the pad with the top of the bench just below your collarbones; arms hang vertically from the shoulders.
steps.brace: Lightly tighten your trunk and keep your chest pressed into the pad so you do not lift off.
steps.initiate: Begin by bending the elbows while the upper arms stay vertical.
steps.concentric: Curl both dumbbells up towards your shoulders, squeezing hard at the top, without letting the elbows swing forward.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you curl, inhale as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower the dumbbells slowly until your arms are straight and vertical again.
steps.rom: From full extension with arms hanging to full flexion; tension is greatest at the top of this curl.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-2: two seconds down, one second up, two-second squeeze at the top.
steps.finish: Finish each rep with arms hanging straight and your chest still on the pad.
steps.exit: After the last rep lower the dumbbells, place them on the floor beside the bench, then push yourself up off the pad.

mistakes.m: Swinging the elbows forward to lift the dumbbells.
mistakes.fix: Keep the upper arms vertical and use lighter dumbbells.

mistakes.m: Lifting the chest off the bench.
mistakes.fix: Press your chest into the pad and stop the set when you cannot.

mistakes.m: Bench too low so the dumbbells hit the floor.
mistakes.fix: Raise the bench angle or the bench height.

mistakes.m: Half reps at the top only.
mistakes.fix: Fully straighten the arms on each lowering.

safety: Lying chest-down can be uncomfortable straight after eating; leave time after meals.
Set the dumbbells down before climbing off the bench.
checks: Check the bench back is locked at the chosen angle.
Make sure the dumbbells clear the floor when your arms hang straight.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if the elbows swing forward, you lose the top squeeze, or your chest lifts off the pad.

programming.frequency: 1-3 times per week, 48 h between hard biceps sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Use dumbbells noticeably lighter than your standing curl, enough to hold a two-second squeeze at the top for 15 reps.
programming.judgeLoad: You should still achieve the top squeeze on the last rep with one to two reps in reserve.
programming.progression: Double progression from 10 to 15 reps.
programming.increase: Increase by one dumbbell step when all sets reach 15 reps.
programming.maintain: Keep the load the same while reps are climbing; reduce it if the elbows start moving.

name: Reverse curl
musclesText: Primary: brachioradialis, brachialis. Secondary: biceps brachii, wrist extensors (extensor carpi radialis).

steps.start: Stand tall holding an EZ bar or straight bar at arm's length against your thighs with an overhand grip.
steps.setup: Use an EZ bar if straight-bar wrist position is uncomfortable; load it lightly with collars, as this lift is much weaker than a normal curl.
steps.feet: Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees soft.
steps.grip: Take an overhand (pronated) grip about shoulder-width apart, knuckles facing forward; on an EZ bar use the outer or inner angled grips that keep your wrists comfortable.
steps.posture: Stand upright with chest up, shoulders down and back, and upper arms by your sides.
steps.brace: Brace your trunk and squeeze your glutes to prevent leaning back.
steps.initiate: Start by bending at the elbows while keeping your wrists straight and knuckles pointing forward.
steps.concentric: Curl the bar up until your forearms are about vertical, keeping the backs of your hands in line with your forearms rather than letting the wrists drop.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower the bar slowly until your elbows are fully straight.
steps.rom: From full elbow extension to forearms near vertical; the bar usually reaches mid to upper chest height.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: two seconds down, one second up, short hold at the top.
steps.finish: Finish each rep with arms straight and wrists still neutral.
steps.exit: After the last rep hold the bar at your thighs, bend your knees with a flat back and return it to the rack or floor.

mistakes.m: Wrists bending back under the bar.
mistakes.fix: Grip tightly and keep the knuckles in line with the forearms; lighten the load.

mistakes.m: Using the same load as a normal curl and swinging.
mistakes.fix: Start with roughly half of your normal curl weight.

mistakes.m: Elbows flaring out to the sides.
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows tucked and pointing down.

mistakes.m: Cutting the range short at the bottom.
