mistakes.fix: Straighten the elbows fully before each rep.

safety: The overhand grip loads the wrist extensors; stop if you feel sharp pain at the outer elbow, which can flare tennis elbow.
Use an EZ bar if the straight bar strains your wrists.
checks: Confirm collars are tight.
Check the bar is evenly loaded.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if your wrists bend back, you lean back to finish reps, or outer elbow soreness develops.

programming.rehab: Very light reverse curls are sometimes used in rehabilitation for outer elbow pain, but only as directed by a physiotherapist.
programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week, 48 h between hard arm sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Start with about half your normal curl weight and aim for 15 strict reps.
programming.judgeLoad: Your wrists should stay straight to the last rep, with one to two reps in reserve.
programming.progression: Double progression from 10 to 15 reps.
programming.increase: Add 2.5 kg when all sets reach 15 reps with straight wrists.
programming.maintain: Keep the load the same while reps are increasing; reduce it if outer elbow discomfort appears.

name: Zottman curl
musclesText: Primary: biceps brachii, brachialis, brachioradialis. Secondary: wrist extensors and flexors.

steps.start: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing forward.
steps.setup: Choose a light pair of dumbbells; the load is limited by the slow overhand lowering, not the curl up.
steps.feet: Stand with feet hip-width apart and knees soft.
steps.grip: Begin with an underhand grip, palms facing forward, hands centred on the handles.
steps.posture: Stand upright, chest up, shoulders down and upper arms at your sides.
steps.brace: Brace your trunk so your torso stays still through the rotation at the top.
steps.initiate: Start by curling both dumbbells up with palms facing up, keeping elbows at your sides.
steps.concentric: Curl until the forearms are near vertical, then at the top rotate your hands so the palms face forward and down into an overhand grip.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you curl up, hold your breath briefly through the rotation, then inhale slowly as you lower.
steps.eccentric: With the palms facing down, lower the dumbbells slowly for about three seconds until the arms are straight, then rotate back to palms up at the bottom.
steps.rom: Full elbow extension to full flexion, with the grip change only at the top and bottom positions.
steps.tempo: 1-1-3-0: one second up, one second to rotate at the top, three seconds down overhand, no pause.
steps.finish: Each rep ends with arms straight and palms turned back to face forward.
steps.exit: After the last rep lower both dumbbells to your sides and bend your knees to place them on the rack.

cues: Palms up on the way up
Palms down on the way down

mistakes.m: Rotating the hands during the curl instead of at the top.
mistakes.fix: Complete the curl first, then rotate.

mistakes.m: Dropping quickly in the overhand phase.
mistakes.fix: Take three seconds to lower and use a lighter weight.

mistakes.m: Swinging the torso to lift dumbbells that are too heavy for the lowering.
mistakes.fix: Choose the load for the overhand lowering, not the curl.

mistakes.m: Wrists bending back during the overhand lowering.
mistakes.fix: Keep the knuckles in line with the forearm.

safety: The slow pronated lowering can strain the outer elbow if the load is too heavy; stop with sharp pain.
Keep the trunk braced; do not twist to manage the rotation.
checks: Check the dumbbell heads or collars are secure.
Ensure you have space so the dumbbells do not collide as you rotate.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if you cannot control the three-second overhand lowering or your wrists bend back.

programming.rehab: Light Zottman curls can help in late rehabilitation for forearm and elbow strength if pain free; seek a physiotherapist's guidance.
programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week, 48 h between hard arm sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Pick dumbbells you can lower overhand for three seconds for 12 reps; this is usually lighter than your hammer curl.
programming.judgeLoad: The lowering on the final reps should still last three seconds with straight wrists.
programming.progression: Double progression from 8 to 12 reps.
programming.increase: Increase by one dumbbell step when all sets reach 12 controlled reps.
programming.maintain: Keep the same weight while tempo control improves; drop a size if the lowering speeds up.

name: Standing calf raise
musclesText: Primary: gastrocnemius (medial and lateral heads), soleus. Secondary: tibialis posterior, peroneals, foot intrinsic muscles.

steps.start: Stand on the platform of the standing calf-raise machine with the shoulder pads on top of your shoulders, knees straight but not locked, heels lowered slightly below the platform.
steps.setup: Adjust the shoulder pad height so you must bend your knees slightly to get under them; when you stand up the stack should lift just off its rest. Select the weight with the pin.
steps.feet: Place the balls of your feet on the edge of the platform, hip-width apart, toes pointing forward, heels hanging off.
steps.grip: Hold the machine's handles lightly for balance; your hands do not lift the weight.
steps.posture: Stand tall with knees straight but soft, hips under your shoulders and a neutral spine under the pads.
steps.brace: Brace your trunk to support the load through your shoulders and spine.
steps.initiate: From the stretched bottom position, push through the balls of your feet, especially the big toe, to begin rising.
steps.concentric: Rise as high as you can onto the balls of your feet, keeping the knees straight and the ankles from rolling outwards; pause briefly at the top.
steps.breathing: Breathe out as you rise, breathe in as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower your heels slowly below the platform until you feel a deep stretch in the calves, and hold the bottom for a moment without bouncing.
steps.rom: From a full stretch with heels below the platform to full height on the balls of the feet.
steps.tempo: 2-1-1-1: two seconds down, one-second pause in the stretch, one second up, one-second hold at the top.
steps.finish: Finish each rep with a controlled pause at the bottom before the next rise.
steps.exit: After the last rep lower your heels to platform level, bend your knees to set the stack down on its stops, then step out from under the pads.

mistakes.m: Bouncing out of the bottom using the Achilles tendon's stretch.
mistakes.fix: Pause for one full second at the bottom of each rep.

mistakes.m: Bending the knees to push the weight up.
mistakes.fix: Keep the knees soft but fixed so only the ankles move; lighten the load.

mistakes.m: Short reps in the middle of the range.
mistakes.fix: Lower fully and rise fully on every rep, even with less weight.

mistakes.m: Ankles rolling outwards onto the little toes.
mistakes.fix: Keep pressure through the big toe side of the foot.

safety: Heavy loads compress the spine through the shoulder pads; brace well and reduce the load if your back aches.
Avoid ballistic bouncing, which places high stress on the Achilles tendon.
Stop if you feel sharp pain in the Achilles or a sudden sensation in the calf.
checks: Check the shoulder pad height is set so the stack lifts only when you stand.
Confirm the selector pin is fully in.
Make sure the platform edge is dry and not slippery.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if you cannot reach the full stretch and full height, if you need to bend your knees, or if your Achilles feels sore the next day.
progressions: Standing calf raise with a 3-second pause

programming.rehab: Slow, light standing calf raises are commonly used in Achilles and calf rehabilitation; follow the loading plan set by your physiotherapist.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week; calves usually recover within 48 h.
programming.initialLoad: Start with a load you can lift 15 times through full range with a pause at the bottom and two reps in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: You should hold every pause and reach full height on the last reps; if the range shrinks, the load is too heavy.
programming.progression: Double progression from 10 to 15 reps, keeping the pauses.
programming.increase: Increase by one plate (about 5 kg) when all sets reach 15 full-range reps.
programming.maintain: Keep the load the same while reps are still rising; reduce it if your Achilles or plantar fascia feels irritated.

name: Seated calf raise
musclesText: Primary: soleus (emphasised with the knees bent). Secondary: gastrocnemius (reduced contribution), tibialis posterior, peroneals.

steps.start: Sit on the seated calf machine with the balls of your feet on the footplate edge and the knee pad snug across your lower thighs, just above the knees.
steps.setup: Adjust the knee pad so it presses on your lower thighs with your heels slightly below the footplate; load plates on the lever or select the weight, then release the safety stop.
steps.feet: Place the balls of your feet on the footplate, hip-width apart, toes forward and heels free to drop.
steps.grip: Hold the handles on the lever or the sides of the knee pad; do not pull with your arms.
steps.posture: Sit upright with knees bent to about 90 degrees and hips at the back of the seat.
steps.brace: Gently brace your trunk to keep your upper body still.
steps.initiate: Push through the balls of your feet to lift the pad slightly, then release the safety lever before starting the first rep.
steps.concentric: Rise onto the balls of your feet as high as you can, pressing through the big toe and keeping ankles from rolling out, and pause at the top.
steps.breathing: Breathe out as you rise, breathe in as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower your heels slowly until you feel a full stretch in the calves, pausing briefly at the bottom.
steps.rom: From a deep stretch with heels low to maximal height on the balls of the feet.
steps.tempo: 2-1-1-1: two seconds down, one-second pause at the bottom, one second up, one-second hold at the top.
steps.finish: Finish each rep with a controlled pause in the stretch.
steps.exit: After the final rep rise onto your toes, re-engage the safety stop, then lower and slide out from under the pad.

cues: Pad snug on the lower thighs

mistakes.m: Bouncing at the bottom of each rep.
mistakes.fix: Hold the stretch for a full second before rising.

mistakes.m: Forgetting to re-engage the safety stop before exiting.
mistakes.fix: Rise to the top on the last rep and flip the safety lever before moving your feet.

mistakes.m: Using the arms or torso to rock the pad up.
mistakes.fix: Keep your upper body relaxed and reduce the load.

mistakes.m: Partial reps around the middle.
mistakes.fix: Use the full range from stretch to peak contraction.

safety: Engage the safety stop whenever you get in or out to avoid the lever dropping onto your thighs.
Avoid bouncing, which stresses the Achilles tendon.
Stop if you feel sharp pain in the calf or heel.
checks: Check the knee pad is snug and locked at the right height.
Confirm plates are loaded evenly or the selector pin is fully in.
Test that the safety lever engages and releases smoothly.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if you cannot pause in the stretch, if the range shortens, or if heel or Achilles soreness lingers.
progressions: Seated calf raise with a 3-second pause at the bottom

programming.rehab: Seated calf raises are a common part of Achilles and soleus rehabilitation, progressing from light to heavy loads; follow your physiotherapist's plan.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week; the soleus recovers quickly from most sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Start with a load you can lift 20 times with full range and a pause at the bottom, leaving two reps in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: The final reps should burn and slow down but still reach full height with the pause intact.
programming.progression: Double progression from 12 to 20 reps.
programming.increase: Increase by about 5 kg once all sets reach 20 full reps.
programming.maintain: Keep the load the same while reps rise; reduce it if heel or Achilles discomfort appears.

name: Leg-press calf raise
musclesText: Primary: gastrocnemius, soleus. Secondary: tibialis posterior, peroneals.

steps.start: Sit in the leg press with your back flat on the pad, legs straight but not locked, and the balls of your feet on the bottom edge of the platform.
steps.setup: Load the leg press lightly at first. Press the platform up, keep the safety stops engaged or set as close as the machine allows, and slide your feet down so only the balls of the feet are on the bottom edge.
steps.feet: Feet hip-width apart, toes pointing straight ahead, heels hanging off the bottom edge of the platform.
steps.grip: Hold the side handles lightly to keep your hips in the seat.
steps.posture: Keep your back and hips flat against the pad and your knees straight but soft throughout.
steps.brace: Brace your trunk gently and keep your hips pinned to the seat.
steps.initiate: From the stretched position with heels towards you, push through the balls of your feet to begin pressing the platform away.
steps.concentric: Press the platform away by pointing your ankles as far as possible, keeping your knees fixed and the pressure through the big toes.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you press, inhale as you return.
steps.eccentric: Let the platform return slowly towards you until your ankles reach a full stretch, pausing briefly.
steps.rom: From full ankle dorsiflexion (stretch) to full plantar flexion, with no movement at the knees.
steps.tempo: 2-1-1-1: two seconds back, one-second pause in the stretch, one second press, one-second hold at full extension.
steps.finish: Finish each rep with a controlled stretch before pressing again.
steps.exit: After the last rep move your feet back up onto the middle of the platform, bend your knees slightly, engage the safety handles and then lower the sled to its rest.

cues: Balls of feet on the bottom edge

mistakes.m: Bending and straightening the knees to move the platform.
mistakes.fix: Keep the knees fixed with a slight bend and reduce the load.

mistakes.m: Feet placed too low so they risk slipping off.
mistakes.fix: Keep the balls of the feet firmly on the platform edge with plenty of contact.

mistakes.m: Racking the sled with feet still on the edge.
mistakes.fix: Move your feet back to the middle of the platform before engaging the safety handles.

mistakes.m: Bouncing the sled at the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Pause briefly in the stretch each rep.

safety: Never fully lock the knees under heavy load, and keep a slight bend throughout.
If a foot starts to slip, stop and reposition before continuing.
Avoid bouncing at the bottom to protect the Achilles tendon.
checks: Check that the safety stops engage and that you can reach the release handles.
Make sure the platform and your shoe soles are dry and not slippery.
Load plates evenly on both sides of the sled.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if your knees start to bend during reps, your feet slide, or you cannot reach a full stretch.

programming.rehab: Can be used in calf rehabilitation once a physiotherapist confirms you are ready for loaded calf work, starting with light loads.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week, with at least 48 h between hard calf sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Start well below your normal leg press load and pick a weight you can press through full ankle range for 15 reps.
programming.judgeLoad: The last reps should be hard but your knees must stay still and the stretch must be full.
programming.progression: Double progression from 10 to 15 reps.
programming.increase: Add 5-10 kg once all sets reach 15 full-range reps.
programming.maintain: Keep the load while reps are increasing; reduce it if foot position becomes insecure.

name: Single-leg calf raise
musclesText: Primary: gastrocnemius, soleus. Secondary: tibialis posterior, peroneals, foot intrinsic muscles, hip abductors for balance.

steps.start: Stand on one foot on a step with the ball of your foot on the edge and your heel hanging off, holding a rail for balance.
steps.setup: Use a sturdy stair, step or plyo box with a rail or wall to hold; hold a dumbbell in the hand on the working side if you need extra load.
steps.feet: Place the ball of the working foot on the step edge, toes forward; bend the other knee to lift the free foot behind you or hook it behind the working ankle.
steps.grip: Hold the rail lightly with one hand for balance only; the other hand holds the optional dumbbell by your side.
steps.posture: Stand tall with the working knee straight but soft and your hips level.
steps.brace: Brace your trunk and keep your pelvis level so you do not lean into the rail.
steps.initiate: From a full stretch with the heel below the step, push through the ball of the foot and big toe to start rising.
steps.concentric: Rise as high as you can onto the ball of the foot, keeping the ankle from rolling outwards, and hold the top briefly.
steps.breathing: Breathe out as you rise, breathe in as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower slowly until the heel is below the step and the calf is fully stretched, pausing without bouncing.
steps.rom: Heel fully below the step to as high as you can rise.
steps.tempo: 2-1-1-1: two seconds down, one-second pause at the bottom, one second up, one-second hold at the top.
steps.finish: Finish each rep in the stretched position; complete all reps on one leg, then switch.
steps.exit: After the last rep lower your heel to step level, place the other foot down, and set any dumbbell down before stepping off.

cues: Ball of foot on the edge

mistakes.m: Pulling on the rail to help lift the body.
mistakes.fix: Use only light fingertip pressure on the rail.

mistakes.m: Bending the knee to bounce up.
mistakes.fix: Keep the knee soft but still and pause at the bottom.

mistakes.m: Ankle rolling out onto the little toe.
mistakes.fix: Drive through the big toe and keep the knee over the second toe.

mistakes.m: Too little of the foot on the step so it slips.
mistakes.fix: Keep the whole ball of the foot in contact with the step edge.

safety: Use a stable step with a rail and dry footwear to avoid slipping.
Avoid bouncing to protect the Achilles tendon.
Stop if you feel sharp pain in the Achilles or calf.
checks: Check the step or box is stable and will not tip.
Make sure there is a rail or wall within reach.
If using a dumbbell, ensure you can hold it securely with a dry hand.
reduceLoad: Remove or reduce the dumbbell if you cannot reach full height, if the ankle rolls outwards, or if Achilles soreness lasts into the next day.
regressions: Double-leg calf raise on a step
Single-leg calf raise on flat ground
progressions: Single-leg calf raise holding a heavier dumbbell

programming.rehab: Slow single-leg calf raises are a staple of Achilles and calf rehabilitation; follow your physiotherapist's progression for range, tempo and load.
programming.frequency: 2-4 times per week, 48 h between hard sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Start with bodyweight only and check you can do 15 full-range reps per leg; add a light dumbbell once you exceed 20.
programming.judgeLoad: Both legs should reach similar reps with full height; the last reps should be hard but controlled.
programming.progression: Add reps first, then add a dumbbell and progress its weight.
programming.increase: Add or increase a dumbbell (about 2 kg) when you reach 20 full reps per leg on all sets.
programming.maintain: Keep the same load while either leg is still building reps; reduce it if one side's range shrinks.

name: Donkey calf raise
musclesText: Primary: gastrocnemius (emphasised in a lengthened position by hip flexion), soleus. Secondary: tibialis posterior, peroneals.

steps.start: Stand with the balls of your feet on a raised platform, hinge forward at the hips with a flat back so your torso is roughly parallel to the floor, and support your upper body on the machine handles or a bench, with the load on your hips.
steps.setup: On a donkey calf machine, set the pad so it sits across your lower back and hips. Without a machine, stand on a step or block in front of a bench and rest your forearms on it, with a weight plate or loaded belt on your hips or a training partner sitting on your hips.
steps.feet: Feet hip-width apart, balls of the feet on the edge of the platform, toes forward, heels hanging off.
steps.grip: Hold the machine handles or rest your forearms on the bench to support your upper body.
steps.posture: Hinge from the hips with a long neutral spine, legs straight but knees soft, so the load sits over the hips rather than the lower back.
steps.brace: Brace your trunk firmly to keep your back flat under the load.
steps.initiate: From the stretched bottom position, push through the balls of your feet and big toes to start rising.
steps.concentric: Rise onto the balls of your feet as high as possible, keeping your knees still and the ankles from rolling out; pause at the top.
steps.breathing: Breathe out as you rise, breathe in as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower your heels slowly below the platform to a full stretch and pause briefly.
steps.rom: From a deep stretch to full height on the balls of the feet, knees unchanged.
steps.tempo: 2-1-1-1: two seconds down, one-second pause at the bottom, one second up, one-second hold at the top.
steps.finish: Finish each rep with a controlled pause in the stretch.
steps.exit: After the set lower to a neutral ankle, remove the load from your hips (or let your partner step off) and rise carefully out of the hinge before stepping down.

cues: Rise as high as you can

mistakes.m: Rounding the lower back under the load.
mistakes.fix: Keep a neutral spine, brace harder and reduce the load.

mistakes.m: Bending the knees to bounce.
mistakes.fix: Hold the knees still and pause at the bottom.

mistakes.m: Load placed on the lower back instead of the hips.
mistakes.fix: Position the pad or plate over the hip bones.

mistakes.m: Shortened range at the top.
mistakes.fix: Rise fully and hold for a second.

safety: Keep a neutral spine in the hinged position; skip this variation if it aggravates your lower back.
Make sure any plate on the hips is secure or held in place so it cannot slide off.
Avoid bouncing to protect the Achilles tendon.
checks: Check the platform or block is stable and non-slip.
Set the machine pad height or secure the hip load before starting.
Make sure the bench or handles are solid enough to lean on.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if your back rounds, the knees start bending, or you cannot reach a full stretch.
progressions: Donkey calf raise with a 3-second pause in the stretch

programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week, 48 h between hard calf sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Start with bodyweight or a light plate and pick a load you can lift for 15 full reps with a neutral back.
programming.judgeLoad: The last reps should be slow but reach full height without the knees bending or the back rounding.
programming.progression: Double progression from 10 to 15 reps.
programming.increase: Increase by about 5 kg once all sets reach 15 full-range reps.
programming.maintain: Keep the load while reps are rising; reduce it if your back position becomes hard to hold.

name: Smith machine calf raise
musclesText: Primary: gastrocnemius, soleus. Secondary: tibialis posterior, peroneals, trunk stabilisers.

steps.start: Stand under a Smith machine bar resting across your upper back, with the balls of your feet on a step or weight plate and heels hanging off.
steps.setup: Set the bar at about shoulder height, just below where you stand tall, so you can unrack it by rising slightly. Place a sturdy step or stacked plates under the bar so your feet sit directly under it. Set the safety stops just below the bar's lowest point in the rep.
steps.feet: Place the balls of your feet on the edge of the step, hip-width apart, toes forward, directly under the bar.
steps.grip: Grip the bar just outside shoulder-width with an overhand grip, as for a squat, and pull it into your upper back.
steps.posture: Stand tall with knees straight but soft, chest up and spine neutral under the bar.
steps.brace: Brace your trunk firmly to support the bar on your back.
steps.initiate: Rotate the bar to unhook it, then from the stretched position push through the balls of your feet to start rising.
steps.concentric: Rise as high as you can onto the balls of your feet with the knees still and the pressure through the big toes; pause at the top.
steps.breathing: Breathe out as you rise, breathe in as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower your heels slowly below the step to a full stretch and pause briefly.
steps.rom: Heels below the step to maximal height on the balls of the feet.
steps.tempo: 2-1-1-1: two seconds down, one-second pause at the bottom, one second up, one-second hold at the top.
steps.finish: Finish each rep with a controlled pause in the stretch.
steps.exit: After the last rep rise onto your toes, rotate the bar back onto the hooks, confirm it is locked, then duck out and step off.

cues: Hook the bar before stepping off

mistakes.m: Feet in front of or behind the bar so the step tilts.
mistakes.fix: Place the step so the balls of your feet sit directly under the bar.

mistakes.m: Bouncing out of the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Pause at the bottom for a full second.

mistakes.m: Using an unstable step or a single plate that slides.
mistakes.fix: Use a solid block or a plate stack that will not shift.

mistakes.m: Stepping off before the bar is fully hooked.
mistakes.fix: Rotate the bar onto the hooks and check it is locked first.

safety: Set the safety stops so the bar cannot fall far if you lose balance.
Use a stable, non-slip surface under your feet.
Avoid bouncing to protect the Achilles tendon.
checks: Set the bar height and safety stops before loading.
Check that the step or plates are stable and positioned directly under the bar.
Confirm plates are loaded evenly and collars are on.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if you cannot reach full height, the step shifts, or the bar feels uncomfortable on your back.

programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week, 48 h between hard calf sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Start with the empty bar or a light load and pick a weight you can lift for 15 full-range reps with a pause.
programming.judgeLoad: The final reps should still reach full height and hold the pause, with one to two reps in reserve.
programming.progression: Double progression from 10 to 15 reps.
programming.increase: Add 5 kg once all sets reach 15 full reps.
programming.maintain: Keep the load while reps are still building; reduce it if the bar position or balance feels insecure.

name: Rope triceps pushdown
musclesText: Primary: triceps brachii (lateral and medial heads, with long head contribution). Secondary: anconeus, wrist and forearm flexors for grip, rectus abdominis and obliques as torso stabilisers.

steps.start: Stand facing the high pulley holding the rope with your elbows bent to roughly 90 degrees and tucked against your sides.
steps.setup: Set the pulley at its highest position and clip on the rope attachment so both ends hang evenly. Choose a weight you can control for the full target reps.
steps.feet: Stand about a foot from the stack with feet hip-width apart, or take a short split stance if you prefer extra stability.
steps.grip: Hold the rope with a neutral grip (palms facing each other), hands just below the rubber stoppers so the ends can travel past your thighs.
steps.posture: Lean forward very slightly from the hips with a neutral spine, chest up and shoulders drawn down and back.
steps.brace: Brace your abdominals lightly and squeeze your glutes so your torso stays still while your arms move.
steps.initiate: Start the rep by pushing the rope down with your forearms only, keeping your upper arms pinned to your sides.
steps.concentric: Extend your elbows fully and, in the last few centimetres, pull the rope ends apart so your hands finish just outside your thighs.
steps.breathing: Breathe out as you press down and breathe in as the rope returns.
steps.eccentric: Let the rope rise under control until your forearms are just above parallel to the floor, without letting your elbows drift forward or up.
steps.rom: Move from about 90 degrees or slightly more of elbow bend to full lockout with the hands spread; the upper arm should not move.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: two seconds letting the rope rise, no pause, one second pressing down, a one-second squeeze with the rope split.
steps.finish: Finish each rep with arms straight, rope ends split and triceps squeezed hard for a moment.
steps.exit: After the last rep let the rope rise slowly to the start position, then step towards the stack so the weight touches down gently before letting go.

cues: Elbows stay glued to your sides
Split the rope at the bottom
Control the rope on the way up

mistakes.m: Elbows flaring and drifting forward so the shoulders and lats help push
mistakes.fix: Reduce the load and keep your upper arms fixed against your ribs throughout.

mistakes.m: Leaning over the rope and using bodyweight to drive it down
mistakes.fix: Stand taller with only a slight forward lean and pick a weight you can move with your arms alone.

mistakes.m: Stopping short of lockout
mistakes.fix: Finish every rep with the elbows fully straight and the rope ends pulled apart.

mistakes.m: Letting the stack yank the hands up past the chest
mistakes.fix: Stop the return when your forearms reach just above parallel and keep the weight moving slowly.

safety: Stop if you feel sharp pain at the back of the elbow; adjust grip width or try the straight-bar version, and see a professional if it persists.
Keep the wrists neutral rather than bent back, to reduce strain on the forearm tendons.
Avoid locking out violently; finish firmly but smoothly to protect the elbow joint.
checks: Check that the rope is fully seated in the carabiner and the carabiner gate is closed.
Confirm the pin is fully inserted in the stack and the pulley is locked at the top position.
Check the rope for fraying and that the end stoppers are secure.
reduceLoad: Reduce the weight if your elbows leave your sides, you need to lean or swing to complete reps, you cannot reach full lockout, or you feel elbow pain rather than triceps fatigue.

programming.rehab: A light rope pushdown with a slow tempo is often used to reload the triceps after an elbow niggle; follow your physiotherapist's guidance on load and range.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week for the triceps, at least 48 h between hard sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Start with a weight you could lift for about 15 strict reps, then settle into the 10-15 range.
programming.judgeLoad: The final 1-2 reps should be hard but still strict, with elbows fixed and full lockout; if the torso starts to rock, the load is too heavy.
programming.progression: Use double progression: work up to the top of the rep range on all sets before adding one plate on the stack.
programming.increase: Increase the load when you complete all sets at the top of the range with clean form and 1-2 reps in reserve.
programming.maintain: Keep the load the same if any set falls below the bottom of the range, and reduce it if elbow discomfort appears.

name: Straight-bar triceps pushdown
musclesText: Primary: triceps brachii (lateral and medial heads, plus the long head). Secondary: anconeus, forearm flexors and extensors for the overhand grip, rectus abdominis as a stabiliser.

steps.start: Stand close to the high pulley holding the bar at about chest height with elbows bent and tucked into your sides.
steps.setup: Set the pulley to the top and attach a straight bar (a short straight bar or the standard pushdown bar). Select a load you can control for the full set.
steps.feet: Stand with feet hip-width apart and close enough that the cable runs almost vertically in front of your face.
steps.grip: Take an overhand (pronated) grip about shoulder-width or slightly narrower, thumbs wrapped around the bar and wrists straight.
steps.posture: Stand tall with a slight hip hinge, chest up, shoulder blades set down and back.
steps.brace: Brace your midsection lightly so your torso does not rock forward as you push.
steps.initiate: Push the bar down by straightening your elbows, keeping your upper arms still against your sides.
steps.concentric: Drive the bar down in an arc until it touches or nearly touches the front of your thighs with your elbows fully extended.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you press the bar down, inhale as it rises.
steps.eccentric: Let the bar rise slowly until your forearms are just above parallel to the floor, elbows staying at your sides.
steps.rom: Full elbow extension at the bottom to about 90 degrees or a little more at the top; the bar should not rise above chest height.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: two seconds letting the bar rise, no pause, one second pressing down, a one-second squeeze at lockout.
steps.finish: Finish each rep with locked elbows, bar at your thighs and triceps fully contracted.
steps.exit: Return the bar to the start slowly after the final rep, then step forward towards the stack so the plates settle before releasing the bar.

cues: Push the bar into your thighs

mistakes.m: Letting the elbows travel forward and up on the return
mistakes.fix: Stop each return at forearms parallel and keep your upper arms against your sides.

mistakes.m: Bending the wrists back so the bar rolls into the fingers
mistakes.fix: Grip firmly with the bar over the heel of the palm and the wrist stacked over the forearm.

mistakes.m: Using a forward lean and shoulder push to move heavy weights
mistakes.fix: Reduce the load and keep only a slight, constant lean.

mistakes.m: Gripping too wide, which shifts tension to the shoulders
mistakes.fix: Keep hands about shoulder-width or a touch narrower.

safety: The fixed overhand grip can irritate the elbows or wrists in some lifters; switch to a rope or angled bar if you feel joint pain.
Do not jerk the bar down from a high start position, which loads the shoulders and elbows abruptly.
Stop if pain is sharp or localised at the elbow rather than a muscular burn.
checks: Make sure the bar attachment is securely clipped and the carabiner is closed.
Check the stack pin is fully inserted and the cable runs smoothly without catching.
Wipe the bar if it is slippery so your grip does not fail mid-set.
reduceLoad: Reduce the weight if your torso leans heavily, elbows lift off your sides, you cannot lock out, or wrist or elbow joints ache during the set.

programming.rehab: Light, controlled sets can be used to rebuild triceps tolerance after elbow issues; work with a physiotherapist and keep the range pain-free.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week, with 48 h between hard triceps sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Pick a load you could lift for about 12-15 strict reps and use it for the first sessions.
programming.judgeLoad: You should finish each set with 1-2 reps in reserve and no change in elbow position or torso angle.
programming.progression: Double progression: build to the top of the rep range on all sets, then add the smallest stack increment.
programming.increase: Add load when every set reaches the top of the range with full lockout and controlled returns.
programming.maintain: Hold the load if reps drop below the range or form slips; reduce it if the elbows or wrists become sore.

name: Overhead cable triceps extension
musclesText: Primary: triceps brachii with emphasis on the long head due to the overhead arm position. Secondary: anconeus, rectus abdominis and obliques resisting extension, anterior deltoid and serratus anterior holding the arms up.

steps.start: Stand facing away from the pulley in a split stance with the rope behind your head, elbows bent and pointing forward and up.
steps.setup: Set the pulley at about head height or slightly lower, and attach a rope (or a straight or EZ bar if preferred). Pick a light load first; this position feels much harder than pushdowns.
steps.feet: Take a staggered stance with one foot forward and knees soft, so you can lean slightly into the cable without losing balance.
steps.grip: Grip the rope ends with a neutral grip, hands next to each other behind your head, elbows roughly shoulder-width apart.
steps.posture: Lean your torso forward slightly from the hips so it is in line with the rear leg, keeping ribs down and spine neutral rather than arched.
steps.brace: Brace your abdominals firmly so the weight pulling backwards does not arch your lower back.
steps.initiate: Begin by straightening your elbows, keeping your upper arms beside your head and pointed forwards.
steps.concentric: Extend the elbows fully so the rope ends finish in front of and slightly above your head, separating the rope slightly at lockout.
steps.breathing: Breathe out as you extend and breathe in as you lower the rope behind your head.
steps.eccentric: Bend your elbows slowly to let the rope travel back behind your head until you feel a deep stretch in the back of your arms.
steps.rom: Go from a full stretch with the hands behind the head to full lockout, staying within a range that is comfortable for your shoulders.
steps.tempo: 3-1-1-0: three seconds lowering into the stretch, a one-second pause, and one second to extend.
steps.finish: Finish each rep with arms straight overhead in line with your torso and triceps squeezed.
steps.exit: After the final rep, bring the rope down beside your head with bent elbows, step back towards the pulley to unload the cable, then release it.

mistakes.m: Arching the lower back to push the weight
mistakes.fix: Brace harder, tuck the ribs down and use a split stance with a slight forward lean.

mistakes.m: Elbows flaring wide
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows about shoulder-width and pointing forward; reduce load if needed.

mistakes.m: Moving the upper arm to turn it into a pullover
mistakes.fix: Fix the upper arm beside your head and move only at the elbow.

mistakes.m: Cutting the stretch short
mistakes.fix: Lower until the hands are well behind the head, as far as your shoulders allow comfortably.

safety: Getting into and out of position with a heavy load can strain the shoulders; walk out with a manageable weight.
Avoid this variation if overhead positions cause shoulder pain; try a pushdown instead.
Keep the stretch controlled rather than bouncing, as the elbow and long-head tendon are under tension.
checks: Check the pulley height is locked and the rope is secured in a closed carabiner.
Make sure there is room behind and around you to step out.
Confirm the stack pin is fully inserted.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if your back arches, the elbows flare wide, you cannot get a full stretch, or the shoulder or elbow hurts in the bottom position.

programming.frequency: 1-3 times per week, ideally paired with a pushdown variation for full triceps development.
programming.initialLoad: Start with a load you can handle for 15 reps with a full stretch and no back arch.
programming.judgeLoad: The last reps should slow down but your torso and upper arms should stay still.
programming.progression: Double progression within 10-15 reps, then add one stack increment.
programming.increase: Increase load when all sets hit 15 reps with a full stretch and controlled tempo.
programming.maintain: Keep the load if reps fall short or the stretch shortens; reduce if shoulder or elbow discomfort appears.

name: Overhead dumbbell extension
musclesText: Primary: triceps brachii, particularly the long head stretched in the overhead position. Secondary: anconeus, anterior deltoid and serratus anterior to hold the arms overhead, core muscles for trunk stability.

steps.start: Sit on an upright bench with your back against the pad, holding one dumbbell with both hands at arm's length above your head.
steps.setup: Set an adjustable bench to its most upright position (about 80-90 degrees). Choose one dumbbell you can lift safely overhead.
steps.feet: Place your feet flat on the floor, slightly wider than hip-width, knees roughly over ankles.
steps.grip: Cup the top inner plate of the dumbbell with both palms, thumbs and fingers overlapping around the handle, so the dumbbell hangs vertically.
steps.posture: Keep your head, upper back and hips in contact with the pad, ribs down and lower back in its natural curve rather than arched off the pad.
steps.brace: Brace your core and press your back gently into the pad to stop your lower back arching as you lower the weight.
steps.initiate: Begin by bending your elbows to lower the dumbbell behind your head, keeping your upper arms close to your ears.
steps.concentric: Extend your elbows to press the dumbbell back up until your arms are straight overhead.
steps.breathing: Inhale as you lower the dumbbell, exhale as you press it up.
steps.eccentric: Lower slowly behind your head until your forearms are just past parallel to the floor or you feel a strong stretch in the triceps.
steps.rom: From full lockout to a deep stretch behind the head, as far as your shoulders allow without the elbows flaring or the back arching.
steps.tempo: 3-0-1-1: three seconds down, no pause, one second up, a one-second squeeze at the top.
steps.finish: Finish with arms straight and the dumbbell directly above your head.
steps.exit: Bring the dumbbell down in front of your face with bent elbows to your chest, then lower it to your thigh and onto the floor. For heavy weights, kick it up and down off your knee.

mistakes.m: Elbows flaring out wide
mistakes.fix: Keep elbows narrow and pointed forward; drop the weight if you cannot.

mistakes.m: Arching the lower back off the pad
mistakes.fix: Brace, keep ribs down and reduce the load.

mistakes.m: Shallow reps that skip the stretch
mistakes.fix: Lower until forearms are at least parallel to the floor if your shoulders allow.

mistakes.m: Insecure grip with the dumbbell tilting
mistakes.fix: Cup the inner plate with both palms and keep the handle vertical.

safety: Use a dumbbell with secure, fixed plates; never use loose-collared dumbbells overhead.
Avoid or modify if you have shoulder pain in overhead positions.
Lower the weight slowly; a fast drop behind the head stresses the elbow and can strike your neck.
checks: Check the dumbbell plates or head are tight and not rattling.
Lock the bench back pad at the upright angle.
Make sure the floor around the bench is clear.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if your back arches, elbows flare, you cannot get past 90 degrees of elbow bend, or you feel elbow or shoulder pain.

programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week, 48-72 h between hard triceps sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Start with a dumbbell you could lower and press for about 15 controlled reps.
programming.judgeLoad: Your final rep should be slow but complete, with no elbow flare or back arch.
programming.progression: Double progression in the 8-12 range, then move up 2-2.5 kg.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets reach 12 reps with full range and control.
programming.maintain: Keep the weight if reps fall below 8 or the range shortens; reduce if elbows feel sore after sessions.

name: Dumbbell skull crusher
musclesText: Primary: triceps brachii (all three heads, long head moderately stretched). Secondary: anconeus, forearm muscles gripping the dumbbells, and the shoulder stabilisers holding the upper arms in place.

steps.start: Lie on your back on a flat bench holding two dumbbells at arm's length above your shoulders, palms facing each other.
steps.setup: Use a flat bench and a pair of dumbbells you can control above your face. Sit on the end of the bench with the dumbbells on your thighs before lying back.
steps.feet: Place your feet flat on the floor either side of the bench, slightly wider than hip-width, to keep you stable.
steps.grip: Hold each dumbbell with a neutral grip (palms facing in), handles parallel, wrists straight and stacked over the forearms.
steps.posture: Keep your head, upper back and glutes on the bench with a small natural arch, and tilt your upper arms back slightly from vertical so the triceps stay loaded at the top.
steps.brace: Brace your abdominals and keep your ribs down so your lower back does not over-arch as the weights move.
steps.initiate: Bend only at the elbows to lower the dumbbells towards the sides of your head, keeping your upper arms still.
steps.concentric: Straighten your elbows to press the dumbbells back to the start, squeezing the triceps without letting the dumbbells touch.
steps.breathing: Inhale as you lower the dumbbells and exhale as you press them back up.
steps.eccentric: Lower slowly until the dumbbells are beside your ears or temples, just above the bench, elbows pointing to the ceiling.
steps.rom: Full elbow extension to roughly 90-120 degrees of elbow bend, with the dumbbells finishing beside the head rather than over the face.
steps.tempo: 3-0-1-0: three seconds down, no pause, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish each rep with the elbows nearly locked and the dumbbells over your upper chest or forehead.
steps.exit: Bring the dumbbells down to your chest with bent elbows, then rock up to sitting with them resting on your thighs, or lower them to the floor beside the bench under control.

cues: Keep a slight backward tilt of the arms

mistakes.m: Upper arms swinging, turning it into a press or pullover
mistakes.fix: Fix the upper arms and lighten the load so only the elbows move.

mistakes.m: Elbows flaring outwards
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows in line with your shoulders and pointing to the ceiling.

mistakes.m: Dropping the dumbbells quickly towards the head
mistakes.fix: Use a slow three-second lowering and stop beside the head.

mistakes.m: Wrists bending back under the load
mistakes.fix: Keep the knuckles pointing up and the wrists straight.

safety: Always control the lowering; the dumbbells travel close to your head.
Stop if you feel sharp pain at the elbow; reduce load or switch to a cable variation.
Get into and out of position safely using your thighs; do not swing heavy dumbbells over your face.
checks: Check the dumbbells are secure with no loose plates or collars.
Make sure the bench is stable and the area beside it is clear for setting the dumbbells down.
Choose matching dumbbells of the same weight.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if the upper arms drift, you cannot control the lowering, the dumbbells wobble near your head, or you get elbow pain.

programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week, 48-72 h between hard triceps work.
programming.initialLoad: Start with light dumbbells you could lift for 15 slow reps; most people need much less than they expect.
programming.judgeLoad: Stop the set when the upper arms start to move or the lowering speeds up; aim for 1-2 reps in reserve.
programming.progression: Double progression in the 8-12 range, then increase each dumbbell by the smallest jump available.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets reach 12 controlled reps.
programming.maintain: Keep the load if reps fall below 8, and reduce it if the elbows ache after training.

name: EZ-bar lying triceps extension
musclesText: Primary: triceps brachii with emphasis on the long head, which is lengthened as the bar travels behind the head. Secondary: anconeus, forearm flexors gripping the bar, and latissimus dorsi and teres major stabilising the upper arm.
aliases: lying triceps extension behind the head

steps.start: Lie on a flat bench holding the EZ bar at arm's length above your forehead, upper arms angled slightly back towards your head.
steps.setup: Load the EZ bar with collars on both sides and use a flat bench. Sit on the end with the bar on your thighs, then lie back and press it up, or have a partner hand it to you.
steps.feet: Plant your feet flat on the floor, wider than the bench, to stay stable.
steps.grip: Hold the inner angled parts of the EZ bar with an overhand, semi-pronated grip, hands about 15-20 cm apart and thumbs wrapped.
steps.posture: Keep your head, upper back and hips on the bench and your ribs down; let your upper arms tilt back about 20-30 degrees from vertical.
steps.brace: Brace your core so the lower back stays in a neutral position as the bar travels behind your head.
steps.initiate: Begin by bending your elbows and letting the bar travel back past your forehead, allowing the upper arms to drift back slightly to increase the stretch.
steps.concentric: Extend the elbows to bring the bar back up and over your forehead, returning the upper arms to their start angle.
steps.breathing: Inhale as you lower the bar behind your head, exhale as you press it back.
steps.eccentric: Lower slowly until the bar is behind the top of your head, close to bench level, with a strong stretch in the back of the arms.
steps.rom: From near lockout above the forehead to the bar behind the head at about bench height, with the elbows staying shoulder-width.
steps.tempo: 3-1-1-0: three seconds down, a one-second pause in the stretch, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish with the elbows extended and the bar above your forehead, not over your chest, to keep tension on the triceps.
steps.exit: Bring the bar to your chest by bending the elbows and lowering the upper arms, then sit up with it on your thighs, or hand it to a spotter.

mistakes.m: Bringing the bar down to the forehead instead of behind the head
mistakes.fix: Let the upper arms tilt back slightly and lower the bar behind the head for the long-head stretch.

mistakes.m: Elbows flaring wide
mistakes.fix: Grip the narrower angle of the EZ bar and keep elbows shoulder-width.

mistakes.m: Turning it into a pullover with excessive shoulder movement
mistakes.fix: Allow only a small upper-arm drift; most motion must come from the elbow.

mistakes.m: Bouncing out of the bottom
mistakes.fix: Pause briefly in the stretch and extend smoothly.

safety: The bar passes over your face; always use collars and controlled movement.
The deep stretch loads the elbow and long-head tendon; build range and load gradually.
If you have shoulder mobility limits or pain overhead, shorten the range or choose a pushdown.
checks: Put collars on both sides of the EZ bar.
Check the bench is stable and that you can lie with your head at the end of the pad.
Consider a spotter for heavier loads.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if the elbows flare, the bar drifts towards your face, you cannot pause in the stretch, or the elbows or shoulders hurt.

programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week, 48-72 h between hard triceps sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Begin with the empty EZ bar or a light load to learn the behind-the-head path before adding weight.
programming.judgeLoad: The last reps should be slow with the bar still going fully behind the head; if range shrinks, stop.
programming.progression: Double progression, adding 2.5 kg total once the top of the range is reached on every set.
programming.increase: Increase load when all sets hit 12 reps with a controlled pause in the stretch.
programming.maintain: Keep the load if reps fall short or the elbows feel achy; reduce it if pain appears.

name: JM press
musclesText: Primary: triceps brachii (all heads, particularly the lateral and medial heads). Secondary: pectoralis major (sternal head), anterior deltoid, anconeus.

steps.start: Lie on a flat bench under the bar with the bar unracked and held over your upper chest with arms straight, as for a close-grip bench press.
steps.setup: Set the bench in a power rack with safety pins just above chest height when lying down, or use a Smith machine with the stops set. Set J-hooks so you can unrack with a slight elbow bend.
steps.feet: Feet flat on the floor and set slightly behind the knees so you can create a stable base.
steps.grip: Take an overhand grip about shoulder-width or slightly narrower, thumbs wrapped, wrists stacked over forearms.
steps.posture: Retract and depress your shoulder blades and keep a modest arch with head, upper back and glutes on the bench.
steps.brace: Take a breath, brace your core, and keep your upper back tight throughout.
steps.initiate: Lower by bending your elbows and letting the bar travel down and slightly back towards your upper chest or chin, with the elbows pointing forward towards your feet rather than flaring.
steps.concentric: Press the bar back up and forward by extending the elbows forcefully, returning the bar over your upper chest.
steps.breathing: Inhale and brace before lowering, hold your breath through the bottom, and exhale past the hardest part of the press.
steps.eccentric: Lower until your forearms are roughly vertical-to-angled with the bar a few centimetres above your chin or upper chest, letting the forearms rest lightly against the upper arms (biceps) at the bottom.
steps.rom: From lockout to the point where forearms meet biceps above the chin, not touching the throat or face; shorten the range if the elbows complain.
steps.tempo: 3-0-1-0: three seconds down, no pause, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish with elbows locked and the bar stacked over your shoulders.
steps.exit: After the last rep, press to lockout and guide the bar back into the J-hooks, or rotate the Smith bar to engage the hooks; use the pins if you fail.

mistakes.m: Turning it into a normal close-grip bench press
mistakes.fix: Let the bar come down towards the chin and keep the elbows travelling forward.

mistakes.m: Turning it into a skull crusher with the elbows fixed
mistakes.fix: Allow the upper arm to lower as the elbows bend; it is a hybrid movement.

mistakes.m: Flaring the elbows wide
mistakes.fix: Keep elbows tucked and pointed towards your feet.

mistakes.m: Using too much load too early
mistakes.fix: Start light; the movement stresses the elbows and needs practice.

safety: Always use safety pins or a Smith machine; the bar path ends near your face and throat.
The elbows take high stress; avoid if you have current elbow pain, and build volume gradually.
Never use a thumbless grip on this lift.
checks: Set safety pins or Smith stops just above the lowest bar position.
Use collars on the barbell.
Check your grip is even by using the knurling marks.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if the bar path wanders, elbows flare, you lose upper-back tightness, or you feel elbow pain during or after the session.

programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week, at least 72 h apart if paired with heavy pressing.
programming.initialLoad: Start at about 40-50% of your close-grip bench press and refine the groove before progressing.
programming.judgeLoad: Bar speed should stay steady and the path consistent; stop the set if it slows dramatically or elbows flare.
programming.progression: Double progression, adding 2.5 kg once all sets hit the top of the rep range.
programming.increase: Increase when every set reaches the top of the range with consistent bar path and no elbow pain.
programming.maintain: Hold or reduce the load if the elbows feel irritated or technique varies from rep to rep.

name: Assisted triceps dip
musclesText: Primary: triceps brachii. Secondary: pectoralis major (lower fibres), anterior deltoid, rhomboids and lower trapezius stabilising the shoulder blades.

steps.start: Kneel on the assisted dip pad with straight arms supporting you on the handles, shoulders over hands and torso upright.
steps.setup: Set the counterweight: more weight on the stack gives more help. Begin with enough assistance to complete your reps with good form. Set the handles to the dip position if they rotate.
steps.feet: Kneel (or stand, depending on the model) on the pad with knees hip-width apart and shins hanging behind you without swinging.
steps.grip: Grip the parallel handles with a neutral grip, hands about shoulder-width, wrists stacked over forearms.
steps.posture: Keep your torso upright with only a slight forward lean, chest up and shoulders pulled down away from your ears.
steps.brace: Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your body moves as one unit.
steps.initiate: Bend your elbows and lower your body straight down, keeping the elbows pointing backwards.
steps.concentric: Press through your palms to straighten your elbows and push yourself back to the top.
steps.breathing: Inhale on the way down and exhale as you press up.
steps.eccentric: Lower under control until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor or slightly above, or as far as your shoulders tolerate.
steps.rom: From full elbow lockout to roughly 90 degrees of elbow bend; do not sink further if the front of the shoulder feels strained.
steps.tempo: 2-1-1-0: two seconds down, a one-second pause at the bottom, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish at the top with elbows locked and shoulders depressed, not shrugged.
steps.exit: At the top of your last rep, step one foot carefully onto the step, then the other, before letting go of the handles.

mistakes.m: Shrugging the shoulders up at the bottom
mistakes.fix: Stop higher and keep pressing the shoulders down.

mistakes.m: Leaning far forward, shifting work to the chest
mistakes.fix: Stay more upright to keep the emphasis on the triceps.

mistakes.m: Elbows flaring wide
mistakes.fix: Keep elbows tracking backwards.

mistakes.m: Dropping quickly into the bottom
mistakes.fix: Lower over two seconds and pause briefly.

safety: Do not go deeper than your shoulders allow; deep dips can irritate the front of the shoulder.
Step off carefully; releasing the knee pad suddenly can cause the platform to spring up.
Stop if you feel pain in the front of the shoulder or sternum.
checks: Check the counterweight pin is fully inserted.
Make sure the knee pad moves freely and the step is dry.
Adjust handle position and confirm they are locked.
reduceLoad: Increase assistance (more counterweight) if you cannot reach elbows at 90 degrees, shoulders shrug, or you feel shoulder pain.

programming.frequency: 2 times per week, 48-72 h apart.
programming.initialLoad: Choose an assistance setting that lets you do 10-12 controlled reps.
programming.judgeLoad: Reps should be smooth with a controlled descent; if you need to bounce or shrug, add more assistance.
programming.progression: Double progression, then reduce the assistance by one stack increment.
programming.increase: Reduce assistance when all sets reach the top of the range with good form.
programming.maintain: Keep assistance unchanged if reps fall below target, and add assistance if shoulders feel uncomfortable.

name: Bench dip
musclesText: Primary: triceps brachii. Secondary: anterior deltoid, pectoralis major (clavicular and sternal portions), with the shoulder stabilisers working to control the position.

steps.start: Sit on the edge of a bench, place your hands beside your hips, then slide your hips forward off the bench supported by straight arms.
steps.setup: Use a stable flat bench or sturdy box that will not slide. Position yourself at its long edge.
steps.feet: Begin with knees bent at 90 degrees and feet flat on the floor; straighten your legs only once the bent-knee version is easy and pain-free.
steps.grip: Place your hands shoulder-width apart on the edge of the bench, fingers pointing forward and gripping the edge.
steps.posture: Keep your back close to the bench, chest up and shoulders pulled down and back, not rolled forward.
steps.brace: Brace your core and keep your hips just in front of the bench throughout.
steps.initiate: Bend your elbows to lower your hips straight down, keeping your back close to the bench.
steps.concentric: Press through the heels of your hands to straighten your elbows and lift back to the start.
steps.breathing: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you press up.
steps.eccentric: Lower slowly until the upper arms are no lower than parallel to the floor, or stop earlier if you feel the front of the shoulders stretch uncomfortably.
steps.rom: Keep the range short: elbows bent to about 90 degrees at most. Going deeper forces the shoulders into extreme extension and internal rotation.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-0: two seconds down, no pause, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish with straight elbows and shoulders depressed.
steps.exit: After the last rep, step your feet in towards the bench and sit back onto it before releasing your hands.

mistakes.m: Dropping too low so the shoulders roll forward
mistakes.fix: Stop when the upper arms are parallel to the floor or higher.

mistakes.m: Hips drifting away from the bench
mistakes.fix: Keep your back brushing the bench edge.

mistakes.m: Elbows flaring outwards
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows pointing straight back.

mistakes.m: Shrugging the shoulders up towards the ears
mistakes.fix: Pull the shoulders down actively; shorten the range if you cannot.

safety: Bench dips place the shoulder in combined extension and internal rotation under bodyweight, which can irritate the front of the shoulder, the rotator cuff and the acromioclavicular joint; avoid them if you have a history of shoulder impingement, instability or AC joint pain.
Stop immediately if you feel sharp or pinching pain at the front or top of the shoulder, clicking with pain, or tingling into the arm; do not push through it.
Keep the depth to 90 degrees of elbow bend or less, and do not add plates on the lap until bodyweight reps are easy and pain-free.
Wrists are loaded in extension; switch to pushdowns if your wrists hurt.
checks: Make sure the bench is stable and will not tip or slide.
Check the bench edge is not slippery and your hands have secure contact.
Clear the floor around your feet.
reduceLoad: Make it easier by bending the knees more and bringing feet closer, or reduce the depth, if you cannot control the lowering or feel any shoulder discomfort.

programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Start with bent knees and a partial range, and only straighten the legs when 15 pain-free reps are easy.
programming.judgeLoad: Reps should be controlled and comfortable for the shoulders; any shoulder pinching means the variation is too hard.
programming.progression: Add reps first, then move the feet further out; avoid adding external load unless shoulders are healthy and fully comfortable.
programming.increase: Progress when you complete 15 controlled reps on all sets without shoulder discomfort.
programming.maintain: Hold or regress if shoulders feel achy after sessions or depth control slips.

name: Single-arm cable pushdown
musclesText: Primary: triceps brachii (lateral and medial heads, with long head assistance). Secondary: anconeus, forearm muscles gripping the handle, obliques resisting rotation.

steps.start: Stand side-on or facing the high pulley holding a D-handle in one hand, elbow bent to about 90 degrees and tucked at your side.
steps.setup: Set the pulley at the top and attach a single D-handle. Use a light stack weight; one arm handles far less than a two-handed pushdown.
steps.feet: Stand with feet hip-width apart, or with the same-side foot slightly back, close to the stack.
steps.grip: Hold the D-handle with an overhand or neutral grip; a neutral grip is often more comfortable for the elbow. Rest the free hand on the machine or your hip.
steps.posture: Stand tall with a very slight forward lean, shoulder of the working arm drawn down and back.
steps.brace: Brace your trunk to resist twisting towards the working side.
steps.initiate: Push the handle down by straightening the elbow, keeping the upper arm against your side.
steps.concentric: Extend the elbow fully until the handle is beside your thigh, rotating the palm slightly down if using a neutral grip.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you press down, inhale as the handle returns.
steps.eccentric: Allow the handle to rise slowly until your forearm is just above parallel to the floor.
steps.rom: From about 90 degrees of elbow bend to full lockout beside the thigh, with no shoulder movement.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: two seconds up, no pause, one second down, one-second squeeze at lockout.
steps.finish: Finish with the arm straight and the triceps fully contracted.
steps.exit: Let the handle return to the top slowly after the final rep, then switch arms and repeat with the same number of reps.

mistakes.m: Rotating the torso to help push the weight
mistakes.fix: Brace and use a lighter load; hold the machine with the free hand.

mistakes.m: Elbow drifting forward or out
mistakes.fix: Pin the elbow to your side.

mistakes.m: Not matching reps between arms
mistakes.fix: Start with the weaker arm and match reps on the stronger side.

mistakes.m: Locking the wrist into extension
mistakes.fix: Keep the wrist straight in line with the forearm.

safety: Use a light load; unilateral work concentrates stress on one elbow.
Stop if elbow pain is sharp or localised.
Keep the movement smooth to avoid jerking the shoulder at the top.
checks: Check the D-handle and carabiner are secure.
Confirm the pin is fully inserted.
Make sure the pulley is locked at the top.
reduceLoad: Reduce the weight if your torso twists, the elbow leaves your side, or you cannot complete full lockout.

programming.rehab: Very light single-arm pushdowns with a slow tempo can help rebuild an injured arm under a physiotherapist's guidance.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Start with the lightest stack plates and choose a load you could press for 15-20 reps.
programming.judgeLoad: The final reps should be hard, with no twisting and full lockout.
programming.progression: Double progression in 10-15 reps, then add the smallest stack increment.
programming.increase: Increase when both arms reach 15 reps on all sets.
programming.maintain: Hold the load if one arm lags behind, and reduce it if the elbow hurts.

name: Cross-body cable extension
musclesText: Primary: triceps brachii, with strong lateral head involvement. Secondary: anconeus, posterior deltoid and rotator cuff stabilising the shoulder, forearm muscles.

steps.start: Stand centred between two high pulleys holding the cables crossed in front of your face, right hand holding the left cable and left hand holding the right cable, elbows bent and raised to about shoulder height.
steps.setup: Set both pulleys at the top of a cable crossover station and remove the handles so you can hold the cable stopper balls, or attach small single handles. Select a very light and equal load on both sides.
steps.feet: Stand with feet hip-width apart in the middle of the station, a step in front of the pulleys line.
steps.grip: Hold the left cable with the right hand and the right cable with the left hand, palms facing down or towards you, wrists straight.
steps.posture: Stand tall with a slight forward lean, elbows raised to about shoulder height and pointing out to the sides.
steps.brace: Brace your core lightly and keep your torso still as the cables pull.
steps.initiate: Extend your elbows to push your hands outwards and downwards, keeping your upper arms at roughly the same position.
steps.concentric: Continue until your elbows are straight and your arms form a wide low V shape out to the sides.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you extend your arms, inhale on the return.
steps.eccentric: Bend your elbows slowly and let your hands return to cross in front of your face.
steps.rom: From hands crossed in front of the face to full elbow extension with the arms out and slightly down.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: two seconds back in, no pause, one second out, a one-second squeeze at full extension.
steps.finish: Finish with arms straight and triceps squeezed.
steps.exit: Bring the hands back in to the start under control and let both cables return to the stack at the same time before releasing.

cues: Hands cross in front of your face

mistakes.m: Using the shoulders to sweep the arms down
mistakes.fix: Fix the upper arms and move only at the elbows.

mistakes.m: Using too much load and leaning forward
mistakes.fix: Use light weights and stand tall.

mistakes.m: Mismatched speed on each side
mistakes.fix: Move both arms together.

mistakes.m: Shrugging the shoulders
mistakes.fix: Keep the shoulders down.

safety: Use light loads; the upper arms are held raised and slightly out to the sides, which places the shoulder in a position some people find uncomfortable.
Avoid this variation if it causes shoulder pain, and choose a standard pushdown instead.
Release the cables one at a time in a controlled way so they do not snap back.
Stop if you feel sharp pain at the elbow rather than a muscular burn.
checks: Set both pulleys to the same height and both stacks to the same weight.
Check the cable ends or handles are secure and the carabiners closed.
Ensure there is enough space either side of you and that the stack pins are fully inserted.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if your upper arms swing down, you need to lean forward to finish reps, one arm finishes ahead of the other, or you feel shoulder discomfort.

programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week as a finishing exercise.
programming.initialLoad: Start with the lightest plate on each stack and aim for 15 smooth reps.
programming.judgeLoad: Stop each set with 1-2 reps in reserve, upper arms still and both sides moving together.
programming.progression: Double progression within 12-15 reps, then add one stack increment per side.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets reach 15 clean reps.
programming.maintain: Hold the load if form slips or one arm lags, and reduce it if the shoulders or elbows complain.

name: Dumbbell kickback
musclesText: Primary: triceps brachii, all three heads strongly shortened at lockout. Secondary: posterior deltoid and latissimus dorsi holding the upper arm back, erector spinae and core for torso position.

steps.start: Hinge forward with one hand and knee on a bench, or hinge at the hips standing, holding a dumbbell with your upper arm parallel to your torso and elbow bent at 90 degrees.
steps.setup: Use a flat bench for support, or a standing hip hinge. Choose a light dumbbell; this is a short-lever finisher, not a heavy lift.
steps.feet: Bench-supported: same-side knee on the bench, other foot planted on the floor. Standing: feet hip-width, knees soft.
steps.grip: Hold the dumbbell with a neutral grip, wrist straight and in line with the forearm.
steps.posture: Torso nearly parallel to the floor, flat back, neck neutral; upper arm tight against the side of your torso and parallel to it.
steps.brace: Brace your core so the torso stays still; on the bench push the supporting hand into the pad.
steps.initiate: Extend the elbow to swing the forearm backward without moving the upper arm.
steps.concentric: Straighten the arm fully so the dumbbell is behind you and the whole arm is in line with your torso.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you extend, inhale as you return.
steps.eccentric: Bend the elbow slowly back to 90 degrees, keeping the upper arm fixed.
steps.rom: From 90 degrees of elbow bend to full extension with the arm parallel to your torso.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: two seconds back down, no pause, one second up, one-second squeeze at lockout.
steps.finish: Finish each rep with the elbow straight and triceps squeezed.
steps.exit: After the final rep, lower the dumbbell to the floor or bench and switch sides.

mistakes.m: Upper arm dropping down
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbow high beside your torso; use a lighter dumbbell.

mistakes.m: Swinging the dumbbell
mistakes.fix: Slow down and pause at lockout.

mistakes.m: Rounded back
mistakes.fix: Hinge from the hips with a flat back.

mistakes.m: Partial lockout
mistakes.fix: Straighten the arm fully.

safety: Keep a neutral spine throughout, as you are holding a hip hinge; use the bench-supported version if your lower back is sensitive.
Use a light dumbbell so you can extend fully without swinging, which can jar the elbow at lockout.
Stop if you feel sharp pain behind the elbow.
checks: Check the bench is stable and the pad is dry.
Use a fixed dumbbell or check collars are tight.
Make sure there is room behind you for the dumbbell to travel.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if the upper arm drops below parallel to your torso, you swing the dumbbell, you cannot reach full lockout, or you cannot hold the top for a second.

programming.rehab: Very light kickbacks can be part of a rehab programme for the elbow under the guidance of a physiotherapist.
programming.frequency: 1-3 times per week, usually as a finisher after heavier triceps work.
programming.initialLoad: Start with a light dumbbell you can lock out for 15 reps with a one-second pause; most people need much less than for curls.
programming.judgeLoad: The last reps should slow but still reach full lockout without swinging.
programming.progression: Double progression in 12-15 reps.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets reach 15 reps with a pause.
programming.maintain: Hold the load if you swing; reduce if the elbow hurts.

name: Cat-cow
musclesText: Primary: erector spinae and multifidus (moving the spine into extension), rectus abdominis and obliques (moving it into flexion). Secondary: rhomboids, serratus anterior and trapezius around the shoulder blades, and the pelvic floor and deep neck muscles.

steps.start: Start on your hands and knees on a mat with your spine in a neutral, flat position.
steps.setup: Use a mat or soft surface for your knees; fold it over if your knees are sensitive.
steps.feet: Knees directly under your hips, hip-width apart, with the tops of your feet resting on the mat.
steps.grip: Hands directly under your shoulders, fingers spread and pointing forward, pressing evenly through the palms.
steps.posture: Neck in line with your spine, looking at the floor just in front of your hands.
steps.brace: Keep a light brace and move slowly; the goal is control rather than tension.
steps.initiate: Start the movement from the pelvis: tilt the tailbone first, then let the movement travel up the spine to the head.
steps.concentric: For the cat, tuck the tailbone, round the spine towards the ceiling, push the floor away and let the head drop; for the cow, tilt the tailbone up, let the belly sink and lift the chest and gaze forward.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you round into the cat, inhale as you move into the cow.
steps.eccentric: Return through neutral each time in a smooth wave, one vertebra at a time.
steps.rom: Move through a comfortable, pain-free range; do not force the end of either position.
steps.tempo: Slow and rhythmic: about 3 seconds into each position, with a brief pause at each end.
steps.finish: Finish in a neutral spine position on hands and knees.
steps.exit: Sit back onto your heels or slowly come to kneeling after the final rep.

cues: Move one segment at a time
Push the floor away in cat

mistakes.m: Moving only at the neck and lower back
mistakes.fix: Think of a wave through the whole spine, especially the mid-back.

mistakes.m: Rushing the reps
mistakes.fix: Slow down to 3 seconds each way.

mistakes.m: Bending the elbows
mistakes.fix: Keep the arms straight and push through the palms.

mistakes.m: Forcing the end range
mistakes.fix: Stop at a comfortable stretch.

safety: Stay within a pain-free range, especially if you have back pain.
Use padding under the knees.
Stop if you get pain radiating into the legs, numbness or tingling.
checks: Use a mat on a non-slip surface.
Make sure you have room to move.
Remove anything uncomfortable under your knees.
reduceLoad: Reduce the range if any position causes pain or if you feel radiating symptoms.

programming.rehab: A gentle, pain-free cat-cow is a common early tool to restore movement in back pain; ask a physiotherapist if symptoms persist.
programming.frequency: Daily or before training as part of a warm-up.
programming.initialLoad: Bodyweight only; begin with a small range of motion.
programming.judgeLoad: The movement should feel smooth and comfortable, with no pain.
programming.progression: Progress by increasing range and control, not speed.
programming.increase: Increase range gradually as comfort improves.
programming.maintain: Keep a smaller range if pain or stiffness appears.

name: Thoracic rotations
musclesText: Primary: thoracic spine rotators including the multifidus, rotatores and internal and external obliques. Secondary: pectoralis major and minor (stretched in the open-book), rhomboids and middle trapezius.

steps.start: For the open-book, lie on your side with hips and knees bent to 90 degrees and both arms straight out in front at shoulder height, palms together. For the quadruped version, start on hands and knees with one hand behind your head.
steps.setup: Use a mat. For the side-lying version, place a small cushion or folded towel under your head; a foam roller or pillow between or under the top knee helps keep the hips still.
steps.feet: Side-lying: stack the knees and keep them together. Quadruped: knees under hips, hip-width apart.
steps.grip: Side-lying: palms together in front. Quadruped: supporting hand under the shoulder, other hand lightly behind your head.
steps.posture: Keep your lower back and hips still so the rotation comes from your upper back and ribcage.
steps.brace: Brace lightly and keep the knees pressed together in the side-lying version.
steps.initiate: Side-lying: lift the top arm and sweep it up and over your body. Quadruped: rotate the elbow down towards the supporting arm first.
steps.concentric: Open the chest: in side-lying let the top arm land on the floor on the other side while your eyes follow it; in quadruped rotate the elbow up towards the ceiling.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you rotate open, inhale as you return.
steps.eccentric: Bring the arm or elbow back to the start slowly, retracing the path.
steps.rom: Rotate only as far as your hips and knees stay still; the arm does not need to touch the floor.
steps.tempo: 3-2-3-0: three seconds to rotate open, a two-second hold with a slow breath, three seconds to return.
steps.finish: Finish each rep back in the start position with the chest facing the floor or side.
steps.exit: After the last rep on one side, roll onto the other side or switch arms, and get up slowly.

mistakes.m: Rolling the hips to fake extra rotation
mistakes.fix: Pin the knees together or onto a pillow.

mistakes.m: Forcing the arm to the floor
mistakes.fix: Rotate only within a comfortable range.

mistakes.m: Holding your breath
mistakes.fix: Exhale as you open.

mistakes.m: Fast, jerky rotations
mistakes.fix: Slow down and pause at end range.

safety: Avoid forcing rotation if you feel pain in the back or shoulder.
Support the head to protect the neck.
Stop with numbness or tingling in the arm.
checks: Use a mat on a flat surface.
Have a towel or pillow ready to support your head or knee.
Ensure enough room for your arm to rotate fully.
reduceLoad: Reduce the range if you feel pinching in the shoulder or back.

programming.rehab: Useful in rehabilitation for stiff upper backs and shoulder problems; see a physiotherapist if pain persists.
programming.frequency: Daily or before upper-body training.
programming.initialLoad: Bodyweight only.
programming.judgeLoad: You should feel a stretch through the chest and upper back, never pain.
programming.progression: Progress by increasing the end-range hold or range of motion.
programming.increase: Increase range gradually as mobility improves.
programming.maintain: Keep the same range if you feel discomfort.

name: Hip flexor mobility
musclesText: Primary: iliopsoas and rectus femoris (stretched on the kneeling side). Secondary: gluteus maximus contracting to extend the hip, tensor fasciae latae, and abdominals controlling pelvic tilt.

steps.start: Kneel on one knee on a mat with the other foot flat in front, both knees bent at about 90 degrees.
steps.setup: Place a folded mat or pad under the down knee for comfort.
