steps.feet: Front foot flat, knee over the ankle; back knee under the hip, top of the back foot on the floor or toes tucked.
steps.grip: Hands on your hips, or the arm on the kneeling side raised overhead for extra stretch.
steps.posture: Tall torso, ribs stacked over the pelvis, chin level.
steps.brace: Brace your abdominals and tilt the pelvis backwards (tuck the tailbone).
steps.initiate: Squeeze the glute on the kneeling side hard; this alone should create a stretch at the front of the hip.
steps.concentric: Shift your hips forward a few centimetres while keeping the pelvis tucked and the glute squeezed, until you feel a stretch at the front of the hip and thigh.
steps.breathing: Breathe slowly through the nose and out through the mouth, relaxing into the stretch on each exhale.
steps.eccentric: Ease back out of the forward shift before switching sides.
steps.rom: Only shift as far as you can while keeping the pelvis tucked; the stretch should be at the front of the hip, not the lower back.
steps.tempo: Hold 20-45 s with steady breathing, or do 8-10 slow rocks with a 2-3 s hold.
steps.finish: Finish by easing the hips back, releasing the glute squeeze.
steps.exit: Bring the back knee forward, stand up using the front leg, then switch sides.

mistakes.m: Arching the lower back to go further
mistakes.fix: Tuck the pelvis and squeeze the glute; shorten the forward shift.

mistakes.m: Front knee travelling far past the toes
mistakes.fix: Move the front foot further forward.

mistakes.m: Leaning the torso forward
mistakes.fix: Stay tall with ribs over hips.

mistakes.m: Not squeezing the glute
mistakes.fix: Actively contract the glute on the kneeling side.

safety: Pad the down knee.
Stop if you feel pinching at the front of the hip or pain in the lower back.
Avoid bouncing into the stretch.
checks: Use a pad or folded mat for the knee.
Kneel on a non-slip surface.
Have something to hold for balance if needed.
reduceLoad: Reduce the forward shift if you feel back discomfort, hip pinching, or lose the pelvic tuck.

programming.rehab: Gentle use helps restore hip extension after long sitting or some back pain; check with a physiotherapist if pain persists.
programming.frequency: Daily or before lower-body training.
programming.initialLoad: Bodyweight only; start with the glute squeeze before adding any forward shift.
programming.judgeLoad: You should feel a moderate stretch at the front of the hip, never pain.
programming.progression: Progress by adding an overhead reach or lengthening holds.
programming.increase: Increase the hold time or range once comfortable.
programming.maintain: Stay at the same range if the back arches or discomfort appears.

name: Ankle mobility drills
musclesText: Primary: gastrocnemius and soleus (lengthened as the knee travels over the toes), with the talocrural joint moving into dorsiflexion. Secondary: tibialis anterior pulling the shin forward, and the foot's intrinsic muscles keeping the arch stable.

steps.start: Stand facing a wall in a split stance with the front foot a few centimetres from the wall.
steps.setup: Use a clear section of wall. Optionally put a ruler or tape on the floor to measure the toe-to-wall distance.
steps.feet: Front foot points straight at the wall, about 5-10 cm away; back foot a stride behind for balance.
steps.grip: Place your hands on the wall at chest height for balance.
steps.posture: Stand tall with hips square to the wall.
steps.brace: Keep a light brace so the movement comes only from the ankle.
steps.initiate: Keep your whole front heel on the floor and start to bend the front knee forward.
steps.concentric: Drive the knee forward towards the wall, aiming the knee over the second and third toes, until it touches the wall or you feel a stretch in the calf or front of the ankle.
steps.breathing: Breathe out as you rock forward, breathe in as you return.
steps.eccentric: Rock back slowly to straighten the knee, keeping the heel down.
steps.rom: Go only as far as the heel stays down and the arch does not collapse; move the foot further from the wall as it gets easier.
steps.tempo: 2-1-2-0: two seconds forward, a one-second hold, two seconds back.
steps.finish: Finish each rock with the knee straightened and the weight back in the middle.
steps.exit: After your reps, step away from the wall and switch legs.

cues: Do not let the arch collapse

mistakes.m: Heel lifting
mistakes.fix: Move the foot closer to the wall.

mistakes.m: Knee collapsing inwards
mistakes.fix: Aim the knee over the second and third toes.

mistakes.m: Rushing
mistakes.fix: Pause briefly at end range.

mistakes.m: Feeling a pinch at the front of the ankle and pushing through it
mistakes.fix: Reduce depth; try placing the knee slightly outwards.

safety: Avoid forcing through pinching at the front of the ankle.
Do not bounce into end range.
After an ankle sprain or surgery, follow your physiotherapist's guidance.
checks: Check the floor is not slippery.
Have a clear wall area.
Wear flat shoes or go barefoot.
reduceLoad: Reduce the distance from the wall if the heel lifts or you feel pain at the front of the ankle.

programming.rehab: Commonly used after ankle sprains to restore dorsiflexion; a physiotherapist can guide progressions.
programming.frequency: Daily or before squats and lunges.
programming.initialLoad: Bodyweight only; start close to the wall.
programming.judgeLoad: It should feel like a stretch in the calf or a gentle feeling at the ankle joint, not pain.
programming.progression: Progress by moving the foot further from the wall in 1 cm steps.
programming.increase: Move the foot further when the knee easily touches the wall with the heel down.
programming.maintain: Stay at the same distance if the heel lifts or the ankle pinches.

name: Bodyweight squats
musclesText: Primary: quadriceps and gluteus maximus. Secondary: adductor magnus, hamstrings, calves and core stabilisers.

steps.start: Stand tall with feet about shoulder-width apart, arms by your sides or held in front.
steps.setup: No equipment needed; a box or bench behind you can act as a depth target while you learn.
steps.feet: Feet shoulder-width, toes turned out 15-30 degrees, weight spread across the whole foot.
steps.grip: Hold your arms straight out in front at shoulder height, or clasp your hands at chest height, to help balance.
steps.posture: Chest up, neutral spine and gaze ahead.
steps.brace: Take a breath and brace your core lightly.
steps.initiate: Push your hips back and bend your knees at the same time.
steps.concentric: Stand up by driving through the whole foot and squeezing your glutes at the top.
steps.breathing: Inhale as you squat down, exhale as you stand.
steps.eccentric: Lower under control with the knees tracking in line with the toes and the heels flat.
steps.rom: Squat as deep as you can with heels flat and back neutral, ideally with thighs at or below parallel.
steps.tempo: 2-1-1-0: two seconds down, one-second pause at the bottom, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish standing tall with hips and knees fully extended.
steps.exit: Simply stand after the last rep and move on to your next exercise.

cues: Squeeze your glutes at the top

mistakes.m: Knees collapsing inwards
mistakes.fix: Push the knees out over the toes.

mistakes.m: Heels lifting
mistakes.fix: Widen the stance or work on ankle mobility.

mistakes.m: Rounding the back at the bottom
mistakes.fix: Squat only as deep as you can keep the back neutral.

mistakes.m: Rushing the reps
mistakes.fix: Slow down and pause at the bottom.

safety: Stop if you feel sharp knee or hip pain.
Use a box target if balance or depth is a problem.
Avoid rapid bouncing at the bottom.
checks: Make sure the floor is not slippery.
Wear stable shoes or go barefoot.
Have clear space around you.
reduceLoad: Reduce the depth or use a box if pain occurs or the back rounds.

programming.rehab: A shallow box squat can rebuild confidence after knee or hip problems; check with a physiotherapist.
programming.frequency: Daily as a warm-up, or 2-3 times per week as conditioning.
programming.initialLoad: Bodyweight only.
programming.judgeLoad: Each rep should be smooth with good depth and knees in line.
programming.progression: Progress depth, then reps or tempo, then move to goblet squats.
programming.increase: Progress when 20 smooth reps are easy.
programming.maintain: Stay at the same depth if pain or form issues appear.

name: Glute bridges
musclesText: Primary: gluteus maximus. Secondary: hamstrings, gluteus medius, erector spinae and abdominals.

steps.start: Lie on your back on a mat with knees bent, feet flat and arms by your sides.
steps.setup: Use a mat. No load is used in this warm-up and activation version.
steps.feet: Feet hip-width apart and flat, heels about 20-30 cm from your glutes so your shins are vertical at the top.
steps.grip: Arms on the floor at your sides, palms down, pressing lightly into the mat.
steps.posture: Ribs down and lower back neutral, not arched.
steps.brace: Brace your core and tuck the pelvis slightly before lifting.
steps.initiate: Press your heels into the floor and squeeze your glutes before your hips leave the mat, so the glutes rather than the lower back start the lift.
steps.concentric: Lift until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees, without arching the lower back.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower your hips slowly to the mat.
steps.rom: From hips on the floor to a straight line from shoulders to knees.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-2: two seconds lowering, no pause at the bottom, one second lifting, a two-second hold at the top.
steps.finish: Finish at the top with glutes squeezed hard.
steps.exit: Lower your hips to the mat after the last rep and roll to one side to stand.

mistakes.m: Arching the lower back at the top
mistakes.fix: Stop at a straight line and keep the ribs down.

mistakes.m: Feeling it mainly in the hamstrings
mistakes.fix: Bring the feet a little closer.

mistakes.m: Knees falling inwards
mistakes.fix: Push the knees outward.

mistakes.m: Rushing
mistakes.fix: Pause at the top for two seconds.

safety: Avoid pushing the hips so high that the lower back arches; finish at a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Stop if you feel back pain, and if the hamstrings cramp, bring the feet slightly closer.
This is the unloaded warm-up version; do not add a barbell until you can perform 20 controlled reps with a pause.
checks: Use a mat.
Ensure a flat surface.
Clear space for your feet.
reduceLoad: Make it easier by reducing the height if you feel back pain or cramping.

programming.rehab: A gentle glute bridge is a common early rehab exercise for back and hip issues; follow a physiotherapist's advice.
programming.frequency: Daily as activation, or 2-3 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Bodyweight only.
programming.judgeLoad: You should feel the glutes working strongly with only mild hamstring involvement and no lower-back strain.
programming.progression: Progress by longer holds at the top, then single-leg bridges, then loaded barbell bridges or hip thrusts.
programming.increase: Progress when 20 reps with a pause are easy.
programming.maintain: Stay at the same level if back discomfort appears.

name: Band pull-aparts
musclesText: Primary: posterior deltoid, rhomboids and middle trapezius. Secondary: lower trapezius, infraspinatus and teres minor.

steps.start: Stand tall holding a light resistance band at shoulder height with straight arms in front of you.
steps.setup: Use a light, long loop band or a flat resistance band without nicks or tears. A lighter band lets you keep straight arms through the full range.
steps.feet: Feet hip-width apart, knees soft.
steps.grip: Take an overhand grip on the band with hands about shoulder-width apart and thumbs wrapped; a narrower grip makes the movement harder, a wider grip easier.
steps.posture: Stand tall with ribs down and neck neutral.
steps.brace: Brace lightly so the torso stays still.
steps.initiate: Start by setting your shoulder blades back and down, then begin pulling your hands apart from the shoulders rather than the hands.
steps.concentric: Pull the band apart in a wide arc until it lightly touches your chest at shoulder height, arms straight and shoulder blades squeezed together.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you pull apart, inhale as you return.
steps.eccentric: Return slowly to the start, resisting the band.
steps.rom: From arms in front at shoulder width to the band at your chest.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: two seconds returning to the start, no pause, one second pulling apart, a one-second squeeze at the chest.
steps.finish: Finish with the band at your chest and shoulder blades squeezed.
steps.exit: Let the band return to the start slowly and release it without letting it snap.

mistakes.m: Shrugging
mistakes.fix: Keep the shoulders down.

mistakes.m: Bending the elbows
mistakes.fix: Keep arms straight.

mistakes.m: Arching the lower back
mistakes.fix: Keep ribs down.

mistakes.m: Letting the band snap back
mistakes.fix: Control the return.

safety: Inspect the band before every use; a snapping band can strike your face or eyes.
Keep the band at shoulder height or lower and avoid shrugging, which shifts the work to the upper trapezius and neck.
Stop if you feel pinching at the front of the shoulder.
checks: Inspect the band for tears.
Choose the correct band tension.
Grip the band securely.
reduceLoad: Use a lighter band or a wider grip if you shrug, cannot keep your arms straight, arch your lower back, or cannot control the return.

programming.rehab: Light band pull-aparts are often used for shoulder rehab; consult a physiotherapist for specific programmes.
programming.frequency: Daily or before upper-body training.
programming.initialLoad: Start with the lightest band.
programming.judgeLoad: You should feel the rear shoulders and between the shoulder blades working, not your neck, and reach the chest on every rep.
programming.progression: Progress by narrower grip or a heavier band.
programming.increase: Progress when 20 reps are easy.
programming.maintain: Stay with the same band if form slips.

name: Shoulder circles
musclesText: Primary: anterior, lateral and posterior deltoid moving the arm through circles. Secondary: rotator cuff (supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor, subscapularis), upper and lower trapezius and serratus anterior moving the shoulder blade.

steps.start: Stand tall with your arms relaxed by your sides.
steps.setup: No equipment needed; make sure you have an arm's length of clear space around you.
steps.feet: Feet hip-width apart, knees soft, weight evenly spread.
steps.grip: Start with shoulder rolls (hands relaxed at your sides), then progress to arm circles with arms straight out to the sides and fingers extended, palms down.
steps.posture: Stand tall, ribs down, neck relaxed and long, eyes forward.
steps.brace: Keep a gentle brace so the lower back does not arch as the arms move overhead.
steps.initiate: Begin with small shoulder rolls, lifting the shoulders up, back, down and forward.
steps.concentric: Progress to arm circles: start small at shoulder height and gradually increase to large, full circles through overhead.
steps.breathing: Breathe naturally and rhythmically; do not hold your breath.
steps.eccentric: Reverse the direction after each set, moving forward then backward.
steps.rom: Start small and build to the largest comfortable circle; avoid ranges that cause pinching.
steps.tempo: Smooth and controlled, about 1-2 seconds per circle.
steps.finish: Finish each set with the arms lowered and shoulders relaxed.
steps.exit: Lower your arms to your sides and shake them out gently.

mistakes.m: Starting with large, fast circles
mistakes.fix: Build up from small to large.

mistakes.m: Arching the lower back overhead
mistakes.fix: Keep the ribs down and brace.

mistakes.m: Shrugging the shoulders tensely
mistakes.fix: Relax the neck and upper traps.

mistakes.m: Only one direction
mistakes.fix: Do equal reps forwards and backwards.

safety: Stop if you feel pinching or clicking with pain in the shoulder.
Keep within a comfortable range after shoulder injury.
Avoid fast flinging motions.
checks: Clear space around you.
Remove anything you could strike with your hands.
Stand on a stable surface.
reduceLoad: Reduce the size and speed of circles if you feel pinching or pain.

programming.rehab: Small pain-free circles can be useful in early shoulder rehab; follow your physiotherapist's guidance.
programming.frequency: Before every upper-body session or daily.
programming.initialLoad: Bodyweight only.
programming.judgeLoad: Movement should feel smooth and warm, with no catching, clicking with pain or pinching at the top of the shoulder.
programming.progression: Increase circle size gradually.
programming.increase: Increase the size when smaller circles feel easy.
programming.maintain: Keep the circle size the same if you feel discomfort.

name: World's greatest stretch
musclesText: Primary: iliopsoas and rectus femoris of the rear leg, gluteus maximus and hamstrings of the front leg. Secondary: thoracic spine rotators and obliques during the reach, adductors of the front leg, pectoralis major and the shoulder of the reaching arm.

steps.start: From standing, step your right foot forward into a long lunge and place both hands on the floor, the left hand directly under your left shoulder and the right hand inside your right foot.
steps.setup: No equipment is required; use a mat or clear floor with about two metres of space in front and to the sides. A yoga block under the hands helps if you cannot reach the floor.
steps.feet: Front foot flat with the knee stacked over the ankle; back leg long with the back knee off the floor and the heel lifted, or rest the back knee on a mat for an easier version.
steps.grip: Start with both hands on the floor inside the front foot, fingers spread; during the reach, the inside hand rotates up towards the ceiling while the other hand stays planted under the shoulder.
steps.posture: Keep the spine long from head to back heel, hips low and square, and the front knee pointing over the second toe rather than falling in.
steps.brace: Squeeze the glute of the back leg and keep a light brace, which also deepens the stretch at the front of the back hip.
steps.initiate: Lower the right elbow (the arm on the same side as the front leg) towards the inside of the right instep and hold briefly, feeling the stretch in the groin and rear hip.
steps.concentric: Bring the right hand back to the floor, then rotate your chest open to the right and reach the right arm straight up to the ceiling, following the hand with your eyes.
steps.breathing: Exhale slowly as you drop the elbow and again as you rotate open; inhale as you return.
steps.eccentric: Return the hand to the floor inside the foot; for an optional hamstring finish, shift your hips back and straighten the front knee, pulling the toes up, then bend it again.
steps.rom: Lower the elbow only as far as your hips allow and rotate only as far as the chest turns without the front knee collapsing; the elbow does not need to touch the floor.
steps.tempo: Slow: 2-3 seconds into each position with a one-breath hold, so one full sequence takes about 10-15 seconds.
steps.finish: Finish each repetition back in the lunge with both hands down and hips level.
steps.exit: After the last rep, step the back foot forward to meet the front foot and stand up, or step the front foot back to a push-up position and switch legs.

cues: Rotate the chest, not just the arm

mistakes.m: Taking too short a lunge so the stretch disappears
mistakes.fix: Step out further so the back hip opens; drop the back knee to the mat if balance suffers.

mistakes.m: Rotating only the arm and shoulder
mistakes.fix: Turn the whole ribcage until the chest faces the side.

mistakes.m: Front knee falling inwards during the rotation
mistakes.fix: Press the front knee out over the toes with the inside arm or hand.

mistakes.m: Rushing through the positions
mistakes.fix: Hold each position for one slow breath.

safety: Drop the back knee to the floor if you have knee, hip or balance issues.
Do not force the elbow to the floor; pinching at the front of the hip means you have gone too far.
If you have a recent hamstring strain, skip the straight-leg finish until cleared.
checks: Clear about two metres of floor space.
Use a non-slip floor or mat.
Have a block or step ready if you cannot reach the floor comfortably.
reduceLoad: Shorten the lunge, lower the back knee or use a block under the hands if you feel pain, lose balance or the front knee caves in.

programming.frequency: Daily or as part of every lower-body or running warm-up.
programming.initialLoad: Bodyweight only; start with the back knee down if needed.
programming.judgeLoad: You should feel stretch in the hip flexors, groin and upper back, never joint pain.
programming.progression: Progress from back knee down to knee up, then add the hamstring finish and longer holds.
programming.increase: Progress when 5 reps per side feel smooth with good balance.
programming.maintain: Stay with the easier version if balance or knee alignment slips.

name: Dynamic hamstring mobility
musclesText: Primary: hamstrings (biceps femoris, semitendinosus and semimembranosus) taken through a moving stretch. Secondary: gluteus maximus, hip flexors that drive the forward swing, gastrocnemius during the heel-down sweep and inchworm.

steps.start: Stand side-on to a wall or sturdy upright with your inside hand on it for balance, standing on the inside leg with the outside leg free to swing.
steps.setup: Use a wall, rack or rail for balance during leg swings, and a few metres of open floor for sweeps and inchworms.
steps.feet: Swings: stand on one leg with that knee slightly soft and foot pointing forwards. Sweeps: step one foot a half-pace forward with the heel down and toes up.
steps.grip: For swings, rest one hand on the support; for sweeps, let your arms hang; for inchworms, place both hands flat on the floor in front of your feet.
steps.posture: Stay tall with a neutral spine in the swings; in sweeps, hinge from the hips with a flat back.
steps.brace: Brace lightly so the pelvis and lower back stay still while the leg moves.
steps.initiate: Start leg swings with small forward and backward swings of the straight or slightly bent outside leg at about knee height.
steps.concentric: Gradually increase the swing height over 10-15 reps, letting the hamstring stretch at the front of each swing. For sweeps, hinge over the straight front leg and sweep your hands low along the floor past the foot as you step forward. For inchworms, walk the hands out to a plank and back, keeping the legs as straight as is comfortable.
steps.breathing: Breathe naturally and rhythmically; do not hold your breath.
steps.eccentric: Let the leg swing back under control rather than kicking it back, and return to standing tall between sweeps.
steps.rom: Build up gradually to a comfortable end range; the swing height is controlled by hamstring comfort, never by momentum.
steps.tempo: Rhythmic: roughly one swing per second; sweeps and inchworms about 2-3 seconds per rep.
steps.finish: Finish each set standing on both feet with the pelvis level.
steps.exit: After your reps, set the swinging foot down, turn around and repeat on the other leg.

cues: Hinge, do not round, in sweeps
Toes up on the sweeping leg

mistakes.m: Kicking as high as possible from the first rep
mistakes.fix: Begin at knee height and increase over several reps.

mistakes.m: Rounding the lower back to reach further in sweeps
mistakes.fix: Hinge from the hips with a flat back and only go as low as your hamstrings allow.

mistakes.m: Leaning back as the leg swings forward
mistakes.fix: Keep the torso tall and let the leg do the work.

mistakes.m: Locking the standing knee hard
mistakes.fix: Keep a soft standing knee.

safety: Avoid ballistic swings if you have a recent hamstring strain; use gentle sweeps and follow your physiotherapist's guidance.
Stop if you feel a sharp pull at the back of the thigh or pain behind the knee.
Avoid if you get tingling or nerve-type pain down the leg; this suggests sciatic nerve irritation rather than tight hamstrings.
checks: Clear space so the swinging leg cannot strike anything.
Use a stable support for balance.
Use a non-slip floor or wear grippy shoes.
reduceLoad: Reduce the swing height or switch to slow sweeps if you feel pulling, pain or loss of balance.

programming.frequency: Before lower-body training, sprinting or running.
programming.initialLoad: Bodyweight only; start with small swings.
programming.judgeLoad: Movement should feel free and warm, with a mild stretch at the top of each swing.
programming.progression: Progress by increasing swing height gradually and adding inchworms.
programming.increase: Progress when full-height swings feel comfortable.
programming.maintain: Keep the range smaller if hamstrings feel tight or sore.

name: Barbell back squat
musclesText: Primary: quadriceps (vastus lateralis, vastus medialis, vastus intermedius, rectus femoris), gluteus maximus. Secondary: adductor magnus, hamstrings, erector spinae, rectus abdominis and obliques.

steps.start: Stand under the bar in the rack with the bar resting on the upper trapezius, just below the bony bump at the base of your neck, then stand it up and take two or three short steps back.
steps.setup: Set the J-hooks at mid-chest height so you can unrack with a slight knee bend, and set the safety arms just below the depth of your lowest squat, usually a few centimetres under the bar position at the bottom. Load evenly and fit collars.
steps.feet: Stance about hip to shoulder width, toes turned out roughly 15-30 degrees so your knees can track over them.
steps.grip: Grip the bar just outside the shoulders with a full grip, pull it down into your traps and keep the wrists stacked over the elbows rather than bent back.
steps.posture: Chest up and torso fairly upright, as the high-bar position lets you sit straight down between the hips; neutral head with eyes forward or slightly down.
steps.brace: Take a big breath into your belly and sides, then tighten your trunk as if bracing for a push, keeping the ribs stacked over the pelvis.
steps.initiate: Break at the hips and knees together, letting the knees travel forward over the toes while you sit down between your heels.
steps.concentric: Drive the floor away through the whole foot, pushing knees out in line with toes, and keep chest and hips rising at the same rate.
steps.breathing: Breathe in and brace at the top, hold the breath through the descent and the hardest part of the ascent, then exhale near the top or between reps.
steps.eccentric: Lower under control with the bar travelling straight down over mid-foot, keeping the knees tracking out and the back neutral.
steps.rom: Squat as deep as you can while keeping a neutral spine and heels down, ideally to thighs at or just below parallel; stop above the point where your pelvis tucks under.
steps.tempo: 3-0-1-0: three seconds down, no pause, drive up in about one second.
steps.finish: Stand fully with hips and knees extended, without leaning back or locking aggressively, then rebrace before the next rep.
steps.exit: After the last rep, walk forward until the bar touches the uprights, then lower it into both J-hooks together. If you fail a rep, sit down to the safety arms and slide out from under the bar.

cues: Bar on the traps, not the neck

mistakes.m: Heels lifting or weight shifting to the toes
mistakes.fix: Keep the bar over mid-foot, widen the stance slightly or use small heel wedges if ankle mobility is limited.

mistakes.m: Knees caving inward on the way up
mistakes.fix: Reduce the load and actively spread the floor with your feet so knees follow the toes.

mistakes.m: Hips shooting up first so it becomes a good morning
mistakes.fix: Lead with the chest out of the bottom and drop the load until the torso angle stays constant.

mistakes.m: Lower back rounding at the bottom
mistakes.fix: Stop the descent slightly higher and work on ankle and hip mobility before adding depth.

mistakes.m: Loose upper back so the bar rolls
mistakes.fix: Squeeze the shoulder blades together and pull the bar into your traps before unracking.

safety: Always set the safety arms at a height that catches the bar just below your bottom position.
Avoid grinding maximal reps without spotters or safeties; stop a set with 1-2 reps in reserve.
Stop if you feel sharp knee, hip or back pain, or any numbness or tingling down the legs.
checks: Check J-hook height, safety-arm height and that both are locked in.
Check plates are matched on each side and collars are on.
Make sure the floor around the rack is clear for your walk-out.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if your depth shortens, knees cave, heels lift, the bar drifts forward, or bar speed drops sharply before the target reps.

programming.rehab: Light, pain-free bodyweight or empty-bar squats to a comfortable depth can rebuild confidence after knee or back problems; follow a physiotherapist's guidance.
programming.frequency: 1-3 times per week, 48-72 h between hard sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Start with the empty 20 kg bar and add 5-10 kg per warm-up set until you reach a weight you can lift for the target reps with 2-3 reps left.
programming.judgeLoad: The last rep should still move at a steady speed with unchanged depth and bar path; stop when form or speed drops noticeably.
programming.progression: Double progression: work within a rep range, then add 2.5-5 kg once every set reaches the top of the range.
programming.increase: Increase the load when you hit the top of the rep range on all sets with 1-2 reps in reserve and clean technique.
programming.maintain: Keep the load the same if you miss reps or depth, and drop 5-10 percent if you are sore, poorly recovered or your form has degraded across two sessions.

name: Front squat
musclesText: Primary: quadriceps (vastus lateralis, vastus medialis, vastus intermedius, rectus femoris). Secondary: gluteus maximus, adductor magnus, thoracic erector spinae and upper back, rectus abdominis and obliques.

steps.start: Step under the bar so it sits across the front of your shoulders, against your throat but not choking you, with elbows high; stand it up and take two short steps back.
steps.setup: Set the J-hooks around upper-chest or collarbone height and the safety arms just below your deepest squat position; load evenly and fit collars.
steps.feet: Feet about shoulder width, toes turned out 10-25 degrees.
steps.grip: Clean grip: fingertips under the bar just outside the shoulders, bar resting on the front delts, not held up by the hands. Cross-arm: arms crossed, hands resting on top of the bar with elbows high and level.
steps.posture: Keep a very upright torso and lift the elbows so the upper arms are close to parallel with the floor; this keeps the bar over mid-foot.
steps.brace: Take a deep breath, brace hard through the trunk and keep the upper back tight so the elbows cannot drop.
steps.initiate: Bend the knees and hips together and sit straight down, letting the knees travel well forward.
steps.concentric: Drive up through the whole foot while pushing the elbows up first out of the bottom so the chest stays tall.
steps.breathing: Inhale and brace before the descent, hold through the bottom and ascent, exhale at the top.
steps.eccentric: Lower in a controlled line with the elbows staying high and the torso upright.
steps.rom: Go as deep as you can with a tall chest and neutral spine, usually below parallel; stop where the elbows drop or the back rounds.
steps.tempo: 3-0-1-0: three seconds down, no pause, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish standing tall with hips and knees extended, elbows still high.
steps.exit: Walk the bar forward into the J-hooks and set it down evenly. If a rep fails, push the bar forward off your shoulders onto the safety arms rather than trying to hold on, and step back.

cues: Bar sits on the shoulders, not the hands
Chest tall out of the hole

mistakes.m: Elbows dropping so the bar rolls forward
mistakes.fix: Lift the elbows harder, work wrist and lat mobility, or switch to the cross-arm grip.

mistakes.m: Leaning forward out of the bottom
mistakes.fix: Lead the ascent with the elbows and reduce the load.

mistakes.m: Gripping the bar with a full fist and straining the wrists
mistakes.fix: Use fingertips only, widen the grip slightly, or use the cross-arm position.

mistakes.m: Heels lifting
mistakes.fix: Widen the stance a little or use heel wedges or lifting shoes, and improve ankle mobility.

safety: Set safety arms correctly and learn to dump the bar forward before using heavy loads.
Wrist discomfort is common; adjust grip width or use the cross-arm grip rather than forcing the position.
Stop with any sharp knee or back pain, or numbness in the hands.
checks: Check J-hook and safety-arm height and that they are secure.
Check collars and equal loading.
Practise the rack position with the empty bar before loading.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load when the elbows sink, your torso tips forward, depth shortens, or you need to rescue the bar with your hands.

programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week, 48-72 h between hard squat sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Begin with the empty bar to learn the rack position, then add 5-10 kg per set; expect to use roughly 70-85 percent of your back squat.
programming.judgeLoad: You should finish each set with 1-3 reps left and no elbow drop; if upper-back fatigue limits you before the legs, the load is too heavy.
programming.progression: Double progression in the chosen rep range, adding 2.5-5 kg when all sets reach the top of the range.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets hit the top of the range with an upright torso and steady speed.
programming.maintain: Hold the load if the rack position slips or reps slow sharply, and reduce it if wrists or upper back are limiting you.

name: Goblet squat
musclesText: Primary: quadriceps, gluteus maximus. Secondary: adductors, rectus abdominis and obliques, upper back muscles holding the weight.

steps.start: Stand tall holding one dumbbell vertically by the top end, or a kettlebell by the horns, close against your breastbone.
steps.setup: Choose a dumbbell or kettlebell you can lift to your chest safely; pick it up from a bench or the floor with a straight back.
steps.feet: Feet shoulder width or slightly wider, toes turned out 15-30 degrees.
steps.grip: Cup the top plate of the dumbbell in both palms, or hold the kettlebell horns with the bell against your chest; elbows point down.
steps.posture: Tall chest and neutral spine, with the weight held tight to the body throughout.
steps.brace: Breathe in, brace your trunk and keep the weight pulled into your chest so it acts as a counterbalance.
steps.initiate: Bend hips and knees together and sit down between your feet.
steps.concentric: Push through the whole foot to stand, keeping the knees out over the toes and the chest tall.
steps.breathing: Inhale at the top, hold through the descent and turn, exhale as you stand.
steps.eccentric: Lower under control, letting the elbows travel down inside the knees.
steps.rom: Squat to the deepest position where your back stays neutral and heels stay down, often with elbows lightly brushing the inner knees.
steps.tempo: 3-1-1-0: three seconds down, one-second pause at the bottom, one second up.
steps.finish: Stand fully with hips extended and the weight still against your chest.
steps.exit: Lower the weight to the floor with a hinge or squat, or place it on a bench, keeping it close to your body.

mistakes.m: Weight drifting away from the body
mistakes.fix: Pull the weight back to the breastbone and keep elbows down.

mistakes.m: Rounding the back at the bottom
mistakes.fix: Stop slightly higher and use the pause to stay tall.

mistakes.m: Knees collapsing inward
mistakes.fix: Use the elbows to gently cue the knees out and reduce the weight.

mistakes.m: Rising onto the toes
mistakes.fix: Shift weight to mid-foot and widen stance slightly.

safety: Pick up and put down the weight with a neutral back; heavy dumbbells can be awkward to get into position.
Stop if you feel sharp knee or hip pain.
checks: Check the dumbbell head is secure or the kettlebell handle is not damaged.
Clear space around you to set the weight down.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if your upper back or arms give out before your legs, the chest drops, or depth shortens.

programming.rehab: A light goblet squat to a box at comfortable depth is a useful way to retrain squatting after knee or hip niggles; check with a physiotherapist if you are recovering from injury.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Start with a light dumbbell (around 8-12 kg for many beginners) and do a set of 10; increase until 10-12 reps leave 2-3 in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: Reps should stay smooth with full depth; if you cannot hold the weight comfortably, it is too heavy for a goblet hold.
programming.progression: Double progression: add reps to the top of the range, then move up 2 kg per dumbbell or the next kettlebell.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets reach the top of the range with clean form.
programming.maintain: Keep the same load if depth or posture worsens, and when the weight becomes limited by your arms rather than your legs, move on to a barbell squat or leg press.

name: Smith machine squat
musclesText: Primary: quadriceps, gluteus maximus. Secondary: adductors, hamstrings.

steps.start: Stand under the Smith bar with it across your upper traps, feet placed slightly in front of the bar, then rotate the bar to unhook it.
steps.setup: Set the bar at mid-chest height on the hooks and set the safety stops just below the bottom of your squat. Load evenly and fit collars if available.
steps.feet: Place your feet about shoulder width and roughly 15-30 cm in front of the bar line, toes slightly out, so you can sit back while the bar moves vertically.
steps.grip: Hold the bar just outside shoulder width with a full grip, wrists straight, ready to rotate the hooks on and off.
steps.posture: Lean back lightly into the bar with a neutral spine; the fixed path lets you keep the torso fairly upright.
steps.brace: Breathe in and brace the trunk before releasing the hooks and before each rep.
steps.initiate: Bend the knees and push the hips back slightly so you sit down into the bar's path.
steps.concentric: Drive through mid-foot and heels to straighten the legs, keeping your back in contact with the line of the bar.
steps.breathing: Inhale and brace at the top, hold during the descent, exhale as you finish the rep.
steps.eccentric: Lower slowly along the fixed path, knees tracking over the toes.
steps.rom: Go down until thighs are about parallel or slightly below while your lower back stays neutral and heels stay down.
steps.tempo: 3-0-1-0: three seconds down, no pause, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish standing with knees straight but not snapped into lockout.
steps.exit: Rotate the bar back onto the nearest hooks and confirm it has caught before stepping out from under it.

mistakes.m: Feet directly under the bar, which pitches you forward
mistakes.fix: Move the feet forward until you can sit down without your heels lifting.

mistakes.m: Feet too far forward so the lower back rounds
mistakes.fix: Bring the feet back a little and stop the descent before the pelvis tucks.

mistakes.m: Forgetting to set the safety stops
mistakes.fix: Set them before loading, just below your bottom position.

mistakes.m: Bouncing out of the bottom
mistakes.fix: Use a controlled descent and reverse smoothly.

safety: Always set the safety stops; the bar can only move vertically, so you cannot step out from under it.
Rotate the hooks fully on after the last rep before letting go.
Stop with sharp knee or back pain.
checks: Check the bar rotates freely and the hooks engage.
Set safety stops and check plates and collars.
Note whether the bar is counterbalanced so you know the true starting weight.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if your heels lift, the lower back rounds at depth, or you cannot control the lowering.

programming.rehab: A light Smith squat to a comfortable depth gives a stable option when returning to squatting; get guidance from a physiotherapist if you are recovering from injury.
programming.frequency: 1-3 times per week, 48-72 h between hard leg sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Start with the unloaded bar, then add 5-10 kg per set until 10-12 reps leave 2-3 in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: Your last rep should be controlled with full depth and no heel lift.
programming.progression: Double progression: reach the top of the range on all sets, then add 5 kg.
programming.increase: Increase when every set reaches the top of the range with steady technique.
programming.maintain: Keep the load if reps fall short or depth shrinks; reduce it if knees or back feel irritated.

name: Leg press
musclesText: Primary: quadriceps, gluteus maximus. Secondary: adductor magnus, hamstrings.

steps.start: Sit in the 45-degree leg press with your back and hips flat against the pad and feet on the sled.
steps.setup: Adjust the back pad so you can reach depth without your hips lifting. Load plates evenly and check the safety stops or release handles work.
steps.feet: Place your feet hip to shoulder width in the middle of the platform, toes slightly out; a lower placement biases the quads, a higher one the glutes and hamstrings.
steps.grip: Hold the side handles lightly to keep your hips pinned into the seat.
steps.posture: Keep the lower back and pelvis in contact with the pad throughout; head rests back.
steps.brace: Breathe in and brace the trunk before releasing the sled and before each rep.
steps.initiate: Press the sled up slightly, turn the safety handles out, then begin bending the knees.
steps.concentric: Push through the whole foot to straighten the legs, keeping knees in line with toes.
steps.breathing: Inhale and brace at the top, hold as you lower, exhale as you press past the hardest point.
steps.eccentric: Lower the sled under control towards your chest until the knees are deeply bent.
steps.rom: Lower as far as you can without your hips curling off the pad, usually to around 90 degrees of knee bend or a little deeper.
steps.tempo: 3-0-1-0: three seconds down, no pause, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish with the knees almost straight but not locked out.
steps.exit: After the last rep, extend the legs, turn the safety handles back in and lower the sled onto the stops before taking your feet off.

cues: Hips stay glued to the seat

mistakes.m: Lowering so deep the pelvis tucks off the pad
mistakes.fix: Stop the descent just before the hips start to curl.

mistakes.m: Locking the knees out hard
mistakes.fix: Stop just short of full lockout.

mistakes.m: Pressing through the toes so the heels lift
mistakes.fix: Move the feet a bit higher on the platform.

mistakes.m: Knees caving inward
mistakes.fix: Lower the load and keep knees in line with the toes.

mistakes.m: Using very short reps with a heavy stack
mistakes.fix: Reduce the load and use a full, controlled range.

safety: Never lock the knees out under a heavy load.
Engage the safety stops before getting in or out.
Stop with sharp knee pain or back pain, especially if the lower back lifts from the pad.
checks: Check the safety handles move freely and the stops are set.
Check plates are matched on both sides.
Check the back pad angle lets you reach depth with hips down.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load when your hips lift at the bottom, the range shortens, or knees drift inward.

programming.rehab: Light leg presses through a pain-free range are often used in knee rehabilitation; follow a physiotherapist's guidance on range and load.
programming.frequency: 1-3 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Start with the empty sled or a light pair of plates, aiming for 12 controlled reps with 3 left, then add plates.
programming.judgeLoad: The last rep should still reach your full depth with hips pinned; if reps shorten, it is too heavy.
programming.progression: Double progression: reach the top of the range on every set, then add 5-10 kg.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets hit the top of the range with full depth.
programming.maintain: Keep the load if depth or tempo slips; reduce it if you feel knee or back discomfort.

name: Hack squat
musclesText: Primary: quadriceps (especially vastus lateralis and vastus medialis). Secondary: gluteus maximus, adductors.

steps.start: Step into the hack squat machine with your back flat against the angled pad and your shoulders under the shoulder pads.
steps.setup: Adjust the shoulder pads (if adjustable) so they rest firmly on your shoulders when standing tall; load plates evenly and check the safety catch levers.
steps.feet: Feet hip to shoulder width in the middle or slightly low on the platform for quad emphasis, toes slightly out; heels must stay down.
steps.grip: Hold the handles beside the shoulder pads to keep your upper body pinned to the pad.
steps.posture: Keep your entire back, from hips to head, in contact with the pad.
steps.brace: Breathe in and brace before releasing the safety levers and before each rep.
steps.initiate: Stand up slightly, release the safety handles, then bend the knees, letting them travel forward over the toes.
steps.concentric: Drive the platform away through mid-foot and heels until your legs are nearly straight.
steps.breathing: Inhale at the top, hold through the descent, exhale as you pass the hardest part of the ascent.
steps.eccentric: Lower slowly with the knees tracking over the toes and your back on the pad.
steps.rom: Lower to at least parallel and deeper if your hips stay against the pad and heels stay down.
steps.tempo: 3-1-1-0: three seconds down, one-second pause at the bottom, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish with knees softly extended, not snapped into lockout.
steps.exit: After the last rep, re-engage the safety handles at the top and step out only once they are locked.

mistakes.m: Heels lifting at depth
mistakes.fix: Move the feet slightly higher on the platform.

mistakes.m: Hips peeling off the pad
mistakes.fix: Shorten the range a little and reduce the load.

mistakes.m: Bouncing out of the bottom
mistakes.fix: Use a brief pause and control the turnaround.

mistakes.m: Locking out the knees hard
mistakes.fix: Stop just short of lockout to keep tension and protect the knees.

safety: Engage the safety handles before entering and exiting.
Do not lock the knees under heavy loads.
Stop with sharp knee or back pain.
checks: Check the safety levers engage and release properly.
Check the shoulder pads sit firmly and plates are balanced.
Check the platform is clean and dry so feet do not slip.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load when depth shortens, the hips lift off the pad, or the knees drift inward.

programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Start with the empty sled, which already weighs a fair amount, and add plates until 10-12 reps leave 2-3 in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: Final reps should stay deep and controlled; if you start cutting depth, the load is too heavy.
programming.progression: Double progression: add reps up to the top of the range, then add 5-10 kg.
programming.increase: Increase once all sets hit the top of the range with full depth.
programming.maintain: Keep the load the same if depth or tempo drops; reduce it if the knees feel irritated.

name: Bulgarian split squat
musclesText: Primary: quadriceps and gluteus maximus of the front leg. Secondary: adductor magnus, hamstrings, gluteus medius for balance, hip flexors of the rear leg are stretched, trunk stabilisers.

steps.start: Stand about a stride in front of a flat bench, facing away from it, with the top of your rear foot resting on the bench.
steps.setup: Use a stable flat bench at about knee height; place dumbbells beside your front foot if loading.
steps.feet: Front foot far enough forward that the front shin is roughly vertical to slightly forward at the bottom; feet about hip width apart side to side for balance.
steps.grip: Hold dumbbells at your sides with a neutral grip, or place hands on hips when unloaded.
steps.posture: Torso tall or with a slight forward lean (more lean shifts emphasis to the glutes); keep the spine neutral.
steps.brace: Brace the trunk and keep the pelvis square to the front.
steps.initiate: Bend the front knee and drop the back knee straight down towards the floor.
steps.concentric: Drive through the whole front foot to stand, letting the rear leg assist only lightly.
steps.breathing: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you push up.
steps.eccentric: Lower under control until the back knee is just above the floor.
steps.rom: Descend until the front thigh is about parallel or the rear knee nearly touches the floor, without the front heel lifting.
steps.tempo: 3-0-1-0: three seconds down, no pause, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish nearly upright on the front leg, keeping tension, then complete all reps before switching legs.
steps.exit: Step the rear foot down from the bench, set the dumbbells down beside you, then swap sides.

cues: Rear foot is just a kickstand
Drop the back knee straight down

mistakes.m: Front foot too close so the heel lifts
mistakes.fix: Step the front foot further from the bench.

mistakes.m: Pushing mostly with the back leg
mistakes.fix: Shift weight onto the front foot and keep the rear foot relaxed.

mistakes.m: Front knee caving inward
mistakes.fix: Reduce the load and keep the knee over the second and third toes.

mistakes.m: Losing balance
mistakes.fix: Start without weight, widen the feet side to side, or hold a fixed support with one hand.

safety: Use a bench that will not slide and set your foot position before loading.
Start light; balance is often the limiter before strength.
Stop with sharp front-knee pain or discomfort at the front of the rear hip beyond a normal stretch.
checks: Check the bench is stable and at a suitable height.
Clear the area around you in case you need to step out.
Check dumbbell grip and that the floor is not slippery.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if you lose balance, the front knee caves, or you cannot control the lowering.

programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Start with bodyweight for 10 reps per leg, then add dumbbells starting around 6-10 kg each.
programming.judgeLoad: You should finish each leg with 1-3 reps in reserve and still be balanced and controlled.
programming.progression: Double progression: add reps per leg to the top of the range, then add 2 kg per dumbbell.
programming.increase: Increase once all sets reach the top of the range on both legs.
programming.maintain: Keep the load if balance or depth is inconsistent; reduce it if the knee or hip feels irritated.

name: Split squat
musclesText: Primary: quadriceps and gluteus maximus of the front leg. Secondary: adductors, hamstrings, gluteus medius for stability.

steps.start: Stand in a long staggered stance with both feet on the floor, one foot forward and the other back on the ball of the foot.
steps.setup: No equipment is needed; add dumbbells at your sides once bodyweight is easy, and log the extra weight.
steps.feet: Front foot flat, rear foot about a long stride behind on the ball of the foot, feet roughly hip width apart side to side.
steps.grip: Hands on hips, or dumbbells held at your sides with a neutral grip.
steps.posture: Upright torso with a neutral spine and hips square to the front.
steps.brace: Brace the trunk lightly and keep your ribs over your pelvis.
steps.initiate: Bend both knees and drop the back knee straight down; the feet stay in place for the whole set.
steps.concentric: Push through the front foot to rise back up, with the rear leg assisting.
steps.breathing: Inhale on the way down, exhale on the way up.
steps.eccentric: Lower under control until the back knee is just above the floor.
steps.rom: Lower until the back knee nearly touches the floor and the front thigh is about parallel.
steps.tempo: 2-1-1-0: two seconds down, a one-second pause near the floor, one second up.
steps.finish: Stand nearly upright without fully locking the front knee, then repeat on the same side.
steps.exit: Complete all reps on one side, step the feet together, then switch legs.

mistakes.m: Stance too narrow side to side so you wobble
mistakes.fix: Keep the feet on two separate tracks about hip width apart.

mistakes.m: Front heel lifting
mistakes.fix: Lengthen the stance.

mistakes.m: Leaning forward and collapsing the chest
mistakes.fix: Stay tall and control the descent.

mistakes.m: Dropping the back knee onto the floor
mistakes.fix: Stop a few centimetres above, or use a pad under the knee.

safety: Use a pad under the rear knee if you are worried about touching the floor.
Stop with sharp knee pain.
checks: Clear the space and check the floor is not slippery.
Check dumbbells are secure if using them.
reduceLoad: If loaded, reduce weight or return to bodyweight when balance is lost or the front knee caves.
regressions: Assisted split squat holding a support

programming.rehab: A shallow, supported split squat is a common early-stage knee and hip rehabilitation exercise; follow a physiotherapist's guidance on depth.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Begin with bodyweight; once 15 controlled reps per leg are easy, hold light dumbbells.
programming.judgeLoad: You should complete the reps with steady balance and 1-3 reps in reserve.
programming.progression: Add reps, then a pause at the bottom, then light dumbbells, progressing 2 kg per hand.
programming.increase: Progress when all sets reach the top of the range with control.
programming.maintain: Stay at the current level if balance is unsteady or the knee feels irritated.

name: Walking lunges
musclesText: Primary: quadriceps, gluteus maximus. Secondary: adductors, hamstrings, gluteus medius, forearm flexors (grip), trunk stabilisers.

steps.start: Stand tall with feet hip width apart, a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, at the start of a clear walkway.
steps.setup: Choose a straight, clear path of 10-20 metres and pick dumbbells you can grip for the whole set.
steps.feet: Take a long step forward with feet staying on hip-width tracks; the rear heel lifts as you lower.
steps.grip: Hold the dumbbells with a neutral grip, arms straight and relaxed at your sides.
steps.posture: Upright torso, shoulders down and back, eyes forward.
steps.brace: Brace the trunk so the dumbbells do not pull you side to side.
steps.initiate: Step forward and plant the front foot whole, then lower straight down.
steps.concentric: Push through the front foot to rise and bring the rear leg forward straight into the next step.
steps.breathing: Inhale as you step and lower, exhale as you drive up.
steps.eccentric: Lower under control until the back knee is just above the floor.
steps.rom: Front thigh about parallel, back knee a few centimetres from the floor.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-0: two seconds down, no pause, one second up into the next step.
steps.finish: Each rep finishes as you pass through standing and step into the next lunge; finish the set with feet together.
steps.exit: Bring the feet together, stand tall, then squat or hinge to set the dumbbells down at your sides.

mistakes.m: Short steps so the front knee shoots forward and the heel lifts
mistakes.fix: Lengthen the stride.

mistakes.m: Walking on a tightrope
mistakes.fix: Keep the feet on hip-width tracks.

mistakes.m: Letting the torso pitch forward
mistakes.fix: Lighten the dumbbells and stay tall.

mistakes.m: Rushing the reps
mistakes.fix: Pause briefly at the top of each step to regain balance.

safety: Make sure the walkway is clear and the floor is not slippery.
Use dumbbells you can grip securely for the whole walk; if you lose balance, let them drop to the sides rather than twisting to save them.
Stop with sharp knee pain.
checks: Check the path is clear and long enough.
Check dumbbells are secure.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if you lose balance, steps get shorter, or grip fails before the legs.

programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Begin with bodyweight, then dumbbells around 6-10 kg each, choosing a load that leaves 2-3 reps per leg.
programming.judgeLoad: Steps should stay even and controlled through the last reps.
programming.progression: Double progression on reps per leg, then add 2 kg per dumbbell.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets reach the top of the range with even steps.
programming.maintain: Keep the load if balance worsens or grip limits you.

name: Reverse lunges
musclesText: Primary: quadriceps, gluteus maximus. Secondary: adductors, hamstrings, gluteus medius.

steps.start: Stand tall with feet hip width apart.
steps.setup: No equipment needed; hold dumbbells at your sides once bodyweight is easy and log the added weight.
steps.feet: Step one foot straight back about a long stride, landing on the ball of the foot; the front foot stays flat.
steps.grip: Hands on hips or dumbbells at your sides with a neutral grip.
steps.posture: Tall torso with a slight forward lean allowed; neutral spine.
steps.brace: Brace the trunk before each step.
steps.initiate: Shift weight onto the front leg and step back with the other foot.
steps.concentric: Push through the front foot to bring the rear foot back beside it.
steps.breathing: Inhale as you step back, exhale as you return.
steps.eccentric: Lower straight down until the back knee is just above the floor.
steps.rom: Back knee just above the floor, front thigh about parallel.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: two seconds down, one second up, brief pause standing.
steps.finish: Return to standing with feet together, then step back with the other leg.
steps.exit: After the last rep, stand with feet together and set any weights down.

cues: Weight stays on the front foot
Push up through the front heel

mistakes.m: Stepping back too short
mistakes.fix: Step further back so the front shin stays near vertical.

mistakes.m: Pushing off the back foot
mistakes.fix: Return using the front leg.

mistakes.m: Front knee wobbling inward
mistakes.fix: Keep the knee over the toes and slow down.

mistakes.m: Leaning heavily forward
mistakes.fix: Stay tall and brace.

safety: Reverse lunges are usually kinder to the knees than forward lunges, but stop with any sharp knee pain.
Use a support for balance if needed.
checks: Clear space behind you.
Check dumbbells if using them.
reduceLoad: If loaded, reduce weight when you lose balance or cannot control the descent.

programming.rehab: Reverse lunges to a comfortable depth are often used in knee rehabilitation as they are easier to control; follow a physiotherapist's guidance.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Start with bodyweight; when 15 per leg is easy, add light dumbbells.
programming.judgeLoad: You should be stable and controlled on every rep with 1-3 reps in reserve.
programming.progression: Add reps, then dumbbells, increasing 2 kg per hand.
programming.increase: Progress when all sets hit the top of the range cleanly.
programming.maintain: Stay at the same level if balance or knee control slips.

name: Forward lunges
musclesText: Primary: quadriceps, gluteus maximus. Secondary: adductors, hamstrings, gluteus medius.

steps.start: Stand tall with feet hip width apart.
steps.setup: No equipment needed; dumbbells at your sides can be added once bodyweight is easy.
steps.feet: Step one foot forward about a long stride, landing heel first and then the whole foot; the rear heel lifts.
steps.grip: Hands on hips or dumbbells at your sides with a neutral grip.
steps.posture: Upright torso, neutral spine, eyes forward.
steps.brace: Brace the trunk before stepping so you can absorb the landing.
steps.initiate: Step forward, plant the foot, and lower straight down.
steps.concentric: Push firmly off the front foot to drive yourself back to the start position.
steps.breathing: Inhale as you step and lower, exhale as you push back.
steps.eccentric: Decelerate the step and lower under control until the back knee is just above the floor.
steps.rom: Back knee just above the floor and front thigh about parallel.
steps.tempo: 2-0-1-1: two seconds to step and lower, one second to push back, brief pause standing.
steps.finish: Return the front foot beside the other and stand tall before stepping with the other leg.
steps.exit: Finish standing with feet together and set any weights down with a straight back.

cues: Land softly on the whole foot
Push back with the front leg

mistakes.m: Step too short so the knee drives far over the toes
mistakes.fix: Take a longer stride.

mistakes.m: Front heel lifting on landing
mistakes.fix: Land heel first and keep it planted.

mistakes.m: Stumbling on the push back
mistakes.fix: Use a shorter stride or a slower tempo, and stand still between reps.

mistakes.m: Torso collapsing forward
mistakes.fix: Stay upright and reduce any load.

safety: Forward lunges load the front knee more on landing; start with bodyweight and stop with sharp knee pain.
Clear space in front of you.
checks: Clear the area in front.
Check dumbbells and floor grip.
reduceLoad: If loaded, reduce weight when the push back becomes unsteady or the front knee caves.

programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Start with bodyweight, then light dumbbells once 15 per leg is easy.
programming.judgeLoad: Each push back should be smooth and balanced with reps in reserve.
programming.progression: Add reps, then dumbbells, increasing 2 kg per hand.
programming.increase: Progress when all sets reach the top of the range cleanly.
programming.maintain: Stay at the same level if balance or knee control slips.

name: Step-ups
musclesText: Primary: quadriceps, gluteus maximus of the working leg. Secondary: hamstrings, adductors, gluteus medius, calves.

steps.start: Stand facing a stable box or bench about knee height, with one whole foot placed on top.
steps.setup: Use a solid box or bench roughly knee height that will not tip or slide; dumbbells optional and should be logged if used.
steps.feet: Place the whole working foot on the box, heel included; the other foot stays on the floor about hip width.
steps.grip: Hands on hips, arms free for balance, or dumbbells at your sides.
steps.posture: Slight forward lean from the hips with a neutral spine so your chest is over the front foot.
steps.brace: Brace the trunk before each rep.
steps.initiate: Shift your weight onto the top foot and push through it without pushing off the floor foot.
steps.concentric: Drive up through the top foot until you stand tall on the box, bringing the trailing foot up beside it.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you step up, inhale as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower the trailing foot slowly back to the floor by bending the working leg.
steps.rom: Full range from floor to standing tall on the box; use a lower step if the knee caves or you rock off the back foot.
steps.tempo: 1-0-3-0: about one second to step up, no pause, three seconds of controlled lowering, no pause at the floor.
steps.finish: Stand tall on top with hip and knee extended before stepping down.
steps.exit: Complete the reps on one leg, step down, swap legs, and set dumbbells down beside the box.

cues: No bounce off the bottom foot

mistakes.m: Pushing off the bottom foot
mistakes.fix: Keep the floor foot relaxed or lift the toes.

mistakes.m: Box too high so you lean and twist
mistakes.fix: Lower the box to about knee height or less.

mistakes.m: Dropping down quickly
mistakes.fix: Control the lowering for two to three seconds.

mistakes.m: Front knee caving inward
mistakes.fix: Keep the knee over the toes and lighten the load.

safety: Use a stable box; never use an unstable bench or stacked plates.
Start without weight to check balance.
Stop with sharp knee pain.
checks: Check the box or bench is stable and non-slip.
Check height is around knee height or lower.
Clear space around the box.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load or box height if you push off the bottom foot, the knee caves, or you cannot control the lowering.

programming.rehab: Low step-ups with slow lowering are common in knee and ankle rehabilitation; follow a physiotherapist's guidance on height.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Start with bodyweight on a lower box, then hold light dumbbells.
programming.judgeLoad: You should rise smoothly on the working leg alone with reps in reserve.
programming.progression: Add reps, then box height, then dumbbells in 2 kg steps.
programming.increase: Progress when all reps are controlled without pushing off the floor.
programming.maintain: Keep the level if balance or knee control is inconsistent.

name: Leg extension
musclesText: Primary: quadriceps (rectus femoris, vastus lateralis, vastus medialis, vastus intermedius). Secondary: none significant.

steps.start: Sit in the leg extension machine with your back against the pad and shins behind the roller pad.
steps.setup: Adjust the back pad so your knees line up with the machine's pivot point, and set the shin pad just above the ankles. Choose the weight on the stack and the start range if adjustable.
steps.feet: Feet relaxed or slightly pulled up, hip width apart behind the roller.
steps.grip: Hold the side handles firmly to keep your hips in the seat.
steps.posture: Sit tall with hips back in the seat; avoid lifting the hips as you extend.
steps.brace: Lightly brace the trunk and keep the pelvis pinned down.
steps.initiate: Begin by straightening the knees smoothly, without kicking.
steps.concentric: Extend the knees until the legs are straight or nearly straight, squeezing the quads.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you extend, inhale as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower the pad under control until the knees are bent about 90 degrees or slightly more.
steps.rom: Full range from roughly 90 degrees of knee bend to full extension, provided it is pain-free.
steps.tempo: 2-1-3-0: two seconds up, one-second squeeze at the top, three seconds down.
steps.finish: Finish each rep with the legs straight and quads contracted briefly.
steps.exit: Lower the stack gently to rest before sliding out of the machine.

cues: Knee joint lines up with the pivot

mistakes.m: Knees not aligned with the pivot
mistakes.fix: Adjust the back pad until they line up.

mistakes.m: Swinging the weight up
mistakes.fix: Lower the load and use a controlled tempo.

mistakes.m: Hips lifting off the seat
mistakes.fix: Grip the handles and reduce the weight.

mistakes.m: Dropping the stack
mistakes.fix: Control the lowering for two to three seconds.

safety: Stop with sharp pain at the front of the knee; reduce the range or load.
Avoid jerking into full extension under heavy loads.
checks: Align the knee with the pivot and set the shin pad above the ankle.
Check the pin is fully in the stack.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if you cannot hold the top squeeze, the hips lift, or the knee feels irritated.

programming.rehab: Light leg extensions through a pain-free range are commonly used in knee rehabilitation; follow a physiotherapist's guidance on range.
programming.frequency: 1-3 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Choose a light stack weight you can lift for 15 controlled reps with a top pause.
programming.judgeLoad: The top squeeze should still be possible on the final reps.
programming.progression: Double progression: reach the top of the range, then add one stack plate.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets hit the top of the range with a controlled pause.
programming.maintain: Keep the load the same if the top position cannot be held; reduce it with knee discomfort.

name: Wall sit
musclesText: Primary: quadriceps. Secondary: gluteus maximus, adductors.

steps.start: Stand with your back flat against a smooth wall and feet about 40-60 cm in front of it.
steps.setup: Use a smooth, solid wall and a non-slip floor; a timer is helpful.
steps.feet: Feet hip width apart and far enough from the wall that knees sit over the ankles when you are seated.
steps.grip: Arms crossed over the chest, hands resting on the thighs, or by your sides; do not push on the thighs.
steps.posture: Back flat against the wall, head and shoulders touching it.
steps.brace: Brace the trunk gently and keep the lower back in contact with the wall.
steps.initiate: Slide down the wall until your thighs are about parallel to the floor.
steps.concentric: Not applicable: isometric hold. Instead, hold the position by pressing your feet into the floor and back into the wall.
steps.breathing: Breathe steadily throughout the hold; do not hold your breath.
steps.eccentric: Not applicable: isometric hold. Instead, slide back up the wall at the end of the hold.
steps.rom: Thighs about parallel, knees bent around 90 degrees; a higher position is easier.
steps.tempo: Hold for the set time, for example 20-60 s, with no movement.
steps.finish: Finish by sliding back up the wall to standing.
steps.exit: Slide up, step away from the wall, and walk around to recover before the next set.

mistakes.m: Feet too close so knees push over the toes
mistakes.fix: Move the feet further out.

mistakes.m: Pushing hands on the thighs
mistakes.fix: Cross the arms on the chest.

mistakes.m: Holding the breath
mistakes.fix: Breathe in a steady rhythm.

mistakes.m: Sliding lower than you can hold
mistakes.fix: Choose a higher position that you can keep for the full time.

safety: Stop with sharp knee pain; a higher position reduces knee load.
Avoid breath-holding, especially if you have high blood pressure.
checks: Check the wall is smooth and free of obstacles.
Check the floor is not slippery.
reduceLoad: Shorten the hold or raise the position if you cannot keep your back on the wall or the knee feels painful.
progressions: Weighted wall sit with a plate on the thighs

programming.rehab: Short wall sits at a comfortable angle are used in knee and tendon rehabilitation; follow a physiotherapist's guidance on angle and time.
programming.frequency: 2-4 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Begin with a 20-30 s hold at a comfortable depth.
programming.judgeLoad: The last few seconds should be hard but your position should stay unchanged.
programming.progression: Add 5-10 s per session, then lower the position, then add load.
programming.increase: Progress when you can hold all sets for the target time with good position.
programming.maintain: Keep the time the same if you cannot complete it with good form.

name: Sissy squat
musclesText: Primary: quadriceps, especially rectus femoris, which is loaded in a lengthened position because the hips stay extended. Secondary: hip flexors and rectus abdominis holding the straight body line, gastrocnemius and foot muscles for balance on the toes.

steps.start: Stand tall side-on to a rack upright or other fixed support, holding it at about chest height with one hand, feet hip width apart.
steps.setup: Use a sturdy rack upright, a squat rack, or a sissy squat bench that pins your ankles. For the first stage, place a box or bench behind you as a depth target so you only travel to a partial range.
steps.feet: Feet hip width apart and parallel; rise onto the balls of your feet as the knees move forward, keeping the heels lifted throughout the rep.
steps.grip: Hold the support firmly with one hand (or both hands in the early, assisted stage); the free arm can reach forward for counterbalance or cross the chest.
steps.posture: Keep a straight line from knees through hips to shoulders, with glutes squeezed so the hips do not bend; the chin stays slightly tucked.
steps.brace: Brace the abs and squeeze the glutes hard so your trunk and thighs move as one rigid unit while you lean back.
steps.initiate: Lift onto the balls of your feet, then push the knees forward and down while the torso tilts back as a single line.
steps.concentric: Straighten the knees by driving them back under you with the quads, keeping the hips extended, until you are upright again; pull lightly on the support only as much as you need.
steps.breathing: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you rise.
steps.eccentric: Lower slowly, letting the knees travel further forward over the toes and the body lean back, until you reach the depth you have earned at your current stage.
steps.rom: Stage 1: assisted partial range, knees bent about 45 degrees with both hands on the support. Stage 2: deeper partial range to about 90 degrees with one hand. Stage 3: full range, knees close to the floor, using one hand only for balance. Only move on when the current stage is pain-free and controlled.
steps.tempo: 3-1-1-0: three seconds down, one-second pause at the bottom of your current range, about one second up.
steps.finish: Finish standing tall with hips and knees extended, then lower the heels briefly before the next rep if you need to reset balance.
steps.exit: After the final rep, stand fully upright, lower your heels and step away only once you are balanced; unhook the ankles first if using a sissy squat bench.

cues: Go only as deep as you control
Use the support, not your back

mistakes.m: Bending at the hips so it turns into a normal squat
mistakes.fix: Squeeze the glutes and keep the knee-to-shoulder line straight; reduce depth until you can.

mistakes.m: Jumping straight to full range
mistakes.fix: Follow the stages: assisted partial range first, then deeper range, then full range, then added load.

mistakes.m: Dropping into the bottom and bouncing out
mistakes.fix: Use a three-second lowering and a brief pause at your current depth.

mistakes.m: Heels slamming down mid-rep
mistakes.fix: Stay on the balls of your feet for the whole rep.

mistakes.m: Pulling yourself up entirely with the arms
mistakes.fix: Use only as much assistance as needed and reduce the depth instead.

safety: Sissy squats place high load on the knee and patellar tendon; build range over several weeks and stop with any sharp pain at the front of the knee.
Keep at least one hand on a stable support until you can control full range.
Avoid this exercise if you have an irritable knee or patellar tendon problem unless a physiotherapist has cleared it.
checks: Check the support is fixed and will not move when you pull on it.
Check the floor is dry and your shoes grip, or train barefoot on a non-slip surface.
If using a sissy squat bench, check the ankle and calf pads are locked securely.
reduceLoad: Go back a stage (less depth or more hand assistance) if your hips start to bend, you cannot control the lowering, or the knees feel sore later that day or the next morning.
regressions: Assisted partial-range sissy squat to a box
progressions: Full-range sissy squat with one-hand balance
Sissy squat holding a plate at the chest

programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week with at least 72 h between sessions, as the knees need time to adapt.
programming.initialLoad: Start at stage 1: both hands on the support, partial range to about 45 degrees of knee bend, for 2 sets of 8-10.
programming.judgeLoad: The final reps should be challenging but with a straight body line and a full three-second lowering, and your knees should feel fine the next day.
programming.progression: Progress in stages: add reps up to 15, then increase depth (45 to 90 degrees to full range), then reduce hand assistance, then hold a plate to the chest.
programming.increase: Move to the next stage once you can do all sets of 15 controlled reps at the current range with no knee pain over two sessions.
programming.maintain: Stay at the current stage if form or tempo slips, and drop back a stage if the knees ache afterwards.

name: Romanian deadlift
musclesText: Primary: hamstrings (biceps femoris long head, semitendinosus, semimembranosus), gluteus maximus. Secondary: erector spinae, adductor magnus, forearm flexors (grip), trapezius and rhomboids (holding the bar).

steps.start: Stand tall holding the barbell at hip height with straight arms, having unracked it or deadlifted it from the floor for the first rep only.
steps.setup: Set the bar in a rack at roughly mid-thigh height so you can lift it out without bending over; load with collars on both sides.
steps.feet: Feet hip-width apart, toes pointing forward or very slightly out, with the bar over the middle of your feet.
steps.grip: Overhand grip just outside your thighs, arms straight; use a mixed grip or straps only once grip limits the hamstring work.
steps.posture: Chest up, shoulders pulled slightly back and down, neutral spine from head to pelvis with a slight bend in the knees that stays fixed.
steps.brace: Take a breath into your belly and brace as if about to be pushed, and pull the bar into your thighs by tightening your lats.
steps.initiate: Unlock the knees a little, then push your hips straight back as though shutting a car door with your backside.
steps.concentric: From the bottom, drive the hips forward and squeeze the glutes to stand up, keeping the bar dragging up your thighs.
steps.breathing: Breathe in and brace at the top, hold the breath on the way down and up, and exhale as you lock out.
steps.eccentric: Slide the bar down your thighs and past the knees under control, hips moving back and shins staying nearly vertical, until you feel a strong hamstring stretch.
steps.rom: Lower to around mid-shin, or to the point just before your lower back starts to round or your hips stop moving back; for most people that is just below the knee to mid-shin.
steps.tempo: 3-0-1-0: three seconds down, no pause, one second up; keep tension on the hamstrings rather than resting at the bottom.
steps.finish: Stand fully upright with glutes squeezed and ribs down, without leaning back or shrugging.
steps.exit: After the last rep, walk the bar back into the rack and set it on both hooks, or bend the knees and lower it to the floor with a flat back.

cues: Bar stays glued to the legs
Soft knees, then lock them in place
Long spine from head to tailbone

mistakes.m: Turning it into a squat by bending the knees more as you descend.
mistakes.fix: Set a slight knee bend at the top and keep it fixed; think of pushing the hips back to a wall behind you.

mistakes.m: Rounding the lower back to reach the floor.
mistakes.fix: Stop the rep at the point your hips stop travelling back, usually mid-shin, even if the bar is well off the floor.

mistakes.m: Letting the bar drift forward away from the legs.
mistakes.fix: Pull the bar into your thighs with your lats and keep it in contact all the way down.

mistakes.m: Over-extending at the top by leaning back.
mistakes.fix: Finish with hips under your ribs and glutes squeezed, standing tall rather than arching.

mistakes.m: Looking up at the mirror, cranking the neck.
mistakes.fix: Keep your gaze on the floor a couple of metres ahead so the neck follows the spine.

safety: Never trade spinal position for depth; range comes from hamstring flexibility and hip hinge skill.
Start from the rack rather than the floor if pulling from the floor is uncomfortable for your back.
Stop if you feel sharp pain in the back of the thigh, as this can indicate a hamstring strain.
checks: Collars fitted and plates equal on both sides.
Rack hooks set at mid-thigh height so unracking needs no bending.
Enough clear space behind you to push the hips back.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if your lower back rounds before mid-shin, the bar drifts off your legs, or you feel the work mainly in your lower back rather than your hamstrings.
