programming.rehab: Very light Romanian deadlifts with a dowel or empty bar can help rebuild hamstring loading after a strain, ideally under the guidance of a physiotherapist.
programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week, at least 48-72 h after heavy deadlifts or squats.
programming.initialLoad: Start with an empty bar to rehearse the hinge, then add weight until 10 reps feel like 2-3 in reserve with a flat back.
programming.judgeLoad: The right load lets you reach mid-shin with a neutral spine and a strong hamstring stretch, with 1-3 reps left; if the bar speed slows sharply or the back rounds, it is too heavy.
programming.progression: Double progression: work within 8-12 reps; when every set reaches 12 with good form, add 5 kg and drop back to 8.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets hit the top of the rep range at the target RIR with no loss of position.
programming.maintain: Keep the load the same while you are still building reps, and reduce it if hamstring soreness lasts more than 72 hours or form slips.

name: Conventional deadlift
musclesText: Primary: gluteus maximus, hamstrings, erector spinae. Secondary: quadriceps, adductor magnus, latissimus dorsi, trapezius and rhomboids, forearm flexors (grip).

steps.start: Stand with the bar over the middle of your feet, close enough that it is about over your shoelaces.
steps.setup: Load the bar with full-size plates (or blocks under smaller plates) so it sits about 22 cm from the floor, and fit collars.
steps.feet: Feet hip-width apart, toes slightly out, bar over the middle of the foot, roughly 2-3 cm from the shins.
steps.grip: Hinge down and grip the bar just outside your legs with an overhand grip; switch to a mixed or hook grip only for heavy sets.
steps.posture: Bend the knees until the shins touch the bar, hips above knees and below shoulders, shoulders slightly in front of the bar, spine neutral and chest proud.
steps.brace: Take a big breath into the belly, brace hard against a belt if you use one, and pull the slack out of the bar until you hear it click against the plates.
steps.initiate: Push the floor away with your legs while keeping the chest and hips rising together.
steps.concentric: Once the bar passes the knees, drive the hips forward into the bar to stand up, keeping it touching your legs.
steps.breathing: Breathe in and brace before each rep, hold through the lift, and exhale at the top or once the bar is back on the floor.
steps.eccentric: Push the hips back first until the bar passes the knees, then bend the knees to return it to the floor under control along the same path.
steps.rom: Full range from the floor to standing lockout; reset the bar on the floor between reps rather than bouncing it.
steps.tempo: 1-0-X-1: controlled one-second descent, reset briefly on the floor, lift as fast as possible with good position.
steps.finish: Stand tall with hips and knees locked, shoulders over the bar and glutes squeezed, without leaning back.
steps.exit: Lower the final rep to the floor with control, release the grip and stand up before stepping away.

cues: Stand tall, do not lean back

mistakes.m: Hips shooting up first so it becomes a stiff-leg pull.
mistakes.fix: Start with the hips slightly lower, brace harder and think of pushing the floor away rather than pulling with the back.

mistakes.m: Starting with the bar too far from the shins.
mistakes.fix: Set the bar over midfoot before you bend down and do not roll it towards you.

mistakes.m: Jerking the bar off the floor and losing back position.
mistakes.fix: Pull the slack out and build tension before the bar leaves the floor.

mistakes.m: Rounding the lower back during the pull.
mistakes.fix: Reduce the load, brace before every rep and keep the lats tight to hold the bar close.

mistakes.m: Hyperextending at lockout.
mistakes.fix: Finish by squeezing the glutes with ribs stacked over the pelvis.

safety: Reset each rep from a dead stop so your back position is checked before every pull.
Use a mixed grip sparingly and alternate hand positions to limit biceps strain on the supinated arm.
Stop the set if you feel sharp back pain or pain or tingling running down the leg.
checks: Collars on and plates loaded evenly; use bumper plates on a lifting platform if available.
Bar height is standard (full-size plates or blocks) so you are not pulling from too low.
Floor is clear around the bar and chalk or straps are ready if needed.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if the bar leaves the floor with a rounded back, the hips shoot up early, or reps slow to a grind well before the final rep.

programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week; most people do best with one heavy and one lighter session, 72 h apart.
programming.initialLoad: Begin with the empty bar on raised plates and add weight in 10-20 kg jumps until 5 reps feel like 3 in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: Each rep should leave the floor without the back rounding and lock out without hitching; leave 1-3 reps in reserve and keep bar speed reasonably consistent.
programming.progression: Linear or double progression: add 5 kg per session as a beginner, then work in a rep range and add 5 kg when all sets reach the top.
programming.increase: Increase when every set and rep is completed at the target RIR with no change in back position.
programming.maintain: Keep the load the same if the last set slows considerably or your setup varies rep to rep, and reduce it by 10% after a missed rep or a poor week of sleep or recovery.

name: Sumo deadlift
musclesText: Primary: gluteus maximus, quadriceps, adductor magnus and adductor longus. Secondary: hamstrings, erector spinae, trapezius and rhomboids, forearm flexors (grip).

steps.start: Stand behind the bar with a wide stance, shins about a fist-width from the bar and the bar over the middle of your feet.
steps.setup: Use full-size plates or bumper plates with collars so the bar is at standard height; a smooth platform helps your feet grip.
steps.feet: Feet wide, typically 1.5-2 times shoulder width, with toes turned out 30-45 degrees so knees can track over them.
steps.grip: Grip the bar overhand inside your knees at about shoulder width, arms hanging straight down from the shoulders.
steps.posture: Chest tall and torso more upright than a conventional deadlift, hips close to the bar, spine neutral and knees pushed out over the toes.
steps.brace: Breathe into the belly and brace hard, then pull the slack out of the bar while pushing the knees out.
steps.initiate: Spread the floor apart with your feet and push through the whole foot, keeping the chest up as the bar breaks the floor.
steps.concentric: Drive the knees out and the hips forward into the bar, standing up in one smooth movement with the bar close to the body.
steps.breathing: Big breath and brace before each rep, hold it through the lift and exhale at lockout or after setting the bar down.
steps.eccentric: Push the hips back and keep the knees out, lowering the bar in a straight line to the floor under control.
steps.rom: Floor to full hip and knee lockout; reset on the floor each rep.
steps.tempo: 1-0-X-1: controlled descent, brief reset on the floor, lift with intent.
steps.finish: Stand tall with knees and hips locked and glutes squeezed, shoulders level.
steps.exit: Lower the last rep to the floor, keep the stance as you let go, then bring the feet together before stepping away.

mistakes.m: Knees caving in as the bar leaves the floor.
mistakes.fix: Use a stance you can actually push the knees out in, and think of spreading the floor with your feet.

mistakes.m: Stance so wide the hips cannot get close to the bar.
mistakes.fix: Narrow the stance until your shins can be close to vertical with the hips near the bar.

mistakes.m: Hips rising first and turning it into a stiff-leg pull.
mistakes.fix: Wedge the hips close to the bar and drive with the legs before the back.

mistakes.m: Gripping too wide so the arms angle out.
mistakes.fix: Hold the bar about shoulder width so the arms hang straight down.

safety: Warm up the adductors and hips thoroughly; groin strains are the main sumo-specific risk.
Avoid forcing a stance width your hips do not tolerate; a pinching feeling at the front of the hip means narrow the stance.
Reset each rep from a dead stop and stop for any sharp back, hip or groin pain.
checks: Collars on and plates loaded evenly.
Floor surface is not slippery under a wide stance.
Bar is at standard height and parallel to the feet.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if the knees cave, the hips shoot up first, the back rounds off the floor, or you feel strain in the groin.

programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week, 72 h apart from other heavy deadlift or squat work.
programming.initialLoad: Start with a light bar to find your stance, then add weight until 5 reps leave about 3 in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: The bar should break the floor without the hips shooting up and lock out cleanly with 1-3 reps in reserve.
programming.progression: Add 5 kg per session while you can, then switch to double progression in a 3-6 or 6-10 rep range.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets are completed at the target RIR with knees tracking well.
programming.maintain: Hold the load while your stance and starting position are still changing rep to rep, and back off after missed reps or groin discomfort.

name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift
musclesText: Primary: hamstrings (biceps femoris, semitendinosus, semimembranosus), gluteus maximus. Secondary: erector spinae, adductor magnus, forearm flexors (grip), trapezius.

steps.start: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs, palms facing you.
steps.setup: Pick two equal dumbbells from the rack and stand in a clear space; no bench or rack needed.
steps.feet: Feet hip-width apart, toes forward, weight spread through the whole foot.
steps.grip: Overhand grip with palms facing your thighs and the dumbbells touching your legs; arms straight and relaxed.
steps.posture: Chest up, shoulders back and down, neutral spine and a slight, fixed bend in the knees.
steps.brace: Breathe into the belly and brace, and squeeze your armpits to keep the dumbbells close.
steps.initiate: Push the hips back and let the dumbbells slide down the front of your thighs.
steps.concentric: Drive the hips forward and squeeze the glutes to return to standing, dumbbells staying close to the legs.
steps.breathing: Inhale and brace at the top, hold on the way down and up, exhale as you stand tall.
steps.eccentric: Lower the dumbbells down the front of the thighs and shins with the hips moving back until you feel a deep hamstring stretch.
steps.rom: Lower to around mid-shin or until your hips stop moving back, keeping the back flat; the dumbbells do not need to touch the floor.
steps.tempo: 3-0-1-0: three-second lowering, no pause, one second up.
steps.finish: Finish standing tall with hips locked out and glutes squeezed, dumbbells resting against the thighs.
steps.exit: Bend the knees and lower the dumbbells to the floor with a flat back, or stand and walk them back to the rack.

mistakes.m: Letting the dumbbells hang away from the body.
mistakes.fix: Keep them touching your thighs and shins by pulling the shoulders back slightly.

mistakes.m: Bending the knees more and squatting the weight down.
mistakes.fix: Lock the slight knee bend in place and push the hips back.

mistakes.m: Reaching for the floor and rounding the back.
mistakes.fix: Stop when the hips stop moving back; depth comes from hip hinge, not the spine.

mistakes.m: Shrugging the shoulders up during the lift.
mistakes.fix: Keep the shoulders down and back; the arms only hold the weight.

safety: Keep the spine neutral throughout and stop each rep where you lose that position.
Use straps if grip fails long before the hamstrings so you do not compensate by rounding.
Stop for sharp pain at the back of the thigh or pain radiating down the leg.
checks: Dumbbells are a matched pair with secure heads.
Clear space around and behind you.
Footwear is flat and stable.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if your back rounds before mid-shin, the dumbbells drift forward, or grip forces you to cut the range short.

programming.rehab: Light dumbbell RDLs with a slow lowering are a common late-stage hamstring rehabilitation exercise; follow a physiotherapist's plan after an injury.
programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week, 48-72 h between hard hinge sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Choose a pair you can lower to mid-shin for 12 slow reps with 3 reps in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: You should feel a strong hamstring stretch at the bottom with a flat back and 1-3 reps left; grip giving out first means use straps or heavier is not yet appropriate.
programming.progression: Double progression: once you reach 12 reps on all sets, move up 2 kg per hand.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets reach the top of the range with clean form.
programming.maintain: Keep the load while reps are still climbing, and reduce it if the lower back fatigues before the hamstrings.

name: Seated leg curl
musclesText: Primary: hamstrings (biceps femoris long and short heads, semitendinosus, semimembranosus). Secondary: gastrocnemius.

steps.start: Sit in the machine with your back against the pad, the backs of your lower legs resting on the lower roller and the thigh pad locked down over your knees.
steps.setup: Adjust the backrest so your knees line up with the machine's pivot point, set the ankle roller just above the heels, and lower the thigh pad until it presses firmly on your thighs just above the knees.
steps.feet: Feet relaxed and hip-width apart, toes pointing up or slightly pulled towards the shins.
steps.grip: Hold the side handles firmly to keep your hips pinned to the seat.
steps.posture: Sit tall with your back on the pad and your hips at the back of the seat; slight forward lean is fine as it increases the hamstring stretch.
steps.brace: Lightly brace the trunk to stop the hips lifting off the seat.
steps.initiate: Begin by pulling the heels down and back towards the seat.
steps.concentric: Curl the roller under the seat as far as possible, squeezing the hamstrings hard at the end.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you curl, inhale as the weight returns.
steps.eccentric: Let the legs straighten slowly against the resistance, without letting the plates touch.
steps.rom: Go from nearly straight knees to as far under the seat as you can curl; most machines allow about 90-120 degrees of knee flexion.
steps.tempo: 2-1-1-1: one second to curl, one-second squeeze, two seconds to return.
steps.finish: Pause briefly with the legs nearly straight while keeping the stack just off its rest.
steps.exit: Let the weight stack settle, lift the thigh pad and swing your legs out before standing.

cues: Knees in line with the pivot

mistakes.m: Knees not aligned with the machine pivot.
mistakes.fix: Move the backrest until the knee joint lines up with the pivot marker.

mistakes.m: Loose thigh pad letting the hips lift.
mistakes.fix: Lower the pad until it holds your thighs firmly against the seat.

mistakes.m: Using momentum and cutting the range short.
mistakes.fix: Pick a load you can curl fully and return over two seconds.

mistakes.m: Pointing the toes hard and cramping the calves.
mistakes.fix: Keep the ankles relaxed or slightly flexed towards the shins.

safety: Avoid snapping the knees straight at the end of the return.
Hamstring cramps are common; stop the set and stretch gently if one occurs.
Stop if you feel pain behind the knee, which may indicate the pad or pivot is set wrong.
checks: Knee joint lined up with the machine pivot.
Ankle roller sitting just above the heels, not on the calves.
Thigh pad locked and the weight pin fully inserted.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if you cannot complete the full curl, the hips lift off the seat, or the last reps rely on swinging.

programming.rehab: Light seated curls through a pain-free range are useful in later hamstring or knee rehabilitation; follow your physiotherapist's guidance on load.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week, 48 h apart.
programming.initialLoad: Choose a stack weight you can curl for 15 reps with 2-3 reps left and full range.
programming.judgeLoad: Reps should be smooth with a clear squeeze; if the hips lift or the range shortens, the load is too heavy.
programming.progression: Double progression in 10-15 reps; when all sets reach 15, add the smallest stack increment.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets hit the top of the range with a controlled two-second return.
programming.maintain: Keep the load while building reps, and reduce if cramping or pain behind the knee appears.

name: Lying leg curl
musclesText: Primary: hamstrings (biceps femoris, semitendinosus, semimembranosus). Secondary: gastrocnemius.

steps.start: Lie face down on the machine with your knees just off the edge of the pad and the ankle roller resting above your heels.
steps.setup: Adjust the roller so it sits on the lower calf just above the heels, and line your knees up with the machine's pivot point.
steps.feet: Feet hip-width apart with ankles relaxed or slightly flexed.
steps.grip: Hold the handles under the front of the bench to stabilise your upper body.
steps.posture: Lie flat with your hips pressed into the pad; many machines have an angled bench that puts the hips slightly flexed.
steps.brace: Brace lightly and press the front of your hips into the pad.
steps.initiate: Begin by pulling the heels towards your glutes without lifting the hips.
steps.concentric: Curl the roller up as far as you can, squeezing the hamstrings at the top.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower the roller slowly until the knees are almost straight, keeping tension on the hamstrings.
steps.rom: From nearly straight knees to the roller close to your glutes, or as far as you can without the hips lifting.
steps.tempo: 2-1-1-0: one second up, one-second squeeze, two seconds down.
steps.finish: Stop each rep with knees nearly straight and the stack just above its rest before the next rep.
steps.exit: Lower the stack fully, then slide down off the pad and stand up carefully.

mistakes.m: Hips rising off the pad as you curl.
mistakes.fix: Reduce the weight and press the hips into the bench throughout.

mistakes.m: Knees too far up the bench, out of line with the pivot.
mistakes.fix: Slide down until the knees sit just off the edge level with the pivot.

mistakes.m: Dropping the weight on the way down.
mistakes.fix: Control a two-second lowering every rep.

mistakes.m: Arching the lower back to finish the rep.
mistakes.fix: Keep the ribs down and stop where the hamstrings finish the curl.

safety: Avoid kicking the weight up with momentum, which strains the hamstring tendons.
Stop if you feel pain behind the knee or cramping that does not ease.
Keep the lower back neutral and the hips down to avoid lumbar strain.
checks: Ankle roller sits above the heels, not on the Achilles tendon.
Knees aligned with the machine pivot.
Weight pin fully inserted.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if the hips lift, the curl is incomplete, or you need momentum for the last reps.

programming.rehab: Light prone curls in a pain-free range are useful in hamstring rehabilitation once a physiotherapist clears you to load the knee.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week, 48 h apart.
programming.initialLoad: Pick a load you can curl through full range for 15 reps with 2-3 left.
programming.judgeLoad: Reps stay smooth with the hips down; if the hips lift or range shortens, it is too heavy.
programming.progression: Double progression from 10-15 reps; add the smallest stack increment when all sets reach 15.
programming.increase: Increase when every set reaches 15 controlled reps.
programming.maintain: Keep the load while reps are rising, and reduce it if you feel pain behind the knee or persistent cramping.

name: Standing leg curl
musclesText: Primary: hamstrings (biceps femoris, semitendinosus, semimembranosus). Secondary: gastrocnemius, gluteus maximus (hip stabilisation).

steps.start: On a standing leg-curl machine, stand facing the pad with your working thigh against the knee pad and the ankle roller behind your lower calf; with a cable, face the low pulley with the ankle strap on your working leg.
steps.setup: Machine: set the thigh pad so your knee lines up with the pivot and the roller sits just above the heel. Cable: attach an ankle strap to the low pulley and stand about a step away so the cable has tension at the start.
steps.feet: Stand on the non-working leg with a soft knee, foot directly under the hip; the working foot hangs just behind you.
steps.grip: Hold the machine handles or the cable column frame with both hands for balance.
steps.posture: Stand tall with the trunk upright or leaning slightly forward onto the pad, hips square and the working thigh kept vertical.
steps.brace: Brace gently so the pelvis does not twist or arch as the leg curls.
steps.initiate: Start by pulling the heel up towards your glutes while the thigh stays still.
steps.concentric: Curl the heel as high as you can without the thigh moving forward or the hip hitching, squeezing the hamstring at the top.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you curl, inhale as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower the heel slowly until the knee is almost straight, keeping tension in the cable or stack.
steps.rom: From near-straight knee to full knee flexion, roughly heel towards the glute; keep the thigh still so the movement stays at the knee.
steps.tempo: 2-1-1-0: one second up, one-second squeeze, two seconds down.
steps.finish: Pause briefly with the leg almost straight before the next rep, then complete all reps before switching legs.
steps.exit: Lower the weight fully, step out of the machine or unclip the ankle strap, and repeat on the other leg.

cues: Stand tall on the support leg

mistakes.m: Swinging the thigh forward to lift more weight.
mistakes.fix: Keep the knee pointing at the floor and reduce the load.

mistakes.m: Arching the lower back at the top of the curl.
mistakes.fix: Brace the trunk and stop the curl where the hamstring finishes.

mistakes.m: Twisting the hips to the side.
mistakes.fix: Keep both hip bones facing forward and hold the support firmly.

mistakes.m: Locking the standing knee hard.
mistakes.fix: Keep a slight bend in the support leg.

safety: Start light on the cable version, as balance and pelvic control limit the load more than the hamstring at first.
Make sure the ankle strap is snug so it cannot slip off mid-rep.
Stop for pain behind the knee or cramping that does not settle.
checks: Ankle strap fastened securely and clipped to the low pulley, or machine roller set above the heel.
Knee aligned with the machine pivot on the plate-loaded or selectorised version.
Floor around the cable is clear and you have a stable handhold.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if the thigh swings, the hips twist, or the back arches to finish the rep.

programming.rehab: Light single-leg curls are a useful way to load each hamstring separately during rehabilitation; follow a physiotherapist's guidance.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week, 48 h apart.
programming.initialLoad: Pick the lightest stack or cable setting and add weight until 15 reps per leg leave 2-3 in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: You should curl fully without the thigh moving and feel it only in the hamstring; balance problems or swinging mean too heavy.
programming.progression: Double progression; add one cable or stack increment when both legs reach 15 reps on all sets.
programming.increase: Increase when the weaker leg also reaches the top of the range.
programming.maintain: Keep the load while the legs are uneven, and reduce it if form slips or the knee aches.

name: Hip thrust
musclesText: Primary: gluteus maximus. Secondary: hamstrings, quadriceps, adductor magnus, gluteus medius.

steps.start: Sit on the floor with your upper back against the side of a bench and a padded barbell over the crease of your hips.
steps.setup: Use a flat bench about knee height, ideally against a wall or secured so it cannot slide; put a thick bar pad or folded mat on the bar and use full-size plates so you can roll the bar over your legs.
steps.feet: Feet flat, roughly hip to shoulder width, toes slightly out, placed so your shins are vertical at the top.
steps.grip: Hold the bar with both hands just outside your hips to keep it steady and centred.
steps.posture: Lower edge of the shoulder blades on the bench edge, chin tucked with eyes looking forward, ribs down.
steps.brace: Breathe in and brace, tucking the pelvis slightly so the ribs stay down.
steps.initiate: Drive through the heels and the whole foot to lift the hips off the floor.
steps.concentric: Push the hips up until your torso and thighs form a straight line, squeezing the glutes hard, with the torso pivoting on the bench.
steps.breathing: Inhale and brace at the bottom, exhale at or just after the top.
steps.eccentric: Lower the hips under control until the bar is just above the floor or your hips are just short of touching.
steps.rom: From hips near the floor to a full lockout with the thighs parallel to the floor; do not push beyond that into a back arch.
steps.tempo: 2-1-1-0: one second up, one-second hold at the top, two seconds down.
steps.finish: Hold the top with glutes squeezed, chin tucked and ribs down, shins vertical.
steps.exit: Lower the bar to the floor, then roll it down over your thighs or slide out from under it and sit up.

mistakes.m: Arching the lower back to finish the rep.
mistakes.fix: Keep the chin tucked and ribs down, and stop when hips and torso are in line.

mistakes.m: Feet too far forward so the hamstrings take over.
mistakes.fix: Move the feet back until the shins are vertical at lockout.

mistakes.m: Feet too close so the quads dominate and knees ache.
mistakes.fix: Walk the feet out slightly.

mistakes.m: Bench sliding during the set.
mistakes.fix: Put the bench against a wall or a heavy rack, or use a dedicated hip-thrust station.

mistakes.m: Rushing reps without a squeeze.
mistakes.fix: Pause for a second at the top of every rep.

safety: Always pad the bar; the hip bones bruise easily under heavy loads.
Secure the bench so it cannot slide out from behind you.
Stop if you feel pinching at the front of the hip or pain in the lower back.
checks: Bar pad fitted and centred on the bar.
Bench is stable and at a height that hits just below the shoulder blades.
Collars on and plates even on both sides.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if you cannot reach full lockout, the lower back arches to finish, or the bar tilts to one side.

programming.rehab: A bodyweight or light hip thrust is often used to restore glute strength after knee or hip issues; get a physiotherapist's advice if you are recovering from injury.
programming.frequency: 1-3 times per week, 48 h between hard sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Start with the empty bar to learn the position, then add weight until 10 reps with a one-second pause leave 2-3 in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: Every rep should reach a full lockout with a held squeeze; if you cannot pause at the top, the load is too heavy.
programming.progression: Double progression from 8-12 reps; add 5-10 kg when all sets reach 12 with the pause.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets hit the top of the range with a full lockout and pause.
programming.maintain: Keep the load while lockout is still inconsistent, and reduce it if hip or back discomfort appears.

name: Barbell glute bridge
musclesText: Primary: gluteus maximus. Secondary: hamstrings, adductor magnus, gluteus medius.

steps.start: Lie on your back on the floor with knees bent, feet flat, and a padded barbell resting across the crease of your hips.
steps.setup: Use full-size plates so the bar can roll over your legs, wrap the bar in a thick pad and lie on a mat; collars on.
steps.feet: Feet hip-width apart, flat on the floor and about 20-30 cm from your glutes, so your shins are near vertical at the top.
steps.grip: Hold the bar with both hands just outside the hips to keep it centred and steady.
steps.posture: Back and head flat on the floor, ribs down and pelvis slightly tucked.
steps.brace: Inhale and brace the abs, keeping the lower back neutral rather than arched.
steps.initiate: Press through the heels and squeeze the glutes to lift the hips.
steps.concentric: Raise the hips until your knees, hips and shoulders form a straight line, squeezing the glutes hard.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower the hips slowly until the glutes lightly touch the floor.
steps.rom: A short range, from glutes on the floor to hips level with the thighs and torso; shorter than a hip thrust because the upper back stays on the floor.
steps.tempo: 1-2-2-0: one second up, two-second hold at the top, two seconds down.
steps.finish: Hold the top with the glutes squeezed and ribs down, without pushing into an arch.
steps.exit: Lower the hips to the floor, then roll the bar down over your thighs and sit up.

mistakes.m: Arching the lower back at the top.
mistakes.fix: Tuck the pelvis slightly and stop when the hips are in line with the thighs.

mistakes.m: Pushing through the toes so the quads take over.
mistakes.fix: Press through the heels and mid-foot.

mistakes.m: Knees caving inwards.
mistakes.fix: Push the knees slightly out in line with the toes.

mistakes.m: Bouncing the glutes off the floor.
mistakes.fix: Touch the floor lightly and pause before the next rep.

safety: Pad the bar to protect the hip bones.
Keep the lower back neutral to avoid lumbar irritation.
Stop if you feel cramping in the hamstrings; move the feet a little closer.
checks: Thick bar pad in place.
Plates large enough to roll the bar over the legs, or a partner to help load it.
Mat or smooth floor under your back.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if you cannot hold the top for two seconds, the back arches, or the bar tilts.

programming.rehab: A light bridge with a pain-free hold is a gentle way to start loading the glutes after back or hip issues; check with a physiotherapist first if injured.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week, 48 h apart.
programming.initialLoad: Start with the empty bar and add weight until 12 reps with a two-second hold leave 2-3 in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: You should hold every rep at the top without the back arching; if the hold breaks, reduce the weight.
programming.progression: Double progression from 10-15 reps; add 5-10 kg when all sets reach 15.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets reach the top of the range with the full hold.
programming.maintain: Keep the load while holds are still shaky, and reduce it if the lower back takes over.

name: Single-leg glute bridge
musclesText: Primary: gluteus maximus, gluteus medius. Secondary: hamstrings, rectus abdominis and obliques (pelvic control).

steps.start: Lie on your back on a mat with one knee bent and that foot flat on the floor; hold the other leg straight in the air or with the knee pulled to the chest.
steps.setup: No equipment needed beyond a mat; for extra load you can later rest a dumbbell or plate on the working hip.
steps.feet: Working foot flat under the knee, about 20-30 cm from your glutes, centred under the hip.
steps.grip: Arms flat on the floor at your sides, palms down, for balance; hugging the free knee to the chest makes it harder to arch the back.
steps.posture: Head and shoulders on the floor, ribs down, pelvis level.
steps.brace: Brace the abs to stop the pelvis rotating or dropping on the free-leg side.
steps.initiate: Press through the heel of the planted foot and squeeze the glute on that side.
steps.concentric: Lift the hips until the working thigh and torso form a straight line, keeping both hip bones level.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower the hips slowly to just above the floor without letting the pelvis twist.
steps.rom: From the glutes just off the floor to a straight line from knee to shoulder on the working side.
steps.tempo: 1-2-2-0: one second up, two-second hold, two seconds down.
steps.finish: Hold the top with the pelvis level and the glute squeezed.
steps.exit: Complete the reps, lower the hips, put the free foot down and switch sides.

mistakes.m: Pelvis dropping on the free-leg side.
mistakes.fix: Brace the abs and think of keeping a level tray on your hips; reduce the height if needed.

mistakes.m: Pushing through the toes and feeling it in the quads.
mistakes.fix: Press through the heel and keep the shin near vertical.

mistakes.m: Arching the lower back to get higher.
mistakes.fix: Stop when the thigh and torso are in line.

mistakes.m: Hamstring cramping.
mistakes.fix: Move the foot a little closer to the glutes.

safety: Keep the range pain free if you have lower back or hip discomfort.
Stop if the hamstring cramps hard; stretch gently and shorten the foot distance.
Avoid twisting through the lower back to complete reps.
checks: Mat on a flat, non-slip surface.
Enough space to extend the free leg.
If loading, the dumbbell or plate is placed securely on the hip.
reduceLoad: Use the two-leg version if your pelvis cannot stay level or you feel it more in the lower back than the glute.

programming.rehab: A common early rehabilitation exercise for glute strength and pelvic control after knee, hip or back issues; use a pain-free range and follow a physiotherapist's advice.
programming.frequency: 2-4 times per week; light enough to use as a warm-up most days.
programming.initialLoad: Start with bodyweight and the free knee hugged to the chest; progress to holding the free leg straight.
programming.judgeLoad: Each rep should finish with a level pelvis and a two-second hold; if not, the variation is too hard.
programming.progression: Add reps up to 15-20 per leg, then lengthen the hold, elevate the foot or add a light weight.
programming.increase: Increase difficulty when you can do 15 controlled reps per leg with level hips.
programming.maintain: Stay at the same level while the weaker side lags, and step back if back or knee pain appears.

name: Cable pull-through
musclesText: Primary: gluteus maximus, hamstrings. Secondary: erector spinae, adductor magnus, forearm flexors.

steps.start: Stand facing away from a low cable pulley, holding a rope attachment between your legs, and walk forward until the stack lifts.
steps.setup: Set the pulley at the lowest position and attach a rope; step one to two big steps away so there is tension even at the bottom.
steps.feet: Feet a little wider than shoulder width, toes slightly out, with the cable running between the feet.
steps.grip: Hold one end of the rope in each hand with a neutral grip, arms straight and hands between the thighs.
steps.posture: Neutral spine, chest up and a soft bend in the knees, weight in the mid-foot and heels.
steps.brace: Brace the trunk before each rep so the hinge happens at the hips, not the lower back.
steps.initiate: Push the hips back and let the rope pull your hands back through your legs.
steps.concentric: Drive the hips forward and squeeze the glutes to stand tall, arms staying straight and passive.
steps.breathing: Inhale as you hinge back, exhale as you drive the hips through.
steps.eccentric: Let the cable pull your hips back into a hinge under control until you feel a hamstring stretch, keeping the back flat.
steps.rom: Hinge until the torso is about 45 degrees or just above, or until you feel a strong hamstring stretch without the back rounding.
steps.tempo: 2-1-1-0: two seconds back, one-second drive forward, one-second squeeze at the top.
steps.finish: Stand tall with the glutes squeezed and the hips fully extended, without leaning back.
steps.exit: Walk back towards the pulley to let the stack rest, then release the rope.

mistakes.m: Pulling with the arms.
mistakes.fix: Keep the arms straight and relaxed; the hips move the weight.

mistakes.m: Squatting down instead of hinging.
mistakes.fix: Keep a soft knee bend fixed and push the hips back.

mistakes.m: Leaning back at the top.
mistakes.fix: Finish upright with the ribs over the pelvis.

mistakes.m: Standing too close so the stack touches down.
mistakes.fix: Walk further from the pulley so there is tension throughout.

safety: Step away from the column carefully, as the cable can pull you backwards.
Keep the spine neutral; the low pull angle is forgiving but rounding still loads the lower back.
Stop for back pain or a sharp hamstring pull.
checks: Pulley at the lowest setting and rope clipped firmly.
Clear space in front of you to walk out.
Weight pin fully inserted.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if the cable pulls you off balance, the arms start pulling, or the back rounds.

programming.rehab: A light pull-through is a back-friendly way to relearn the hip hinge after lower back pain; seek a physiotherapist's guidance if symptoms persist.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week, 48 h apart.
programming.initialLoad: Choose a stack weight that gives 15 controlled reps with 2-3 in reserve and no loss of balance.
programming.judgeLoad: You should feel the glutes and hamstrings rather than the lower back; if balance or posture fails, it is too heavy.
programming.progression: Double progression from 12-15 reps; add one stack increment when all sets reach 15.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets reach 15 with a full squeeze and stable stance.
programming.maintain: Keep the load while you are still finding the hinge, and reduce it if the back works harder than the hips.

name: Cable glute kickback
musclesText: Primary: gluteus maximus. Secondary: hamstrings, gluteus medius.

steps.start: Stand facing a low cable pulley with an ankle strap on your working leg, hinged slightly forward and holding the frame.
steps.setup: Set the pulley at the lowest position and fasten the ankle strap snugly around the lower shin just above the ankle.
steps.feet: Stand on the non-working leg, about half a step back from the column, with a soft knee; working foot just behind the standing foot.
steps.grip: Hold the cable column frame or a handle with both hands for balance.
steps.posture: Hinge forward from the hips about 30-45 degrees with a neutral spine and the hips square to the column.
steps.brace: Brace your trunk so the lower back stays still while the leg moves.
steps.initiate: Start by squeezing the glute and pushing the heel back.
steps.concentric: Kick the leg back and slightly up, with a soft bend or nearly straight knee, until the hip is fully extended.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you kick back, inhale as you return.
steps.eccentric: Let the leg return forward slowly until it is just in front of the standing leg, keeping tension in the cable.
steps.rom: From the foot slightly in front of the body to full hip extension; stop before the lower back arches.
steps.tempo: 2-1-1-0: one second back, one-second squeeze, two seconds forward.
steps.finish: Hold the top briefly with the glute squeezed and the pelvis square.
steps.exit: Finish all reps, return the leg, unclip the ankle strap and repeat on the other side.

mistakes.m: Arching the lower back to lift the leg higher.
mistakes.fix: Stop at full hip extension; the leg does not need to go high.

mistakes.m: Rotating the hip open to the side.
mistakes.fix: Keep both hip bones pointing at the column.

mistakes.m: Swinging the leg with momentum.
mistakes.fix: Reduce the load and pause at the top of each rep.

mistakes.m: Standing upright so the glute range is short.
mistakes.fix: Hinge forward slightly so the hip starts flexed.

safety: Keep the load modest; this exercise is about control, and heavy swinging loads the lower back.
Make sure the ankle strap is secure before you start.
Stop if you feel pinching in the hip or lower back pain.
checks: Ankle strap secure and clipped to the low pulley.
Stable handhold on the column.
Pin fully inserted and the floor dry.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if the lower back arches, the hips rotate, or you cannot pause at the top.

programming.rehab: Light kickbacks with a pause are a useful way to target the glutes after hip or back issues; follow a physiotherapist's plan if you are rehabilitating.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Start with the lightest stack setting and increase until 15 reps per leg with a pause leave 2 in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: You should feel the glute with no lower back arching; swinging or twisting means too heavy.
programming.progression: Double progression from 12-15 reps per leg; add one stack increment when both legs reach 15.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets on both legs reach the top of the range with pauses.
programming.maintain: Keep the load while the weaker side catches up, and reduce if the lower back arches.

name: Good morning
musclesText: Primary: hamstrings, erector spinae. Secondary: gluteus maximus, adductor magnus, upper back (holding the bar).

steps.start: Stand under a barbell in a squat rack with the bar on your upper traps, as for a high-bar back squat.
steps.setup: Set the bar at mid-chest height in the rack and the safety arms just below the lowest bar position you will reach; start much lighter than your Romanian deadlift.
steps.feet: Feet hip to shoulder width, toes forward or slightly out.
steps.grip: Grip the bar just outside the shoulders, pulling it firmly into the upper traps with elbows pointing down.
steps.posture: Chest up, upper back tight, neutral spine and a slight knee bend.
steps.brace: Take a big breath into the belly and brace hard before each rep.
steps.initiate: Push the hips straight back while the bar stays over the middle of the foot.
steps.concentric: Drive the hips forward and lift the chest together to return to standing, squeezing the glutes.
steps.breathing: Inhale and brace at the top, hold during the rep, exhale at the top.
steps.eccentric: Hinge forward with the knees softly bent until the torso is near parallel or you feel a strong hamstring stretch, keeping the back flat.
steps.rom: Lower the torso to about 45 degrees at first, progressing towards parallel only if your back stays neutral.
steps.tempo: 3-0-1-0: three seconds down, no pause, one second up.
steps.finish: Stand tall with hips locked and the bar still tight on the traps.
steps.exit: Walk forward into the rack and set the bar on both hooks before stepping out.

mistakes.m: Rounding the back to go lower.
mistakes.fix: Shorten the range and keep the chest proud.

mistakes.m: Bending the knees and turning it into a squat.
mistakes.fix: Keep the slight knee bend fixed.

mistakes.m: Letting the bar roll up towards the neck.
mistakes.fix: Grip firmly and pull the bar down into the traps.

mistakes.m: Loading it like a deadlift.
mistakes.fix: Use a fraction of your deadlift, often 30-50% of your squat to start.

safety: The load sits far from the hips, so the lower back takes high stress; increase load slowly.
Always use safety arms in the rack.
Stop for any sharp back pain or pain travelling down the leg.
checks: Safety arms set just below your deepest bar position.
Collars on and plates even.
Bar centred on the back before unracking.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if the back rounds, the bar shifts on the back, or the depth gets shorter during the set.

programming.frequency: 1 time per week, or 2 light sessions, away from heavy deadlifts.
programming.initialLoad: Start with the empty bar and add small amounts until 8 reps feel like 3 in reserve.
programming.judgeLoad: Every rep should be smooth with a flat back; slowing sharply or rounding means too heavy.
programming.progression: Double progression from 8-12 reps; add 2.5-5 kg when all sets reach 12.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets reach the top of the range with the same depth.
programming.maintain: Keep the load the same while depth or back position varies, and reduce it after any back niggle.

name: Nordic hamstring curl
musclesText: Primary: hamstrings (biceps femoris, semitendinosus, semimembranosus), working eccentrically. Secondary: gluteus maximus, gastrocnemius, rectus abdominis (holding a straight line).

steps.start: Kneel upright on a padded mat with your ankles anchored under a partner's hands, a Nordic bench, a loaded barbell or a secure low bar.
steps.setup: Put a thick pad under your knees and anchor your heels securely; for the band-assisted progression, attach a strong band high behind you and loop it under your arms.
steps.feet: Knees hip-width apart, ankles hooked under the anchor so the heels cannot lift.
steps.grip: Cross your arms over your chest, or hold the hands ready in front of the chest to catch yourself.
steps.posture: Body in one straight line from knees to head, hips extended and glutes squeezed.
steps.brace: Brace the abs and glutes so you hinge only at the knees, never at the hips.
steps.initiate: Begin by slowly leaning forward as a single straight line from the knees.
steps.concentric: Pull yourself back up with the hamstrings if you can; otherwise push off the floor with your hands just enough to return.
steps.breathing: Breathe out slowly as you lower, and breathe in at the top before the next rep.
steps.eccentric: Lower as slowly as possible, resisting the fall with the hamstrings until you can no longer hold it, then catch yourself with the hands in a push-up position.
steps.rom: Lower as far as you can control; beginners may only control the first third, which is fine. Progressions: partial-range lowers, band-assisted lowers, full lowers with a hand push back, then full concentric return.
steps.tempo: 5-0-X-0: aim for a three- to five-second lowering, then an assisted return.
steps.finish: Return to the upright kneeling position with hips straight.
steps.exit: Catch yourself with your hands on the final rep, kneel up and release your ankles from the anchor.

mistakes.m: Bending at the hips to make it easier.
mistakes.fix: Squeeze the glutes and keep the hips extended; stop the range sooner if needed.

mistakes.m: Dropping quickly after the first few centimetres.
mistakes.fix: Use a band or a shorter range so you can control the whole lower.

mistakes.m: Anchor not secure so the heels lift.
mistakes.fix: Use a partner, Nordic bench or heavy barbell and check it before each set.

mistakes.m: Doing too many reps too soon.
mistakes.fix: Start with 1-2 sets of 3-5 and build slowly.

safety: Expect strong muscle soreness the first time; start with low volume.
Stop at once for a sharp pain in the hamstring, which may indicate a strain.
Pad the knees and make sure the anchor cannot move.
checks: Ankles firmly anchored and the anchor cannot slide.
Thick pad under the knees.
Clear floor in front for the hand catch.
reduceLoad: Regress to a shorter range or band assistance if you cannot control the first half of the lowering or if hips start bending.

programming.rehab: Nordic curls are well researched for reducing hamstring strain risk; after an injury, introduce them only under a physiotherapist's guidance.
programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week; avoid the day before sprinting or heavy leg work in the early weeks.
programming.initialLoad: Start with the band-assisted or partial-range version for 2 sets of 3-5 reps.
programming.judgeLoad: You should control at least a three-second lowering; a sudden drop early means use more help.
programming.progression: Progress by lowering further, then reducing band help, then adding reps, then adding a weight plate held at the chest.
programming.increase: Move to the next progression when you can control 3 sets of 6 slow lowers.
programming.maintain: Stay at the same level while soreness lasts more than 72 h, and reduce volume before competition or sprint weeks.

name: Glute-ham raise
musclesText: Primary: hamstrings (biceps femoris, semitendinosus, semimembranosus). Secondary: gluteus maximus, gastrocnemius, erector spinae.

steps.start: Kneel on the glute-ham developer with your feet against the footplate, ankles locked under the rollers and the front of the thighs on the pad.
steps.setup: Adjust the footplate so your knees sit just behind the pad's highest point; the pad should be under the lower thighs, not the kneecaps.
steps.feet: Balls of the feet pressed against the footplate, ankles secured under the rollers.
steps.grip: Arms crossed over the chest or behind the head; hands in front of the chest are easier.
steps.posture: Torso upright and in line with the thighs, hips extended, glutes squeezed.
steps.brace: Brace the abs to keep a straight line from knees to shoulders.
steps.initiate: Push the toes into the footplate and slowly lean forward as one unit.
steps.concentric: From horizontal, drive the toes into the plate and curl your body back up with the hamstrings until the torso is upright, hips staying extended.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower in a straight line from the knees until your body is about parallel to the floor.
steps.rom: From torso horizontal to upright kneeling; beginners may start from a hip-flexed position and extend the hips first, then curl.
steps.tempo: 3-0-1-1: three seconds down, curl up in one second, one-second pause at the top.
steps.finish: Finish with the torso upright and the hamstrings and glutes squeezed.
steps.exit: Lower to the horizontal or let the hips bend, then put your hands on the handles and unhook your ankles before stepping off.

mistakes.m: Bending at the hips and pushing up with the back.
mistakes.fix: Squeeze the glutes and keep a straight line; use a shorter range or band help.

mistakes.m: Pad sitting on the kneecaps.
mistakes.fix: Move the footplate back so the pad is under the lower thighs.

mistakes.m: Dropping on the lowering.
mistakes.fix: Lower in three seconds and only as far as you can control.

mistakes.m: Ankles loose in the rollers.
mistakes.fix: Tighten the rollers so the heels cannot lift.

safety: Set the machine correctly to avoid pressure on the kneecaps.
Start with low volume; GHRs produce strong hamstring soreness.
Stop for sharp hamstring or knee pain.
checks: Footplate distance and roller height adjusted and locked.
Machine stable on the floor.
Ankle rollers secure around the lower legs.
reduceLoad: Regress if you cannot keep the hips straight, if the lowering speeds up, or if the knees hurt.

programming.frequency: 1-2 times per week, 72 h apart.
programming.initialLoad: Start with assisted or partial range for 3 sets of 5.
programming.judgeLoad: Every rep should keep a straight hip line; if not, use more assistance.
programming.progression: Add range, then reps, then hold a weight plate at the chest.
programming.increase: Progress when 3 sets of 10 full reps are completed with control.
programming.maintain: Keep the variation the same while soreness is high, and regress if the hips start bending.

name: Kettlebell swing
musclesText: Primary: gluteus maximus, hamstrings. Secondary: erector spinae, abdominal muscles, forearm flexors, upper back; cardiovascular system.

steps.start: Stand with a kettlebell on the floor about 30 cm in front of your feet, hinge down and grip the handle with both hands.
steps.setup: Choose a bell you can swing to chest height with hip power alone; clear space in front and behind you.
steps.feet: Feet just wider than shoulder width, toes slightly out, weight through the whole foot.
steps.grip: Both hands on the handle, overhand grip, arms straight; tilt the bell slightly back towards you.
steps.posture: Hinged with a flat back, hips higher than the knees and shoulders over the bell.
steps.brace: Brace the abs and tighten the lats before you hike the bell back.
steps.initiate: Hike the bell back between your legs like a ball snapped in rugby or American football, keeping it above the knees.
steps.concentric: Drive the hips forward forcefully, squeezing the glutes so the bell floats to about chest height, arms straight and relaxed.
steps.breathing: Exhale sharply at the top as the hips snap forward, inhale as the bell swings back.
steps.eccentric: Let the bell fall and hinge as the forearms meet the inner thighs, receiving it back between the legs.
steps.rom: The bell travels from between the thighs to about chest or shoulder height; this is a Russian swing, not overhead.
steps.tempo: Swing rhythm is ballistic: quick hip snap, float at the top, let gravity bring it back.
steps.finish: Stand tall at the top with the glutes squeezed and a straight line from feet to head.
steps.exit: On the last rep, hike the bell back once more and park it on the floor in front of you with a flat back.

mistakes.m: Squatting the swing instead of hinging.
mistakes.fix: Hips go back more than down; shins stay nearly vertical.

mistakes.m: Lifting with the arms.
mistakes.fix: Let the hips drive it; the arms only guide.

mistakes.m: Leaning back at the top.
mistakes.fix: Finish standing tall like a standing plank.

mistakes.m: Hinging too early so the bell drags low.
mistakes.fix: Wait until the forearms touch the thighs before you hinge.

mistakes.m: Rounded back at the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Hike higher and lighter, keeping a flat back.

safety: Use a bell light enough to keep the back flat at the bottom.
Check the space in front and behind you is clear.
Stop for any back pain or loss of grip.
checks: Handle smooth and dry; use chalk if needed.
Clear space around you.
Floor flat and non-slip.
reduceLoad: Reduce the bell if the back rounds, the arms lift it, or the bell height drops sharply.

programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Most beginners start with 12-16 kg for women and 16-20 kg for men, adjusted to ability.
programming.judgeLoad: Each swing should reach chest height with crisp hip snap; power drop means stop the set.
programming.progression: Add reps or sets, then move up 4 kg to the next bell.
programming.increase: Increase when you can do 10 sets of 10 with crisp swings and good form.
programming.maintain: Keep the bell the same while technique varies, and reduce for back fatigue.

name: Reverse hyperextension
musclesText: Primary: gluteus maximus, hamstrings. Secondary: erector spinae, quadratus lumborum.

steps.start: Lie face down on a reverse hyper machine or a high bench with your hips at the edge, legs hanging down and hands gripping the handles.
steps.setup: On a reverse hyper machine, attach the strap or roller around your lower legs and load lightly. On a high bench, lie so the hip bones sit just over the edge and your feet can hang free.
steps.feet: Legs together or hip-width apart, toes pointed down at the start.
steps.grip: Hold the handles or the bench edge firmly to stop the upper body sliding.
steps.posture: Torso flat and supported on the pad, head neutral, hips just over the edge.
steps.brace: Brace the abs lightly and keep the upper body pinned to the pad.
steps.initiate: Squeeze the glutes and begin lifting the legs from the hips.
steps.concentric: Raise the legs until they are in line with the torso, squeezing the glutes at the top.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Lower the legs with control rather than letting them swing back underneath.
steps.rom: From hips flexed to legs level with the torso; do not lift above horizontal into a lumbar arch.
steps.tempo: 2-1-1-0: one second up, one-second squeeze, two seconds down.
steps.finish: Hold the top briefly with the glutes squeezed and the legs level with the torso.
steps.exit: Let the legs return, then step down carefully and remove the strap.

mistakes.m: Swinging the legs with momentum.
mistakes.fix: Slow down and pause at the top.

mistakes.m: Lifting the legs above horizontal and arching the back.
mistakes.fix: Stop when the legs reach torso level.

mistakes.m: Hips too far onto the pad.
mistakes.fix: Slide forward until the hip bones are at the edge.

mistakes.m: Loading too heavily too soon.
mistakes.fix: Start with bodyweight and add load in small steps.

safety: Keep the range to horizontal to avoid lumbar compression.
Stop for sharp back pain or pain radiating down the leg.
Ensure the bench or machine is stable.
checks: Machine strap or roller secure; pendulum swing area clear.
Bench is stable and high enough for the feet to hang free.
Handles secure and dry.
reduceLoad: Reduce the load if you cannot pause at the top or you feel the lower back more than the glutes.

programming.rehab: Light reverse hypers are often used to strengthen the posterior chain for lower back health; follow a physiotherapist's advice if you have back pain.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Start with bodyweight for 15 reps before adding light load.
programming.judgeLoad: You should feel the glutes with no lumbar arching or swinging.
programming.progression: Double progression: add reps up to 15-20, then add a small load.
programming.increase: Increase when all sets reach 15-20 with a full pause.
programming.maintain: Keep the load while you still need momentum, and reduce for back discomfort.

name: Standard plank
musclesText: Primary: rectus abdominis, transversus abdominis. Secondary: internal and external obliques, anterior deltoid, serratus anterior, gluteus maximus, quadriceps.

steps.start: Lie face down on a mat with your forearms on the floor, elbows directly under your shoulders and legs extended behind you.
steps.setup: Use a mat for elbow comfort on a flat, non-slip surface. No other equipment is needed.
steps.feet: Set your feet hip-width apart with your toes tucked under; a wider stance is easier to balance, a narrower one harder.
steps.grip: Forearms parallel or hands lightly clasped, pressing the forearms into the floor as if pushing it away so your upper back does not sag between the shoulder blades.
steps.posture: Lift into a straight line from head to heels: neck neutral with your gaze at the floor just ahead of your hands, ribs down and pelvis slightly tucked.
steps.brace: Squeeze your glutes, pull your ribcage towards your pelvis and tense your abdominal wall as if bracing for a light poke in the stomach.
steps.initiate: From the floor, brace first and then push up through your forearms and toes to lift your hips and knees together.
steps.concentric: Not applicable: isometric hold. Instead, keep pushing the floor away and keep the glutes and abs switched on for the whole hold without letting the hips drift.
steps.breathing: Breathe slowly and steadily through the nose or pursed lips, keeping the brace; do not hold your breath for the full set.
steps.eccentric: Not applicable: isometric hold. To finish, lower your knees to the mat under control rather than dropping your hips first.
steps.rom: Hold only while you can keep a straight line; the set ends when your lower back starts to sag or your hips pike up.
steps.tempo: Steady isometric hold, typically 20-60 s, with slow even breathing.
steps.finish: End the hold by lowering your knees, then your hips, back to the mat.
steps.exit: Rest on your knees or roll onto your back before standing up slowly.

mistakes.m: Hips sagging towards the floor, arching the lower back.
mistakes.fix: Squeeze the glutes, tuck the pelvis slightly and shorten the hold to what you can do with good form.

mistakes.m: Hips piked high to make the hold easier.
mistakes.fix: Lower the hips until your shoulders, hips and ankles line up; use a mirror or video.

mistakes.m: Shoulders collapsing so the shoulder blades pinch together.
mistakes.fix: Actively push your forearms into the floor to spread the upper back.

mistakes.m: Holding your breath and turning red.
mistakes.fix: Practise short holds while breathing slowly behind the brace.

safety: Stop if you feel pain in the lower back rather than effort in the abdomen; it usually means the hips have sagged.
If you have shoulder pain, try the plank from the hands on an incline or reduce hold time.
Long holds beyond about 60 s add little; progress by making the position harder instead.
checks: Use a mat on a non-slip floor to protect your elbows.
Clear space around you so you can drop to your knees safely.
reduceLoad: Shorten the hold or drop to a kneeling plank when your lower back starts to ache, your hips sag or rise, or you cannot breathe steadily behind the brace.
regressions: Incline plank with hands on a bench

programming.rehab: A short kneeling or incline plank is a useful early core exercise after back pain; build tolerance gradually and see a physiotherapist if symptoms persist.
programming.frequency: 2-4 times per week; it is low fatigue and can be done after most sessions.
programming.initialLoad: Start with the longest hold you can do with perfect form minus about 10 s.
programming.judgeLoad: You should finish each hold with a few more seconds possible, form intact and breathing controlled.
programming.progression: Add 5-10 s per hold each week until you reach about 60 s, then move to a harder variation.
programming.increase: Increase when every set reaches the top of the target time with a straight line and steady breathing. Training your abs strengthens them but does not spot-reduce belly fat; fat loss comes from an overall energy deficit.
programming.maintain: Keep the time the same if form slips near the end, and reduce it after a poor night or if your lower back complains.

name: Side plank
musclesText: Primary: internal and external obliques, quadratus lumborum. Secondary: rectus abdominis, transversus abdominis, gluteus medius, deltoid, hip adductors of the top leg.

steps.start: Lie on your side on a mat with your bottom forearm on the floor, elbow directly under your shoulder, and legs straight and stacked.
steps.setup: Use a mat for the supporting elbow and hip. A wall behind you can help you check alignment.
steps.feet: Stack your feet, or place the top foot in front of the bottom foot for a wider, easier base.
steps.grip: Bottom forearm flat on the floor pointing forwards; rest the top hand on your hip or hold it towards the ceiling.
steps.posture: Keep your head, ribs, hips and ankles in one straight line, chest facing forwards rather than rolling towards the floor.
steps.brace: Brace your abs, squeeze your glutes and pull the bottom side of your waist up away from the floor.
steps.initiate: Press the forearm into the floor and lift your hips until your body forms a straight line.
steps.concentric: Not applicable: isometric hold. Instead, keep driving the bottom hip up and the shoulder away from your ear throughout.
steps.breathing: Breathe slowly and steadily behind the brace; keep the breathing quiet.
steps.eccentric: Not applicable: isometric hold. Finish by lowering the hip to the mat under control.
steps.rom: Hold only while your hips stay level with your shoulders and feet; stop when the hips drop.
steps.tempo: Steady isometric hold, typically 15-45 s per side.
steps.finish: Lower your hip to the mat, then switch sides and match the time.
steps.exit: Roll onto your back or sit up slowly; perform the same time on both sides.

mistakes.m: Hips sagging towards the floor.
mistakes.fix: Lift the bottom hip and shorten the hold, or bend the knees to regress.

mistakes.m: Rolling the chest towards the floor.
mistakes.fix: Stack the shoulders and hips vertically; touch a wall behind you to check.

mistakes.m: Shoulder hunched up by the ear.
mistakes.fix: Push the forearm down and lengthen the neck.

mistakes.m: Only training your favourite side.
mistakes.fix: Do equal time on both sides, starting with the weaker one.

safety: Stop if you feel pain at the supporting shoulder; try the knees-bent version or a shorter hold.
People with shoulder instability should build up gradually with a physiotherapist's input.
Do not let the hips sag into the lower back, which loads the spine rather than the obliques.
checks: Use a mat thick enough to protect the elbow and hip.
Make sure there is nothing to fall onto behind or in front of you.
reduceLoad: Shorten the hold or bend your knees when your hips drop, your shoulder aches or you cannot keep the chest facing forwards.
regressions: Side plank with hand on a bench

programming.rehab: The knees-bent side plank is often used in back rehabilitation to build lateral trunk endurance; a physiotherapist can advise on dosage.
programming.frequency: 2-4 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Start with a hold you can manage on your weaker side with clean alignment.
programming.judgeLoad: Finish each hold with a few seconds left in reserve and the hips still level.
programming.progression: Add 5 s per side each week, then progress to leg-raise or reach-through versions after about 45-60 s.
programming.increase: Increase once you reach the top of the time range on both sides with good form.
programming.maintain: Keep the time steady if one side lags, and reduce it if the supporting shoulder becomes sore.

name: Dead bug
musclesText: Primary: rectus abdominis, transversus abdominis. Secondary: internal and external obliques, iliopsoas and rectus femoris.

steps.start: Lie on your back on a mat with your arms pointing straight up over your shoulders and your hips and knees bent to 90 degrees, shins parallel to the floor.
steps.setup: Only a mat is required. Optionally hold a light band or ball between hands and knees later as a progression.
steps.feet: Knees hip-width apart, feet relaxed with ankles in line with the knees in the tabletop position.
steps.grip: Arms straight, fingers pointing at the ceiling, shoulder blades resting on the mat.
steps.posture: Press your lower back gently into the mat by exhaling and drawing the ribs down; keep your head resting on the floor.
steps.brace: Exhale fully to lower the ribs, then hold a gentle brace so the lower back stays in contact with the mat throughout.
steps.initiate: Keeping the brace, start to reach one arm overhead and straighten the opposite leg at the same time.
steps.concentric: Return the arm and leg to the start position by bringing the hand back over the shoulder and the knee back over the hip, keeping the back flat.
steps.breathing: Exhale slowly as you lower the arm and leg, inhale quietly as you return to the start.
steps.eccentric: Lower the opposite arm and leg slowly towards the floor, stopping just before your lower back begins to lift.
steps.rom: Lower the heel and hand as far as you can without the lower back arching; that depth will increase as control improves.
steps.tempo: 3-1-2-0: three seconds out, a one-second pause near the floor, two seconds back.
steps.finish: Return to the tabletop position, then repeat on the other side; one rep per side.
steps.exit: After the last rep, put both feet on the floor and roll to your side before sitting up.

mistakes.m: Lower back arching off the mat as the leg lowers.
mistakes.fix: Shorten the range and lower the leg only as far as you can keep the back down.

mistakes.m: Moving fast and using momentum.
mistakes.fix: Slow to a three-second lowering with a pause near the floor.

mistakes.m: Moving the same-side arm and leg.
mistakes.fix: Pair the right arm with the left leg and vice versa.

mistakes.m: Holding the breath.
mistakes.fix: Exhale long and slow as the limbs extend.

safety: Usually very back-friendly; stop if you feel pain rather than abdominal effort.
If your neck tenses, keep the head resting on the mat and relax the jaw.
checks: Use a mat on a flat floor.
Clear enough space for full arm and leg extension.
reduceLoad: Regress the range when your back lifts, the movement becomes jerky or you feel the effort shifting to the hip flexors or lower back.
progressions: Dead bug holding a band or light weights

programming.rehab: A staple of early back rehabilitation for learning to control the trunk while the limbs move; a physiotherapist can tailor the range.
programming.frequency: 2-5 times per week; also good as a warm-up.
programming.initialLoad: Start with arms only or legs only if the full version makes your back lift.
programming.judgeLoad: Every rep should be slow with the lower back in contact; stop the set when that slips.
programming.progression: Add reps, then add range (lower the leg straighter), then add a light band or weight.
programming.increase: Increase difficulty once you can do 12 slow reps per side without the back lifting.
programming.maintain: Keep the variation the same while you still need to shorten the range to stay flat.

name: Bird dog
musclesText: Primary: erector spinae, multifidus, gluteus maximus. Secondary: rectus abdominis, transversus abdominis, obliques, lower trapezius, posterior deltoid.

steps.start: Kneel on a mat on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
steps.setup: Only a mat is needed; a folded mat under the knees adds comfort.
steps.feet: Knees hip-width apart, toes either tucked or flat on the mat.
steps.grip: Hands flat, fingers spread, pressing the floor away so your shoulder blades sit flat on the ribcage.
steps.posture: Keep a neutral spine from head to pelvis, gaze at the floor just ahead of the hands, neither arching nor rounding.
steps.brace: Lightly brace your abs as if someone could balance a glass of water on your lower back.
steps.initiate: Slide one arm forwards and the opposite leg backwards along the floor before lifting them.
steps.concentric: Extend the arm to shoulder height with the thumb up and the leg to hip height by pushing the heel back, so hand to heel is one long line.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you reach out and hold, inhale as you return.
steps.eccentric: Bring the elbow and knee back underneath you slowly, without letting the hips rock, and lightly touch them back to the start.
steps.rom: Lift the arm and leg only to torso height; higher lifts usually arch the lower back.
steps.tempo: 2-2-2-0: two seconds out, a two-second hold, two seconds back.
steps.finish: Return the hand and knee to the floor and repeat on the other side.
steps.exit: After the set, sit back onto your heels before standing up.

mistakes.m: Lifting the leg too high and arching the back.
mistakes.fix: Stop when the leg is level with the hip and reach back rather than up.

mistakes.m: Hips rotating towards the lifted leg.
mistakes.fix: Keep both hip bones pointing at the floor; imagine a glass on your back.

mistakes.m: Rushing the reps.
mistakes.fix: Pause for two seconds at full reach.

safety: Low-risk; stop if you feel pinching in the lower back or pain in the knees.
Use extra padding under the knees if they are sensitive.
checks: Use a non-slip mat.
Make sure there is space for your arm and leg to fully extend.
reduceLoad: Reduce the range or do legs only if your hips rotate, your back arches or your balance fails.

programming.rehab: Widely used in back rehabilitation to train trunk control with low spinal load; follow a physiotherapist's plan if you are recovering from injury.
programming.frequency: 2-5 times per week; suitable as a warm-up.
programming.initialLoad: Begin with bodyweight and a short hold.
programming.judgeLoad: You should be able to hold each reach steadily with the hips level.
programming.progression: Lengthen the hold, then add reps, then add light ankle weights or a band.
programming.increase: Increase once 12 controlled reps per side with a two-second hold are easy.
programming.maintain: Keep the variation the same while you still wobble or rotate.

name: Reverse crunch
musclesText: Primary: rectus abdominis (especially the lower fibres). Secondary: external and internal obliques, iliopsoas.

steps.start: Lie on your back on a mat with your hips and knees bent to about 90 degrees, thighs vertical and arms by your sides.
steps.setup: A mat is enough. Holding a fixed object behind your head or a bench leg gives extra stability.
steps.feet: Keep your knees and feet together, feet relaxed.
steps.grip: Palms flat on the floor beside your hips, or hands holding a fixed support behind your head.
steps.posture: Head and shoulders rest on the mat; start with the lower back in a neutral position.
steps.brace: Exhale and draw your ribs down towards your pelvis before the first rep.
steps.initiate: Curl your pelvis towards your ribs, peeling your tailbone off the mat rather than swinging the legs.
steps.concentric: Roll your hips up until your lower back lifts slightly off the mat and your knees travel towards your chest, keeping the knee angle constant.
steps.breathing: Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.
steps.eccentric: Uncurl one vertebra at a time and return the hips to the mat slowly, stopping before the feet touch the floor.
steps.rom: Move from hips on the floor to the lower back lifted just off the mat; the movement is short, about 10-15 cm of pelvic travel.
steps.tempo: 1-1-3-0: one second up, a one-second squeeze, three seconds down.
steps.finish: Lower until your tailbone touches the mat with thighs still vertical.
steps.exit: Lower your feet to the floor and roll to the side before getting up.

mistakes.m: Swinging the legs to throw the hips up.
mistakes.fix: Pause at the bottom and start each rep from a dead stop.

mistakes.m: Pushing hard through the hands.
mistakes.fix: Keep the hands light or move them to your chest once stronger.

mistakes.m: Dropping the legs quickly on the way down.
mistakes.fix: Use a three-second lowering.

mistakes.m: Straightening the legs to make it easier to lift.
mistakes.fix: Keep the knees bent at 90 degrees throughout.

safety: Avoid if spinal flexion under load aggravates a known back problem; check with a physiotherapist.
Do not rock onto the neck; the lift ends when the lower back clears the mat.
checks: Use a mat on a flat surface.
If you hold a support, make sure it is fixed and will not move.
reduceLoad: Reduce reps or range when you start swinging, feel your hip flexors take over or the lower back aches.
progressions: Reverse crunch on a decline bench

programming.rehab: Generally not a first-choice rehab exercise; use a gentle range only with a physiotherapist's approval.
programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Start with bodyweight and only as many reps as you can do without swinging.
programming.judgeLoad: Finish each set with one to three clean reps left.
programming.progression: Add reps, then slow the lowering, then move to a decline bench.
programming.increase: Increase difficulty once you reach 15-20 controlled reps. Training your abs strengthens them but does not spot-reduce belly fat; fat loss comes from an overall energy deficit.
programming.maintain: Keep reps the same if your form slips, and reduce if your back aches.

name: Standing cable crunch
musclesText: Primary: rectus abdominis. Secondary: internal and external obliques.

steps.start: Stand facing away from a high pulley, holding the rope or handles at the front of your shoulders, with your back about a step from the stack.
steps.setup: Set the pulley at its highest position with a rope or two single handles attached; choose a light weight to start.
steps.feet: Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees soft, and take a small step forwards so the weight lifts off the stack.
steps.grip: Hold the rope ends or handles at the top of your shoulders or collarbones, elbows pointing forwards and down; keep this arm position fixed.
steps.posture: Stand tall with a neutral spine and the hips over the heels; your hips should stay still throughout.
steps.brace: Brace your abs and keep your glutes lightly squeezed so the hips do not hinge.
steps.initiate: Begin by pulling your ribcage down towards your pelvis rather than bending at the hips.
steps.concentric: Curl your torso forwards and down until your elbows approach your hips, rounding through the upper and middle spine.
steps.breathing: Exhale forcefully as you crunch, inhale as you return.
steps.eccentric: Uncurl slowly back to upright, letting the cable pull you tall without the weight stack slamming.
steps.rom: Crunch through as much spinal flexion as you can control with the hips fixed, typically 30-45 degrees of torso travel.
steps.tempo: 1-1-2-0: one second down, a one-second squeeze, two seconds back.
steps.finish: Return to standing tall with the weight still slightly lifted off the stack.
steps.exit: Step back towards the stack to set the weight down quietly before letting go.

cues: Round the spine, not the hips

mistakes.m: Hinging at the hips instead of flexing the spine.
mistakes.fix: Keep the hips locked over the heels and think of curling the chest down.

mistakes.m: Pulling with the arms.
mistakes.fix: Fix your hands at your shoulders and let the trunk move the cable.

mistakes.m: Using too much weight and leaning back.
mistakes.fix: Choose a load you can control for 10-15 reps.

mistakes.m: Letting the stack slam between reps.
mistakes.fix: Keep tension at the top by stopping short of full lockback.

safety: Avoid if loaded spinal flexion aggravates a known back problem.
Keep the movement smooth; jerking a heavy stack can strain the back or neck.
checks: Check the rope is clipped securely and the pulley pin is fully in.
Make sure the floor around the station is clear.
reduceLoad: Reduce the weight when the hips start to hinge, the arms pull or you lean back to start the rep.

programming.frequency: 2-3 times per week.
programming.initialLoad: Start light, around a load you could do 20 times, and learn the curling pattern.
programming.judgeLoad: Each rep should feel like an abdominal contraction with no hip hinge; stop at one to two reps left.
programming.progression: Double progression: add reps to the top of the range, then add one plate.
programming.increase: Increase the load when all sets reach the top of the rep range with control. Training your abs strengthens them but does not spot-reduce belly fat; fat loss comes from an overall energy deficit.
programming.maintain: Keep the load if you start hinging, and reduce it if you feel it in the lower back.

name: Kneeling rope crunch
musclesText: Primary: rectus abdominis. Secondary: internal and external obliques.

steps.start: Kneel facing the cable stack about an arm's length away, holding the rope beside your head with your hips over your knees.
steps.setup: Set the pulley to its highest position with a rope attachment; place a mat or pad under your knees.
steps.feet: Knees hip-width apart on the pad, shins flat, toes tucked or flat behind you.
steps.grip: Hold the rope ends with a neutral grip and pull them down beside your ears or temples, keeping your hands there throughout.
steps.posture: Sit your hips slightly back but keep them high over the knees, with your spine tall at the start.
steps.brace: Brace your abs and keep your hips fixed so they do not sit back onto your heels.
steps.initiate: Start by pulling your ribcage down towards your pelvis.
steps.concentric: Curl your torso down and forwards, bringing your elbows towards your thighs while keeping the hips still.
steps.breathing: Exhale hard as you crunch, inhale as you return.
steps.eccentric: Uncurl slowly back to the tall start position, letting the abs stretch under control.
steps.rom: Crunch until the elbows near the mid-thigh and return until the spine is long; the hips barely move.
steps.tempo: 1-1-2-0: one second down, one-second squeeze, two seconds up.
steps.finish: Return to the stretched upright position with tension still on the cable.
steps.exit: Sit the hips back and walk the rope forwards so the weight returns to the stack before letting go.

mistakes.m: Sitting the hips back to the heels so the hips do the work.
mistakes.fix: Keep your hips over your knees and move only through the spine.

mistakes.m: Pulling the rope with the arms.
mistakes.fix: Lock the hands beside your head.

mistakes.m: Load too heavy, turning it into a bow.
mistakes.fix: Drop the weight until you can curl fully for 10-15 reps.

mistakes.m: Keeping the spine straight and just hinging.
